chunks.title: start.sh
chunks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts the whole stack inside a Codespace. Safe to re-run.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done
echo "▶ Building and starting FeatureLedger (first time: 3-6 minutes)…"
docker compose up --build -d
echo "▶ Waiting for the dashboard…"
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  if curl -fs http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "✅ FeatureLedger is up: open the PORTS tab → port 3000 (dashboard), 8000/docs (API)"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 5
done
echo "⚠️  Not up yet. Check: docker compose ps && docker compose logs api web"

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Live demo in 30 seconds
chunks.text:
## Live demo in 30 seconds

![Landing: one-click live demo](docs/img/demo-landing.png)

1. **Launch Live Demo.** You are a PM / Tech lead inside *Acme Cloud*, an isolated demo tenant (45 engineers, ~520
   accounts, 6 months of history). The yellow banner switches you to Viewer, CS lead or Admin in one click and
   resets the demo to its starting data.
2. **Feature P&L.** The ledger, the cost-vs-value quadrant, and the **Token-Bleed Radar**: *AI Summaries* is
   used by 37% of accounts, but its LLM tokens eat the revenue (gross margin 11% in the latest month), and
   free and starter accounts burn 16% of the tokens for almost no revenue.
3. **What-if simulator.** The three zombies are pre-selected: ~4.5 FTE and over $600k/yr of avoidable cost.
4. **Zombie-Guard.** Paste the files of a pull request and see the comment the bot would post on GitHub.
5. **Safe Sunset** (switch to *Admin*). *Zapier v1 Webhooks* has passed its scream test: *Approve cleanup PR*
   opens `acme/app#1001`, *Sandbox: merge the PR* archives it. Rolling back puts the flag fully on again.
6. **Integrations** (Admin): *Trigger Sync* runs the five sandbox connectors against vendor-shaped fixture APIs.
7. **Executive brief.** The month's reclaimed zombie tax (with the sunset you just finished), the top 3 bleeding
   features, data health; *Download PDF*, or *Send digest to Slack* (a dry run in the demo).

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Live demo in 30 seconds
chunks.text:
The demo tenant only ever uses sandbox providers (flags, GitHub, PR comments, Slack), even on a deployment
configured with real credentials, and its sessions cannot reach any other tenant (Postgres RLS). Turn it off
with `DEMO_MODE=false` on a production deployment.

FeatureLedger gives every in-house product feature a monthly **profit & loss** statement. It joins
engineering effort (Git), support load, cloud and LLM spend, and tenant-level usage and ARR.
It then turns a "Zombie" verdict into a **guarded, reversible deletion workflow** that drives your feature
flag and opens the dead-code PR itself.

**מדריך הפעלה מלא בעברית, צעד אחר צעד:** [`docs/GETTING_STARTED.he.md`](docs/GETTING_STARTED.he.md)

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build        # migrate → seed → first sync → P&L (≈1 min after the build)
open http://localhost:3000       # dashboard → sign in as Admin / PM-Tech lead / CS lead / Viewer
open http://localhost:8000/docs  # API (OpenAPI; "Authorize" with `make token`)
```

The seed company is *Northwind Cloud*: 45 engineers in 7 teams, ~520 accounts, ~$14M ARR, 22 features and
6 months of history. Everything runs in **sandbox mode** by default: connectors read vendor-shaped fixture
APIs, flags and cleanup PRs go to sandbox providers, and sign-in is one click per role.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Architecture (Phases 1–4)
chunks.text:
## Architecture (Phases 1–4)

```
        Stripe  Jira  PostHog  Zendesk  AWS CE   GitHub (PRs, push, PR merge)   LaunchDarkly / Statsig
           │      │      │        │       │         │                             ▲        │ evaluations
           ▼      ▼      ▼        ▼       ▼         ▼                             │ flag    ▼
   ┌───────────────── Phase 2: connectors (ARQ worker, every 15 min) ──────────┐  │ state  ┌──────────┐
   │ scrub → idempotent inbox → identity stitching → processors → dead letters │  │        │ eval     │
   └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘  │        │ ingest   │
                                   ▼                                              │        │ (15 min) │
   ┌──── Phase 3: Feature Graph ─────────────────────────┐                        │        └────┬─────┘
   │ T1 features.yaml (push-synced) > T2 structural >   │                        │             │
   │ T3 semantic (pgvector, text never stored); human    │                        │             ▼
   │ decisions outrank all; triage below 0.80            │      ┌──── Phase 4: Safe Sunset execution ─────┐
   └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘      │ guarded state machine (pure)            │
                              ▼                                 │ + orchestrator: flag provider,          │
   ┌──── Phase 1: P&L engine (pure) ─────────────────────┐      │   cleanup-PR provider, merge webhook,   │
   │ effort calibration · attribution · classification   │─────▶│   hash-chained audit, fail-closed       │
   └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘      └───────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                              ▼                                                     ▼
            PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector — Row-Level Security on every table (FORCE), app role without BYPASSRLS
                              ▲
   FastAPI ── Principal from session (cookie / bearer) ── RBAC matrix on every route ── tenant from the user record
                              ▲
   Next.js 15 dashboard ── /login (OIDC SSO or sandbox dev login) ── middleware ── role-aware controls
```

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Phase 5: differentiators
chunks.text:
## Phase 5: differentiators

**AI gross margin & Token-Bleed Radar.** Variable LLM spend is now its own cost line, `c_ai_tokens`, separate
from fixed cloud infra (`c_infra`); `c_total` is unchanged. Every feature-month gets
`gross_margin_pct = (v_usage − c_ai_tokens − c_infra) / max(v_usage, 1)` and a per-tier split of token spend
(by usage events) next to the revenue each tier brings. **`margin_bleed`** fires when adoption is above 15% and
gross margin below 20%, and tokens (not infra) drive the cost. Both thresholds are org settings. The flag sits beside
the health class, so a Growth Bet can bleed margin too. It shows on the ledger (badge + radar) and the tear-sheet.

**Zombie-Guard.** On GitHub `pull_request` *opened / synchronize / reopened*, the changed files are resolved
through the Feature Graph (human > manifest > auto-confirmed). If a zombie, a feature in a live sunset plan,
or an archived feature is touched, one non-blocking comment shows its trailing 3-month net P&L, adoption and
sunset stage. On every push the same comment is edited in place, and only if the facts changed (a marker finds it
even after a database reset). FeatureLedger's own `sunset/*` cleanup PRs are skipped.
`GitHubCommentProvider` / `SandboxCommentProvider`; the *Zombie-Guard* page previews the comment for any set of paths.

**Executive digest.** On the 1st of every month (worker cron) and on demand
(`POST /api/v1/reports/executive-digest`):
- the zombie tax reclaimed this month (hours, FTE, $), frozen per sunset at archive time;
- completed sunsets and those still in flight;
- the top 3 bleeding features (net loss or AI overspend against the target margin);
- data-gap health.

It posts Block Kit to `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` (a dry run with a preview in `SANDBOX_MODE` and in the demo).
*Executive brief* in the dashboard is print-ready (*Download PDF*), and `/api/v1/reports/executive-brief.html`
is a self-contained HTML version.

**Live demo (`DEMO_MODE=true`).** The seed company is re-keyed into its own tenant (`acme-demo`) with
deterministic ids, so `POST /api/v1/demo/reset` restores exactly the same plans and users in a few seconds.
- *Launch* and *switch role* issue sessions only for that org.
- Reset refuses any org not flagged `is_demo`.
- The append-only audit log may be purged only for that demo org, and never by the application role.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Phase 4: automated Safe Sunset execution & enterprise auth
chunks.text:
## Phase 4: automated Safe Sunset execution & enterprise auth

**Live feature flags.** A `FeatureFlagProvider` interface with **LaunchDarkly** (semantic patch: turnFlagOn,
fallthrough, replaceTargets), **Statsig** (Console API gate rules; exposures via signed event webhook) and a
**sandbox** provider. The sunset orchestrator drives it:

| Plan step | Flag state | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `customer_outreach → canary_dark_launch` | `zero_usage_off` | Off for every account with 0 events in the last 90 days; on for the rest (targeted by account) |
| promote (same state) | `fully_off` | Off for everyone; the **scream test** clock starts |
| `canary_dark_launch → dead_code_pr_opened` | `fully_off` | Evaluations are re-pulled, then the guards: N quiet days, **0 'on' evaluations**, **0 tickets** → else `409 scream_test_running / flag_still_served / customer_screamed` |
| **rollback** (from canary or PR) | `fully_on` | Back to `customer_outreach`, `rollback_count + 1`, open cleanup PR closed, audit entry |

Evaluation counts are ingested every 15 minutes by the worker (and right before any guard check); a 'on'
evaluation or a ticket during the scream test also writes a one-time `scream_alert` into the audit log.
Every provider call happens inside the transition's transaction and **fails closed**: if LaunchDarkly or
GitHub refuses, the plan does not move.

**Automated dead-code PR.** When an admin approves a quiet canary, FeatureLedger uses the GitHub REST API
(Git Data API, one commit) to create branch `sunset/<feature_key>`, delete every file the manifest attributes
to the feature, remove its `features.yaml` entry (validated), and add `.featureledger/sunset/<key>.json`, a
structured cleanup patch for what a robot must not edit blindly (call sites, flag checks, routes, events).
The PR body carries the blast radius, the scream-test evidence and the hash-chained audit trail. A
`pull_request` *closed + merged* webhook on a `sunset/*` branch archives the plan and the feature and
recomputes the P&L. `SandboxGitHubProvider` builds the identical change without a network.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Phase 4: automated Safe Sunset execution & enterprise auth
chunks.text:
**Enterprise SSO.** OpenID Connect authorization code + PKCE for **Okta, Google Workspace and Auth0** (or any
compliant IdP): state + nonce in a signed short-lived cookie, id_token verified against the IdP's JWKS
(RS256/ES256), `iss`/`aud`/`azp`/`exp`/`nonce`/`email_verified` and an optional domain allowlist. IdP groups map
to roles (`OIDC_ROLE_MAP`); `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAILS` seeds the first admins. With `SANDBOX_MODE=true` the
login page also offers a one-click **dev login** per role (never available outside sandbox mode).
Sessions are HS256 tokens in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie; cookie writes also need an `X-FL-CSRF` header.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Phase 4: automated Safe Sunset execution & enterprise auth › RBAC matrix
chunks.text:
### RBAC matrix

Enforced by FastAPI on every route (`backend/app/auth/rbac.py`); the Next.js UI reads the same permissions
from `/api/v1/auth/me` and disables what your role cannot do. The tenant always comes from the user record;
Postgres RLS isolates tenants underneath.

| Capability | Viewer | PM / Tech lead | CS lead | Admin |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Read P&L, tear-sheets, simulator, sunset board, sync health | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Confirm / reassign / reject mapping triage, run inference, recompute P&L | | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Initiate a sunset plan, compute + acknowledge blast radius, `→ blast_radius_checked` | | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Generate the impact dossier | | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Sign off the dossier, mark accounts contacted, `→ customer_outreach` | | | ✓ | ✓ |
| Approve `→ canary_dark_launch` and the fully-off promotion (flag changes) | | | | ✓ |
| Approve `→ dead_code_pr_opened` (opens the PR), manual archive | | | | ✓ |
| Roll back a canary (flag fully on) | | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Cancel a plan | | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Send the executive digest (Slack) | | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Integrations, imports, features.yaml apply, org settings (rates, thresholds), users & roles | | | | ✓ |

Webhooks (GitHub, Stripe, Jira, Zendesk, PostHog, Statsig) carry no user: the tenant is resolved from the
integration id and the vendor signature is verified before anything is read. `FL_API_TOKEN` is an optional
machine credential that acts as an admin service principal.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Demo walkthrough (sandbox, ≈10 minutes)
chunks.text:
## Demo walkthrough (sandbox, ≈10 minutes)

1. `docker compose up --build`, open http://localhost:3000. You land on **/login**.
2. **Viewer**: browse the ledger and the quadrant. Every write control is disabled with the role it needs;
   *Settings & access* shows the permission matrix with your column highlighted. Sign out (bottom left).
3. **PM / Tech lead**: on **Feature Graph**, confirm a Tier 2 suggestion. Open the *Legacy PDF Exporter*
   tear-sheet → **Start safe sunset**. On the plan: *Compute blast radius* → *Acknowledge call sites* →
   *Confirm blast radius*. *Build account dossier*.
4. **CS lead**: open the plan, *Mark accounts contacted*, tick *CS sign-off*, *Start customer outreach*.
5. **Admin**: *Approve dark launch*. The flag card shows `zero_usage_off` and how many active accounts keep
   it. *Turn flag fully off*: the scream test starts. Advancing now returns **409 scream_test_running**.
6. Any non-viewer: **Roll back** → flag `fully_on`, plan back in outreach, *Rollbacks: 1*, audit entry.
7. **Admin** on *Zapier v1 Webhooks* (fully off since Oct 29, scream test passed): click
   *Sandbox: serve 'on' once* then *Approve cleanup PR* → **409 flag_still_served**. *Reset*, approve again:
   the PR `northwind/app#1001` on `sunset/zapier-v1-webhooks` opens, with its full body (blast radius, scream
   test, audit trail). *Sandbox: merge the PR* delivers the GitHub merge webhook → **Archived**.

The same walkthrough runs headless in CI: `make e2e` (or `python3 scripts/e2e_phase4.py`).

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Earlier phases in one paragraph each
chunks.text:
## Earlier phases in one paragraph each

**Phase 1.** A pure engine computes each feature's monthly cost (calibrated engineering effort, support,
infra, LLM) and value (usage-weighted, tier-gated or critical-dependency attribution), classifies it
(Cash Cow, Growth Bet, Niche Anchor, Zombie, Mandated, Platform, Watch) and keeps the conservation
invariant: feature + overhead + unmapped + unattributed hours = real team capacity.

**Phase 2.** Stripe, Jira, PostHog, Zendesk and AWS Cost Explorer connectors share one protocol (backfill,
incremental, webhook) with allowlist scrubbing, an idempotent inbox, identity stitching, Redis token buckets,
backoff and dead letters after 5 attempts; the P&L recomputes after every sync that brings something new.

**Phase 3.** features.yaml syncs on push (invalid pushes are rejected with exact errors). Tier 2 maps
undeclared code from import edges, co-change and naming; Tier 3 matches tickets, issues and PR titles to
feature centroids in pgvector, with raw text held in memory only. Precedence: human > manifest >
auto-confirmed (≥ 0.80) > triage.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Earlier phases in one paragraph each › What you'll see on the seed data
chunks.text:
### What you'll see on the seed data

| Feature | Class | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy PDF Exporter | **Zombie** | 2.5% adoption and shrinking, ~75% bug tax, ≈ $24k/mo net loss |
| Zapier v1 Webhooks, Bulk CSV Import v1 | **Zombie** | Tiny usage, high maintenance |
| Custom SAML Attribute Mapping | **Niche Anchor** | <7% adoption, but Globex ($180k ARR, renews in Dec) uses it on 14 of 22 days |
| GDPR Data Export | **Mandated** | Regulatory: never a sunset candidate |
| AI Summaries | **Growth Bet** + **margin bleed** | Launched 2026-04, 37% adoption, ~$31k/mo of LLM tokens on ~$40k/mo revenue: 11% gross margin |

The What-if Simulator pre-selects the three zombies: roughly **4.5 FTE** (about 510 engineering hours a month)
and **over $600k/yr** of avoidable cost, against ~$115k of expected ARR loss across 31 accounts.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Development
chunks.text:
## Development

```bash
make test                         # backend unit tests, no database required
make token                        # an admin token (sandbox dev login, or FL_API_TOKEN)
cd backend && python -m app.migrate   # migrate/seed against ADMIN_DATABASE_URL
cd web && npm install && npm run dev  # dashboard on :3000 (API_URL defaults to localhost:8000)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs three jobs:
- **backend:** unit tests; migrations on pgvector Postgres; the RLS check; the Phase 4 and 5 HTTP suites (four roles,
  a second tenant, the demo tenant).
- **web:** typecheck and build.
- **e2e:**
  - `docker compose up` and the sandbox syncs;
  - the Phase 3 checks and the signed-in page renders;
  - the Phase 4 and Phase 5 walkthroughs, including Trigger Sync in the demo leaving the ledger unchanged;
  - README screenshots.

### Use your own data

1. Describe your teams and features in `features.yaml`.
2. In `.env`, set `SEED_ON_START=false`, `DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG`, `ORG_NAME`, and either SSO or `FL_API_TOKEN`.
3. Run `docker compose down -v && docker compose up --build -d`.
4. Import CSVs from `templates/`: `make import KIND=accounts FILE=accounts.csv PERIOD=2026-10`. Do the same for `usage`, `tickets` and `costs`, then run `make pnl`.

Until accounts and usage are imported, every feature is classified **Watch**: cost alone never makes a Zombie.

chunks.title: FeatureLedger: Feature P&L & Safe Deprecation Radar › Principles
chunks.text:
## Principles

- **No surveillance.** No author, reviewer or assignee is stored anywhere. Teams under 3 people are rolled up.
  Cleanup PR bodies name roles, never people.
- **Conservation.** Feature + overhead + unmapped + unattributed hours equal real team capacity, every month.
- **Two lenses.** Additive value (sums to MRR) for the ledger, and counterfactual revenue-at-risk to guard deletions.
- **Reversible by default.** No code is deleted until a fully-off scream test has been quiet for N days, and
  the flag stays the rollback lever until the PR merges.
- **Least privilege.** Read-only ingest tokens; the cleanup token is separate and scoped to one repo;
  approvals that change production (flags, PRs) are admin-only and audited.

See [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) for every formula and threshold.

chunks.text:
"""Feature Graph triage, manifest validation, jobs and connector triggers."""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, BackgroundTasks, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from ..auth.session import Principal, require
from ..config import config
from ..core.manifest import ManifestError, parse_manifest
from ..db import org_tx
from ..jobs.compute_pnl import recompute
from .deps import current_org, org_for, row

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1", tags=["admin"])
log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.api")


@router.post("/manifest/validate")
async def validate_manifest(request: Request, org: str = Depends(current_org)):
    """Body: the raw features.yaml (any content type)."""
    text = (await request.body()).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    try:
        m = parse_manifest(text)
    except ManifestError as e:
        return {"valid": False, "errors": e.errors}
    return {"valid": True, "features": [
        {"key": f.key, "name": f.name, "paths": len(f.paths), "routes": len(f.api_routes), "events": len(f.events),
         "shared_overhead": f.shared_overhead, "regulatory": f.regulatory} for f in m.features]}


@router.post("/jobs/compute-pnl")
async def compute(org: str = Depends(org_for("pnl:recompute"))):
    async with org_tx(org) as conn:
        return await recompute(conn, org)


class GitHubSyncIn(BaseModel):
    repo: str
    default_team_key: str | None = None


@router.post("/integrations/github/sync", status_code=202)
async def github_sync(body: GitHubSyncIn, tasks: BackgroundTasks, org: str = Depends(org_for("integrations:manage"))):
    async with org_tx(org) as conn:
        from ..db import org_is_demo
        if await org_is_demo(conn):
            raise HTTPException(409, "the live demo cannot ingest real repositories")
    if not config.github_token:
        raise HTTPException(412, "set GITHUB_TOKEN (read-only: contents + pull requests) to enable GitHub sync")
    if body.repo.count("/") != 1:
        raise HTTPException(422, "repo must be owner/name")

    async def run() -> None:
        from ..graph.jobs import run_graph
        from ..graph.manifest_store import active_manifest
        from ..graph.semantic_classifier import TextVault
        from ..ingest.github import GitHubClient, sync_repository
        client = GitHubClient(config.github_token)
        vault = TextVault()
        try:
            async with org_tx(org) as conn:
                manifest = await active_manifest(conn)
                integ = await conn.fetchval("SELECT id FROM integrations WHERE kind = 'github' LIMIT 1")
                if integ is None:
                    integ = await conn.fetchval("""INSERT INTO integrations (org_id, kind, status, display_name)
                        VALUES ($1, 'github', 'active', 'GitHub') RETURNING id""", org)
                stats = await sync_repository(conn, org, str(integ), body.repo, client, manifest, body.default_team_key,
                                              vault)
                log.info("github sync %s: %s", body.repo, stats)
            async with org_tx(org) as conn:
                log.info("graph after github sync: %s", await run_graph(conn, org, vault))
                await recompute(conn, org)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("github sync failed for %s", body.repo)
            async with org_tx(org) as conn:
                await conn.execute("""UPDATE integrations SET status = 'error', last_error = 'sync failed: see logs'
                                      WHERE kind = 'github'""")
        finally:
            vault.clear()
            await client.close()

    tasks.add_task(run)
    return {"status": "accepted", "repo": body.repo}

    support_hourly_rate_usd: float | None = Field(None, gt=0, le=2000)

    mapping_auto_confirm: float | None = Field(None, ge=0.5, le=1)
    min_team_size_for_display: int | None = Field(None, ge=1, le=50)
    margin_bleed_min_adoption: float | None = Field(None, ge=0, le=1)
    margin_bleed_max_gross_margin: float | None = Field(None, ge=-1, le=1)


@router.put("/settings")
async def update_settings(body: SettingsIn, recompute_pnl: bool = True, who: Principal = Depends(require("settings:write"))):
    from decimal import Decimal
    changes = {k: Decimal(str(v)) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in body.model_dump(exclude_none=True).items()}
    if not changes:
        raise HTTPException(422, "nothing to change")
    sets = ", ".join(f"{k} = ${i + 1}" for i, k in enumerate(changes))
    async with org_tx(who.org_id) as conn:
        before = row(await conn.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM org_settings"))
        await conn.execute(f"UPDATE org_settings SET {sets}, updated_at = now()", *changes.values())
        after = row(await conn.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM org_settings"))
        log.info("org_settings changed by %s (%s): %s", who.email, who.role.value,
                 {k: (before[k], after[k]) for k in changes})
        pnl = await recompute(conn, who.org_id) if recompute_pnl else None
    return {"settings": after, "changed": sorted(changes), "pnl": pnl}

async def triage_queue(status: Literal["pending", "auto", "decided"] = "pending", tier: int | None = None,
                       org: str = Depends(current_org)):
    """pending: below 0.80, waiting for a person · auto: machine-confirmed (>= 0.80), undoable · decided: by a person."""
    cond = {"pending": "s.status = 'pending' AND s.decided_at IS NULL",
            "auto": "s.auto_confirmed AND s.decided_at IS NULL",
            "decided": "s.decided_at IS NOT NULL"}[status]
    async with org_tx(org) as conn:
        rows = await conn.fetch(f"""
            SELECT s.id, s.subject_type::text AS subject_type, s.subject_id, s.subject_label, s.confidence,
                   s.source::text AS source, s.rationale, s.status::text AS status, s.tier, s.evidence,
                   s.auto_confirmed, s.created_at, s.updated_at, s.decided_at,
                   f.key AS suggested_feature_key, f.name AS suggested_feature_name,
                   d.key AS decided_feature_key, d.name AS decided_feature_name
              FROM mapping_suggestions s
              LEFT JOIN features f ON f.id = s.suggested_feature_id
              LEFT JOIN features d ON d.id = s.decided_feature_id
             WHERE {cond} AND ($1::smallint IS NULL OR s.tier = $1)
             ORDER BY s.confidence DESC, s.created_at LIMIT 500""", tier)
        counts = await conn.fetchrow("""
            SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending' AND decided_at IS NULL) AS pending,
                   count(*) FILTER (WHERE auto_confirmed AND decided_at IS NULL) AS auto,
                   count(*) FILTER (WHERE decided_at IS NOT NULL) AS decided,
                   count(*) FILTER (WHERE tier = 2 AND decided_at IS NULL) AS tier2,

              FROM mapping_suggestions""")
        features = await conn.fetch("""SELECT key, name FROM features WHERE status <> 'archived'
                                        AND NOT is_shared_overhead ORDER BY name""")
    return {"items": [row(r) for r in rows], "features": [row(f) for f in features], "counts": row(counts),

"""Integrations & Sync Health, manual triggers, dead letters, and inbound webhooks."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request

from ..config import config

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1", tags=["integrations"])
_arq = None


async def _queue():
    """ARQ pool, created lazily so the API still serves reads when Redis is down."""
    global _arq
    if _arq is None:
        try:
            from arq import create_pool
            from arq.connections import RedisSettings
            _arq = await create_pool(RedisSettings.from_dsn(config.redis_url))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise HTTPException(503, f"the sync queue (Redis) is not reachable: {e}") from e
    return _arq


def _health(i: dict[str, Any], last_run: dict[str, Any] | None) -> str:
    if i["status"] == "disabled":
        return "disabled"
    if last_run and last_run["status"] == "running":
        return "syncing"
    if i["status"] == "pending" and not i["sandbox"] and not live_configured(i["kind"]):
        return "not_configured"
    if last_run is None:
        return "waiting"
    if last_run["status"] == "failed":
        return "failing"
    if last_run["status"] == "partial":
        return "degraded"
    last = i["last_synced_at"]
    if last and (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - last).total_seconds() > i["sync_interval_minutes"] * 60 * 3:
        return "stale"
    return "healthy"

    for i in rows:
        iid = str(i["id"])
        recent = by_r.get(iid, [])
        d = row(i)
        d["health"] = "manual" if i["kind"] == "github" else _health(i, recent[0] if recent else None)
        d["live_configured"] = live_configured(i["kind"])
        d["cursors"] = by_c.get(iid, [])
        d["inbox"] = by_i.get(iid, {"pending": 0, "processed": 0, "dead_letters": 0})
        d["recent_runs"] = [row({k: v for k, v in r.items() if k not in ("rn", "org_id", "integration_id")})
                            for r in recent]
        if i["kind"] == "github":
            d["manifest"] = row(manifest) if manifest else None
            if manifest and manifest["status"] == "invalid":
                d["health"] = "failing"
        out.append(d)
    return {"integrations": out, "sandbox_mode": config.sandbox_mode}


async def _integration(conn, iid: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    r = await conn.fetchrow("SELECT id, kind::text AS kind, config, sandbox, status::text AS status "
                            "FROM integrations WHERE id = $1", iid)
    if not r:
        raise HTTPException(404, "integration not found")
    return dict(r)

        found = {r["key"]: r for r in feats}
        missing = set(body.feature_keys) - set(found)
        if missing:
            raise HTTPException(404, f"unknown features: {sorted(missing)}")
        blocked = [k for k, r in found.items() if r["is_shared_overhead"] or r["is_regulatory"]]
        if blocked:
            raise HTTPException(422, f"cannot simulate sunsetting platform/regulatory features: {blocked}")
        ids = [r["id"] for r in feats]

                                   WHERE p.feature_id = ANY($1) AND p.period_month = ANY($2::date[])""", ids, months)
        exp = await conn.fetch("""

              FROM account_dependencies d JOIN accounts a ON a.id = d.account_id JOIN features f ON f.id = d.feature_id
             WHERE d.feature_id = ANY($1) AND d.period_month = ANY($2::date[]) AND d.arr_usd > 0

                               for e in exp], ds.settings, body.migration_success, body.one_off_migration_cost)

    """Token-Bleed Radar: every feature with LLM spend, its gross margin trend, and token burn vs revenue by tier."""
    async with org_tx(org) as conn:
        rows = await conn.fetch("""
            SELECT f.key, f.name, f.tier_gate, p.period_month, p.v_usage, p.c_ai_tokens, p.c_infra, p.c_total,
                   p.gross_margin_pct, p.margin_bleed, p.margin_bleed_reason, p.ai_tier_breakdown,

              FROM feature_pnl_monthly p JOIN features f ON f.id = p.feature_id
             WHERE p.feature_id IN (SELECT feature_id FROM feature_pnl_monthly WHERE c_ai_tokens > 0)
               AND p.period_month > (SELECT max(period_month) FROM feature_pnl_monthly) - make_interval(months => $1)
             ORDER BY f.key, p.period_month""", months)
        thresholds = await conn.fetchrow("""SELECT margin_bleed_min_adoption, margin_bleed_max_gross_margin
                                              FROM org_settings""")
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for r in rows:
        d = out.setdefault(r["key"], {"key": r["key"], "name": r["name"], "tier_gate": r["tier_gate"], "history": []})
        d["history"].append({"period": r["period_month"].isoformat()[:7], "v_usage": plain(r["v_usage"]),

                 margin_bleed_reason=r["margin_bleed_reason"], tiers=r["ai_tier_breakdown"] or {})
    feats = sorted(out.values(), key=lambda d: (not d["margin_bleed"], -(d["history"][-1]["c_ai_tokens"] or 0)))
    return {"thresholds": {"min_adoption": plain(thresholds["margin_bleed_min_adoption"]) if thresholds else 0.15,
                           "max_gross_margin": plain(thresholds["margin_bleed_max_gross_margin"]) if thresholds else 0.2},
            "features": feats}

"""Executive Monthly Digest (Slack Block Kit) and the print-ready Executive Brief."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from ..auth.session import Principal, require

from .deps import current_org, parse_period, row

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/reports", tags=["reports"])


def _period(p: str | None) -> date:
    d = parse_period(p)
    if d:
        return d
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return date(now.year, now.month, 1)   # manual default: this month so far


@router.get("/executive-digest")
async def digest_preview(period: str | None = None, org: str = Depends(current_org)):
    """Build the digest without storing or sending it (the Slack payload is included for preview)."""
    async with org_tx(org) as conn:
        d = await build_digest(conn, _period(period))
    return {"summary": d, "slack": slack_blocks(d)}


class DigestIn(BaseModel):
    period: str | None = Field(None, pattern=r"^\d{4}-\d{2}$")
    post_to_slack: bool = True


@router.post("/executive-digest", status_code=201)
async def digest_send(body: DigestIn, who: Principal = Depends(require("reports:send"))):
    """Build, store and (unless SANDBOX_MODE / demo: dry run) post the digest to SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL."""
    async with org_tx(who.org_id) as conn:
        d = await build_digest(conn, _period(body.period))
        blocks = slack_blocks(d)
        status, err = (await post_to_slack(blocks, demo=await org_is_demo(conn))) if body.post_to_slack \
            else ("skipped", "post_to_slack=false")
        r = await conn.fetchrow("""
            INSERT INTO executive_digests (org_id, period_month, trigger, summary, slack_blocks, slack_status,
                                           slack_error, created_by)
            VALUES ($1, $2, 'manual', $3, $4, $5, $6, $7::uuid) RETURNING id, created_at""",
            who.org_id, _period(body.period), d, blocks, status, err, who.user_id)
    return {"id": str(r["id"]), "slack_status": status, "slack_error": err, "summary": d, "slack": blocks}

or any compliant IdP).

    async def login_redirect(self) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]]:
        state, nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(24), secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        verifier, challenge = pkce_pair()
        url = authorization_url(await self.discovery(), self.settings, state, nonce, challenge)
        return url, {"state": state, "nonce": nonce, "verifier": verifier}

    async def complete(self, code: str, verifier: str, nonce: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        disc = await self.discovery()
        s = self.settings
        form = {"grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": code, "redirect_uri": s.redirect_uri,
                "client_id": s.client_id, "code_verifier": verifier}
        tok = await self.http_post_form(disc["token_endpoint"], form,
                                        (s.client_id, s.client_secret) if s.client_secret else None)
        id_token = tok.get("id_token")
        if not id_token:
            raise OIDCError(f"token endpoint returned no id_token ({tok.get('error', 'unknown error')})")
        try:
            claims = verify_jws(id_token, await self.jwks())
        except TokenError:
            claims = verify_jws(id_token, await self.jwks(refresh=True))   # key rotation
        validate_claims(claims, s, disc["issuer"], nonce)
        return claims


def httpx_client(settings: OIDCSettings) -> OIDCClient:
    async def get(url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        import httpx
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10) as c:
            r = await c.get(url)
            r.raise_for_status()
            return r.json()

    async def post_form(url: str, data: dict[str, str], auth: tuple[str, str] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        import httpx
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10) as c:
            r = await c.post(url, data=data, auth=auth, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})
            return r.json()

    return OIDCClient(settings, get, post_form)

"""Role-based access control: four roles, one permission matrix, enforced by FastAPI dependencies.

The matrix is the single source of truth. The API checks it on every route, `/auth/me` returns the
caller's permissions, and the Next.js UI only renders the controls those permissions allow (the UI
is a convenience; the API is the boundary).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from enum import Enum

from ..core.sunset import SunsetState


class Role(str, Enum):
    VIEWER = "viewer"
    PM_TECH_LEAD = "pm_tech_lead"
    CS_LEAD = "cs_lead"
    ADMIN = "admin"


# Phase 1 seed roles still present in older databases.
LEGACY_ROLES = {"pm": Role.PM_TECH_LEAD, "eng_lead": Role.PM_TECH_LEAD, "cs": Role.CS_LEAD, "finance": Role.VIEWER}


def normalize_role(value: str | None) -> Role:
    if value in LEGACY_ROLES:
        return LEGACY_ROLES[value]
    try:
        return Role(value)
    except ValueError:
        return Role.VIEWER


V, P, C, A = Role.VIEWER, Role.PM_TECH_LEAD, Role.CS_LEAD, Role.ADMIN

"""Who is calling: session token (cookie or bearer) -> Principal; FastAPI dependencies that enforce RBAC.

    fl_session cookie   browser sessions (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax). Unsafe methods must also send
                        `X-FL-CSRF: 1`, a header a cross-site form cannot set.
    Authorization: Bearer <session jwt>   scripts, CI, the Next.js server forwarding the cookie
    Authorization: Bearer <FL_API_TOKEN>  machine credential = admin service principal (no user)

The tenant always comes from the user's record in the database, never from a header the caller sends.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import logging
import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable

from fastapi import Depends, Header, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer

COOKIE = "fl_session"
CSRF_HEADER = "x-fl-csrf"
SAFE_METHODS = {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}
_SANDBOX_SECRET = "featureledger-sandbox-only-session-secret"
_ephemeral: str | None = None


def session_secret() -> str:
    global _ephemeral
    if config.session_secret:
        return config.session_secret
    if config.sandbox_mode:
        return _SANDBOX_SECRET
    if _ephemeral is None:
        log.warning("SESSION_SECRET is not set: using a random per-process key (sessions end on restart)")
        _ephemeral = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
    return _ephemeral

    name: str | None = None

        return can(self.role, permission)

"""Real-data mode: create your organization and sync features.yaml into the Feature Graph.

features.yaml is the source of truth for teams, features and Tier 1 mappings. Applying it is
idempotent: teams/features are upserted by key, manifest mappings are replaced, and features
removed from the file are left in place (archive them through Safe Sunset, never by deletion).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date

from .core.manifest import Manifest


async def ensure_org(conn, slug: str, name: str) -> str:
    org = await conn.fetchval("SELECT id FROM organizations WHERE slug = $1", slug)
    if org is None:
        org = await conn.fetchval("INSERT INTO organizations (name, slug) VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING id", name, slug)
    await conn.execute("SELECT set_config('app.org_id', $1, true)", str(org))
    await conn.execute("INSERT INTO org_settings (org_id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT (org_id) DO NOTHING", org)
    return str(org)


async def apply_manifest(conn, org_id: str, manifest: Manifest) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Run inside a transaction where app.org_id = org_id."""
    for t in manifest.teams:
        await conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO teams (org_id, key, name, headcount) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
            ON CONFLICT (org_id, key) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, headcount = EXCLUDED.headcount""",
            org_id, t.key, t.name, t.headcount)
    teams = {r["key"]: r["id"] for r in await conn.fetch("SELECT id, key FROM teams")}
    missing_teams = sorted({f.owner_team for f in manifest.features if f.owner_team and f.owner_team not in teams})
    for key in missing_teams:  # declared only as owner_team: create with headcount 0 and let the user fix it
        teams[key] = await conn.fetchval(
            "INSERT INTO teams (org_id, key, name, headcount) VALUES ($1, $2, $2, 0) RETURNING id", org_id, key)

    fids: dict[str, object] = {}
    for f in manifest.features:
        meta = {"replaced_by": f.replaced_by} if f.replaced_by else {}
        fids[f.key] = await conn.fetchval("""
            INSERT INTO features (org_id, key, name, description, owner_team_id, flag_key, tier_gate,
                                  is_shared_overhead, allocation_rule, allocation_weights, is_regulatory,
                                  launched_at, metadata)
            VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9::allocation_rule, $10, $11, $12, $13)
            ON CONFLICT (org_id, key) DO UPDATE SET
                name = EXCLUDED.name, description = EXCLUDED.description, owner_team_id = EXCLUDED.owner_team_id,
                flag_key = EXCLUDED.flag_key, tier_gate = EXCLUDED.tier_gate,
                is_shared_overhead = EXCLUDED.is_shared_overhead, allocation_rule = EXCLUDED.allocation_rule,
                allocation_weights = EXCLUDED.allocation_weights, is_regulatory = EXCLUDED.is_regulatory,
                launched_at = EXCLUDED.launched_at, metadata = features.metadata || EXCLUDED.metadata,
                updated_at = now()
            RETURNING id""",
            org_id, f.key, f.name, f.description, teams.get(f.owner_team) if f.owner_team else None, f.flag_key,
            f.tier_gate, f.shared_overhead, f.allocation_rule, f.allocation_weights, f.regulatory,
            date.fromisoformat(f.launched_at) if f.launched_at else None, meta)

def remove_feature_block(text: str, key: str) -> str:
    """Remove one `- key: <key>` item (block or flow style) from features.yaml, keeping every other
    byte (comments, ordering, formatting) intact. Raises CleanupError if the result is not valid."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    item = re.compile(r"^(\s*)-\s+(?:key:\s*['\"]?" + re.escape(key) + r"['\"]?\s*(?:#.*)?$|\{.*\bkey:\s*['\"]?"
                      + re.escape(key) + r"['\"]?\s*[,}])")
    start = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if item.match(ln.rstrip("\n"))), None)
    if start is None:
        raise CleanupError(f"{key} not found in the manifest")
    indent = len(item.match(lines[start].rstrip("\n")).group(1))

            end += 1
        # trailing blank lines belong to the separation before the next item: keep exactly one

def _ok(r, what: str, allow: tuple[int, ...] = ()) -> Any:
    if r.status >= 400 and r.status not in allow:
        msg = r.body.get("message") if isinstance(r.body, dict) else str(r.body)[:200]
        raise CleanupProviderError(f"GitHub {what} failed: HTTP {r.status} {msg}")
    return r.body


class GitHubCleanupProvider:
    name = "github"

    def __init__(self, transport: Transport, repo: str, base: str | None = None):
        self.t, self.repo, self.base = transport, repo, base
        self._base_sha: str | None = None
        self._tree_sha: str | None = None
        self._files: list[str] | None = None

    async def _resolve_base(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        if not self.base:
            self.base = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}"), "read repo")["default_branch"]
        if not self._base_sha:
            ref = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/ref/heads/{self.base}"), "read base ref")
            self._base_sha = ref["object"]["sha"]
            commit = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/commits/{self._base_sha}"), "read commit")
            self._tree_sha = commit["tree"]["sha"]
        return self.base, self._base_sha, self._tree_sha  # type: ignore[return-value]

    async def list_files(self) -> list[str] | None:
        _, _, tree = await self._resolve_base()
        body = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/trees/{tree}", params={"recursive": "1"}),
                   "list tree")
        if body.get("truncated"):
            return None
        self._files = [e["path"] for e in body.get("tree", []) if e.get("type") == "blob"]
        return self._files

    async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        base, _, _ = await self._resolve_base()
        r = await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/contents/{path}", params={"ref": base})
        if r.status == 404:
            return None
        body = _ok(r, f"read {path}")
        return base64.b64decode(body.get("content", "")).decode()

async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        base, _, _ = await self._resolve_base()
        r = await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/contents/{path}", params={"ref": base})
        if r.status == 404:
            return None
        body = _ok(r, f"read {path}")
        return base64.b64decode(body.get("content", "")).decode()

    async def open_pr(self, change: CleanupChange, *, next_number: int = 0) -> CleanupPR:
        base, base_sha, tree_sha = await self._resolve_base()
        deletions = [p for p in change.deletions if self._files is None or p in set(self._files)]
        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"path": p, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "sha": None} for p in deletions]
        if change.manifest_after is not None:
            entries.append({"path": change.manifest_path, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob",
                            "content": change.manifest_after})
        entries.append({"path": change.patch_path, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob",
                        "content": json.dumps(change.patch, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"})
        tree = _ok(await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/trees",
                                        json_body={"base_tree": tree_sha, "tree": entries}), "create tree")
        commit = _ok(await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/commits", json_body={
            "message": f"{change.title}\n\nAutomated by FeatureLedger Safe Sunset (plan {change.patch['plan_id']}).",
            "tree": tree["sha"], "parents": [base_sha]}), "create commit")
        r = await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/refs",
                                 json_body={"ref": f"refs/heads/{change.branch}", "sha": commit["sha"]})
        if r.status == 422:   # branch left over from an earlier attempt: move it to the new commit
            _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/git/refs/heads/{change.branch}",
                                     json_body={"sha": commit["sha"], "force": True}), "update branch")
        else:
            _ok(r, "create branch")
        r = await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls", json_body={
            "title": change.title, "head": change.branch, "base": base, "body": change.body,
            "maintainer_can_modify": True})
        if r.status == 422:
            owner = self.repo.split("/")[0]
            existing = _ok(await self.t.request("GET", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls",
                                                params={"head": f"{owner}:{change.branch}", "state": "open"}),
                           "find existing PR")
            if not existing:
                _ok(r, "open PR")
            pr = existing[0]
            _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls/{pr['number']}",
                                     json_body={"title": change.title, "body": change.body}), "refresh PR")
        else:
            pr = _ok(r, "open PR")
        await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/issues/{pr['number']}/labels",
                             json_body={"labels": ["featureledger-sunset"]})   # best effort
        return CleanupPR("github", self.repo, int(pr["number"]), pr.get("html_url"), change.branch, base,
                         commit["sha"], deletions, change.files_edited + [change.patch_path])

    async def close_pr(self, number: int, comment: str) -> None:
        await self.t.request("POST", f"/repos/{self.repo}/issues/{number}/comments", json_body={"body": comment})
        _ok(await self.t.request("PATCH", f"/repos/{self.repo}/pulls/{number}", json_body={"state": "closed"}),
            "close PR")

class SandboxGitHubProvider:
    """Records the PR it would open (same CleanupChange as live) without a network call. A PR merge is
    simulated by POSTing a GitHub-shaped `pull_request` webhook to the real webhook endpoint."""
    name = "sandbox"

    def __init__(self, repo: str = "northwind/app", base: str = "main"):
        self.repo, self.base = repo, base
        self.opened: list[CleanupChange] = []
        self.closed: list[int] = []

    async def list_files(self) -> list[str] | None:
        return None   # use the files FeatureLedger has seen in merged PRs and import edges

    async def manifest_text(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        return None   # use the active manifest version

    async def open_pr(self, change: CleanupChange, *, next_number: int = 1001) -> CleanupPR:
        self.opened.append(change)
        sha = hashlib.sha1((change.body + change.branch).encode()).hexdigest()
        return CleanupPR("sandbox", self.repo, next_number, None, change.branch, self.base, sha,
                         list(change.deletions), change.files_edited + [change.patch_path])

    async def close_pr(self, number: int, comment: str) -> None:
        self.closed.append(number)


_override: CleanupPRProvider | None = None


def set_cleanup_provider(p: CleanupPRProvider | None) -> None:
    global _override
    _override = p


def get_cleanup_provider() -> CleanupPRProvider:
    if _override is not None:
        return _override
    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_CLEANUP_TOKEN")
    if token and config.cleanup_repo:
        from ..connectors.http import HttpxTransport
        t = HttpxTransport("https://api.github.com", headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
            "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28", "User-Agent": "featureledger-sunset"})
        return GitHubCleanupProvider(t, config.cleanup_repo, config.cleanup_base_branch)
    if config.sandbox_mode:
        return SandboxGitHubProvider(config.cleanup_repo or "northwind/app", config.cleanup_base_branch or "main")
    raise CleanupProviderError("set SUNSET_CLEANUP_REPO and GITHUB_CLEANUP_TOKEN (Contents + Pull requests: "
                               "read & write on that repo) to open cleanup PRs")

"""AWS Cost Explorer: monthly UnblendedCost grouped by the `feature` cost-allocation tag and SERVICE.

Cost Explorer is not plain REST (SigV4, JSON-RPC), so this connector talks to a `CostExplorerApi`:
the live one wraps boto3 (run in a thread, behind the same token bucket), the sandbox one serves fixtures.
Months are restated by AWS for a few days after month end, so incremental syncs always re-read the
previous and current month; the processor rebuilds a month from the latest envelopes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import date
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Protocol

from .base import Batch, Connector, SyncCtx, add_months, month_start

LLM_SERVICES = {"Amazon Bedrock", "Amazon SageMaker", "Claude (Amazon Bedrock Edition)"}


class CostExplorerApi(Protocol):
    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


class Boto3CostExplorer:
    def __init__(self, region: str, limiter=None):
        import boto3  # only needed in live mode
        self._ce = boto3.client("ce", region_name=region)
        self._limiter = limiter

    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if self._limiter:
            await self._limiter()
        return await asyncio.to_thread(self._ce.get_cost_and_usage, **kwargs)


def split_tag(key: str, tag: str) -> str | None:
    """CE returns 'feature$legacy-pdf-export' (or 'feature$' when untagged)."""
    prefix = f"{tag}$"
    v = key[len(prefix):] if key.startswith(prefix) else key
    return v or None


def cost_type_for(service: str) -> str:
    return "llm" if service in LLM_SERVICES else "infra"


class AwsCostExplorerConnector(Connector):
    kind = "aws_cost_explorer"
    streams = ("costs",)

    def __init__(self, api: CostExplorerApi, tag_key: str = "feature"):
        super().__init__(transport=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        self.api = api
        self.tag = tag_key

kind = "aws_cost_explorer"
    streams = ("costs",)

    def __init__(self, api: CostExplorerApi, tag_key: str = "feature"):
        super().__init__(transport=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        self.api = api
        self.tag = tag_key

    async def _month(self, ctx: SyncCtx, m: date) -> Batch:
        envs, token = [], None
        while True:
            kw: dict[str, Any] = {
                "TimePeriod": {"Start": m.isoformat(), "End": add_months(m, 1).isoformat()},
                "Granularity": "MONTHLY", "Metrics": ["UnblendedCost"],
                "GroupBy": [{"Type": "TAG", "Key": self.tag}, {"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "SERVICE"}],
            }
            if token:
                kw["NextPageToken"] = token
            r = await self.api.get_cost_and_usage(**kw)
            for period in r.get("ResultsByTime", []):
                for g in period.get("Groups", []):
                    tag_key, service = g["Keys"][0], g["Keys"][1]
                    amt = round(float(g["Metrics"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"]), 4)
                    p = {"month": m.isoformat(), "feature_tag": split_tag(tag_key, self.tag), "service": service,
                         "cost_type": cost_type_for(service), "amount_usd": amt,
                         "unit": g["Metrics"]["UnblendedCost"].get("Unit", "USD")}
                    envs.append(ctx.envelope("aws_cost", f"{m.isoformat()}|{p['feature_tag'] or ''}|{service}",
                                             str(amt), p))
            token = r.get("NextPageToken")
            if not token:
                return Batch("costs", envs, m.isoformat())

    async def backfill(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        now = month_start(ctx.now())
        m = add_months(now, -ctx.backfill_months)
        while m <= now:
            yield await self._month(ctx, m)
            m = add_months(m, 1)

    async def incremental(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str, cursor: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        now = month_start(ctx.now())
        m = min(add_months(now, -1), date.fromisoformat(cursor[:10]))
        while m <= now:
            yield await self._month(ctx, m)
            m = add_months(m, 1)

"""The unified connector contract (spec §3.1).

A connector is a set of *streams* (Jira issues, Stripe invoices, PostHog monthly usage...). Each stream
is read either as a backfill (no cursor yet) or incrementally (from its stored cursor) and yields
`Batch`es. The runner commits a batch's envelopes to `ingest_inbox` and advances the stream's cursor in
the SAME transaction, so a crash can replay a batch but never skip one.

Connectors are pure with respect to storage: they only talk to a `Transport` (live HTTP or sandbox
fixtures) and emit scrubbed, idempotent `Envelope`s. Normalization into canonical tables happens later,
in `processors.py`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Callable, Protocol


class NotConfigured(RuntimeError):
    """Credentials or settings for a live connector are missing."""


class HttpError(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self, status: int, url: str, body: Any = None):
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status} for {url}")
        self.status = status
        self.url = url
        self.body = body


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HttpResponse:
    status: int
    headers: dict[str, str]
    body: Any


class Transport(Protocol):
    async def request(self, method: str, url: str, *, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
                      json_body: Any = None, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> HttpResponse: ...


def content_hash(obj: Any) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def idempotency_key(integration_id: str, entity_type: str, external_id: str, version: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(f"{integration_id}|{entity_type}|{external_id}|{version}".encode()).hexdigest()

def add_months(m: date, n: int) -> date:
    y, mo = divmod(m.month - 1 + n, 12)
    return date(m.year + y, mo + 1, 1)


class Connector:
    """Base class. Subclasses set `kind` and `streams`, and implement `backfill` and `incremental`."""

    kind: str = ""
    streams: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __init__(self, transport: Transport):
        self.t = transport

    async def backfill(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        raise NotImplementedError
        yield  # pragma: no cover

    async def incremental(self, ctx: SyncCtx, stream: str, cursor: str) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        raise NotImplementedError
        yield  # pragma: no cover

    def handle_webhook(self, ctx: SyncCtx, headers: dict[str, str], body: bytes) -> list[Envelope]:
        """Turn a verified webhook into envelopes. Default: none (the webhook only triggers a sync)."""
        return []

    async def sync(self, ctx: SyncCtx, cursors: dict[str, str]) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        for stream in self.streams:
            cur = cursors.get(stream)
            it = self.incremental(ctx, stream, cur) if cur else self.backfill(ctx, stream)
            async for batch in it:
                yield batch

"""Live HTTP transport (httpx). Imported lazily so the pure connector code needs no network stack."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from .base import HttpResponse


class HttpxTransport:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None, auth: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
                 timeout: float = 30.0):
        import httpx
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=base_url, headers=headers or {}, auth=auth, timeout=timeout,
                                         follow_redirects=False)

    async def request(self, method: str, url: str, *, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None, json_body: Any = None,
                      headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> HttpResponse:
        r = await self._client.request(method, url, params=params, json=json_body, headers=headers)
        try:
            body = r.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = r.text
        return HttpResponse(r.status_code, dict(r.headers), body)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._client.aclose()

"""PostHog (Query API + Groups API), B2B usage at the tenant (group) level.

Streams
  `groups` : GET /api/projects/{id}/groups/?group_type_index=N  (paged by `next`), full refresh each run.
  `usage`  : POST /api/projects/{id}/query with two HogQL queries per calendar month:
               per (group, event): distinct active days, distinct persons, event count
               per group:          distinct active days across all events (the concentration denominator)
             Backfill: the last `backfill_months` complete months + the current one. Incremental: the
             previous month (late events) + the current one. Cursor = last month fully read.
Only aggregates leave PostHog: no person ids, no properties other than the group's name and domain.
"""

from datetime import date
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator

USAGE_HOGQL = """
SELECT {group_col} AS group_key, event,
       count(DISTINCT toDate(timestamp)) AS active_days,
       count(DISTINCT person_id) AS active_users,
       count() AS events
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= {start} AND timestamp < {end} AND {group_col} != ''
GROUP BY group_key, event
ORDER BY group_key, event
LIMIT 500000
"""
ACTIVITY_HOGQL = """
SELECT {group_col} AS group_key, count(DISTINCT toDate(timestamp)) AS active_days
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= {start} AND timestamp < {end} AND {group_col} != ''
GROUP BY group_key
LIMIT 500000
"""

    streams = ("groups", "usage")

        super().__init__(transport)

        self.gti = group_type_index
        self.group_col = f"$group_{group_type_index}"

"""Inbox processors: pending envelopes -> canonical tables, in bulk, with dead-letter isolation.

Run inside an org-scoped transaction. Order matters (accounts before anything that stitches to them):
  stripe_customer/subscription/invoice -> zendesk_org, posthog_group (stitching) -> jira_issue ->
  zendesk_ticket -> posthog_usage/activity (month rebuild) -> aws_cost (month rebuild)

Isolation: a payload that fails to normalize fails alone. A handler whose SQL fails is rolled back to its
savepoint and all of its envelopes are marked failed. Every failure increments `attempts`; at 5 the
envelope is dead-lettered (`dead_lettered_at`) and never blocks its stream again. The Sync Health view
lists dead letters and can re-queue them.

Rebuild-style sources (Stripe accounts, PostHog months, AWS months) recompute their output from the
LATEST version of every envelope of that entity, so replays and restatements converge.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from ..core.manifest import Manifest
from . import normalize as N
from .stitching import UNRESOLVED_REF, AccountIndex

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.processors")

ORDER = ["stripe_customer", "stripe_subscription", "stripe_invoice", "zendesk_org", "posthog_group", "jira_issue",
         "zendesk_ticket", "posthog_usage", "posthog_activity", "aws_cost"]
TICKET_NS = uuid.UUID("0d1c9f3e-2b7a-4c55-9a51-6c1f0e2d8b44")

LATEST_SQL = """SELECT DISTINCT ON (external_id) external_id, payload FROM ingest_inbox
                 WHERE entity_type = $1 AND {cond} ORDER BY external_id, received_at DESC"""


@dataclass
class Stats:
    processed: int = 0
    failed: int = 0
    dead_lettered: int = 0
    accounts_upserted: int = 0
    months_rebuilt: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    unresolved_groups: int = 0
    unknown_events: int = 0
    unmatched_orgs: int = 0

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return dict(self.__dict__)


async def _latest(conn, entity: str, cond: str, *args) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [r["payload"] for r in await conn.fetch(LATEST_SQL.format(cond=cond), entity, *args)]

async def process_inbox(conn, org_id: str, manifest: Manifest, fx: dict[str, float], limit: int = 50_000) -> Stats:
    st = Stats()
    pending = await conn.fetch("""
        SELECT idempotency_key, entity_type, external_id, payload, attempts FROM ingest_inbox
         WHERE processed_at IS NULL AND dead_lettered_at IS NULL ORDER BY received_at LIMIT $1""", limit)
    by_type: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    for r in pending:
        by_type[r["entity_type"]].append(dict(r))
    if not pending:
        return st
    index = await load_index(conn)
    failed: dict[str, str] = {}
    done: list[str] = []
    accounts_changed = False

    async def guarded(name: str, envs: list[dict], fn) -> None:
        nonlocal failed
        if not envs:
            return
        try:
            async with conn.transaction():   # savepoint: a SQL failure rolls back this handler only
                await fn()
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
            log.exception("processor %s failed", name)
            for e in envs:
                failed.setdefault(e["idempotency_key"], f"{name}: {ex}"[:500])
        done.extend(e["idempotency_key"] for e in envs if e["idempotency_key"] not in failed)

    stripe_envs = by_type["stripe_customer"] + by_type["stripe_subscription"] + by_type["stripe_invoice"]

    async def do_stripe() -> None:
        nonlocal accounts_changed, index
        accounts_changed = await _stripe(conn, org_id, stripe_envs, fx, st, failed)
        index = await load_index(conn)
    await guarded("stripe", stripe_envs, do_stripe)

    # stitching: pending orgs/groups, or ALL of them when new accounts appeared (late re-stitch)
    for kind, entity in (("zendesk", "zendesk_org"), ("posthog", "posthog_group")):
        envs = by_type[entity]
        if accounts_changed:
            payloads = await _latest(conn, entity, "true")
        else:
            payloads = [e["payload"] for e in envs]

"""Try to take `cost` tokens. Returns 0 on success, else seconds to wait before retrying."""


@dataclass
class MemoryBucketStore:
    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    state: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    async def take(self, key: str, rate: float, capacity: int, cost: float = 1.0) -> float:
        now = self.clock()
        tokens, ts = self.state.get(key, (float(capacity), now))
        tokens = min(float(capacity), tokens + (now - ts) * rate)
        if tokens >= cost:
            self.state[key] = (tokens - cost, now)
            return 0.0
        self.state[key] = (tokens, now)
        return (cost - tokens) / rate


TAKE_LUA = """
local cap = tonumber(ARGV[1]); local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2]); local now = tonumber(ARGV[3]); local cost = tonumber(ARGV[4])
local b = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', 'ts')
local tokens = tonumber(b[1]) or cap
local ts = tonumber(b[2]) or now
tokens = math.min(cap, tokens + math.max(now - ts, 0) * rate)
local wait = 0
if tokens >= cost then tokens = tokens - cost else wait = (cost - tokens) / rate end
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tokens, 'ts', now)
redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], 3600)
return tostring(wait)
"""


class RedisBucketStore:
    """Shared across worker processes, so N workers never exceed one vendor limit together."""

    def __init__(self, redis: Any):
        self.redis = redis

    async def take(self, key: str, rate: float, capacity: int, cost: float = 1.0) -> float:
        wait = await self.redis.eval(TAKE_LUA, 1, f"fl:bucket:{key}", capacity, rate, time.time(), cost)
        return float(wait.decode() if isinstance(wait, bytes) else wait)


class RetryingTransport:
    def __init__(self, inner: Transport, store: BucketStore, bucket_key: str, rate: float, capacity: int,
                 max_attempts: int = 6, sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep,
                 rng: random.Random | None = None):
        self.inner, self.store, self.key = inner, store, bucket_key
        self.rate, self.capacity, self.max_attempts = rate, capacity, max_attempts
        self.sleep, self.rng = sleep, rng
        self.stats = {"requests": 0, "throttled_waits": 0, "retries": 0}

"""Sync runner: connector batches -> ingest_inbox (+ cursor, same transaction) -> processors -> P&L.

Used by the ARQ worker (scheduled, manual and webhook-triggered syncs). `tx` is an org-scoped
transaction factory (app.db.org_tx in production), injectable for tests.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable

from ..config import config
from ..graph.jobs import run_graph
from ..graph.manifest_store import active_manifest
from ..graph.semantic_classifier import TextVault

log = logging.getLogger("featureledger.sync")

INSERT_ENVELOPE = """
    INSERT INTO ingest_inbox (idempotency_key, org_id, integration_id, entity_type, external_id, external_version, payload)
    VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7) ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING"""


async def write_envelopes(conn, org_id: str, envelopes: list[Envelope]) -> int:
    if not envelopes:
        return 0
    before = await conn.fetchval("SELECT count(*) FROM ingest_inbox WHERE idempotency_key = ANY($1)",
                                 [e.idempotency_key for e in envelopes])
    await conn.executemany(INSERT_ENVELOPE, [(e.idempotency_key, org_id, e.integration_id, e.entity_type, e.external_id,
                                              e.external_version, e.payload) for e in envelopes])
    return len({e.idempotency_key for e in envelopes}) - int(before)


async def commit_batch(conn, org_id: str, integration_id: str, batch: Batch) -> int:
    """Envelopes and the stream cursor in ONE transaction: a crash replays a batch, never skips one."""
    new = await write_envelopes(conn, org_id, batch.envelopes)
    if batch.cursor:
        await conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO sync_cursors (integration_id, org_id, entity_type, cursor) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
            ON CONFLICT (integration_id, entity_type) DO UPDATE SET cursor = EXCLUDED.cursor, updated_at = now()""",
            integration_id, org_id, batch.stream, batch.cursor)
    return new

async def run_integration(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, integ: dict[str, Any], trigger: str,
                          store: BucketStore, manifest_text: str, vault: TextVault | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    iid = str(integ["id"])
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        run_id = await conn.fetchval("""INSERT INTO sync_runs (org_id, integration_id, trigger) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
                                        RETURNING id""", org_id, iid, trigger)
        cursors = {r["entity_type"]: str(r["cursor"]) for r in await conn.fetch(
            "SELECT entity_type, cursor FROM sync_cursors WHERE integration_id = $1", iid)}
    res = {"run_id": run_id, "kind": integ["kind"], "batches": 0, "seen": 0, "new": 0, "status": "succeeded",
           "error": None}
    try:
        built = build(integ["kind"], org_id, iid, integ.get("config") or {}, bool(integ.get("sandbox")), store,
                      manifest_text)
    except NotConfigured as e:
        res.update(status="failed", error=str(e))
        async with tx(org_id) as conn:
            await _finish(conn, res)
            await conn.execute("UPDATE integrations SET status = 'pending', last_error = $2 WHERE id = $1", iid, str(e))
        return res
    try:
        async for batch in built.connector.sync(built.ctx, cursors):
            async with tx(org_id) as conn:
                res["new"] += await commit_batch(conn, org_id, iid, batch)
            if vault is not None:   # raw text for Tier 3 stays in memory; only payloads were written above
                for e in batch.envelopes:
                    if e.ephemeral_text:
                        vault.put(e.entity_type, e.external_id, e.ephemeral_text)
            res["batches"] += 1
            res["seen"] += len(batch.envelopes)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - recorded on the run; committed batches stay committed
        log.exception("sync %s failed", integ["kind"])
        res.update(status="partial" if res["batches"] else "failed", error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:500])
    finally:
        await built.close()
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        await _finish(conn, res)
        if res["status"] == "succeeded":
            await conn.execute("""UPDATE integrations SET status = 'active', last_error = NULL, last_synced_at = now()
                                  WHERE id = $1""", iid)
        else:
            await conn.execute("UPDATE integrations SET status = 'error', last_error = $2 WHERE id = $1", iid,
                               res["error"])
    return res


async def _finish(conn, res: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    await conn.execute("""UPDATE sync_runs SET status = $2::sync_status, finished_at = now(), batches = $3,
                          envelopes_seen = $4, envelopes_new = $5, error = $6 WHERE id = $1""",
                       res["run_id"], res["status"], res["batches"], res["seen"], res["new"], res["error"])

async def process_org(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, run_ids: list[int] | None = None) -> Stats:
    async with tx(org_id) as conn:
        manifest = await active_manifest(conn)
        st = await process_inbox(conn, org_id, manifest, fx_rates())
        if run_ids:
            await conn.execute("UPDATE sync_runs SET processed = $2, dead_lettered = $3 WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[])",
                               run_ids, st.processed, st.dead_lettered)
    return st


async def sync_org(tx: Callable[..., Any], org_id: str, integrations: list[dict[str, Any]], trigger: str,
                   store: BucketStore, recompute: Callable[[str], Awaitable[Any]] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Sync the given integrations in dependency order, then process the inbox, then recompute the P&L."""
    manifest_text = config.manifest_path.read_text()   # sandbox fixtures are built from the shipped manifest
    order = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(SYNC_ORDER)}
    results = []
    vault = TextVault()
    try:
        for integ in sorted(integrations, key=lambda i: order.get(i["kind"], 99)):
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            results.append(await run_integration(tx, org_id, integ, trigger, store, manifest_text, vault))
            log.info("sync %s: %s %s in %.1fs", org_id, integ["kind"], results[-1]["status"], time.monotonic() - t0)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        st = await process_org(tx, org_id, [r["run_id"] for r in results])
        log.info("sync %s: processed %d envelopes in %.1fs", org_id, st.processed, time.monotonic() - t0)
        async with tx(org_id) as conn:
            graph = await run_graph(conn, org_id, vault)
    finally:
        vault.clear()
    pnl = None
    changed = graph["reallocated"] or graph["tier2"]["auto_confirmed"] or graph["tier3"]["auto_confirmed"]
    if recompute and (st.processed or any(r["new"] for r in results) or changed):
        pnl = await recompute(org_id)
    return {"runs": results, "processing": st.as_dict(), "graph": graph, "pnl": pnl}

"""SANDBOX_MODE: realistic, vendor-shaped API responses served from memory.

The sandbox APIs are built from the deterministic seed company (Northwind Cloud), so a fresh
`docker compose up` exercises the *real* connector code (pagination, cursors, scrubbing, retries,
stitching, processors) end to end, and the resulting ledger matches the Phase 1 demo exactly.

The responses deliberately include the fields a real API returns and the scrubbers must drop
(assignees, reporters, requester ids, emails, contact names, ticket descriptions) so the privacy
guarantees are tested on every sandbox sync, not only in unit tests.

class SandboxCostExplorer:
    def __init__(self, manifest_text: str, page_size: int = 20):
        w = _world(manifest_text)
        self.page_size = page_size
        self.by_month: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        for c in w["seed"].dataset.cost_lines:
            key = "feature$" + (w["feats"][c.feature_id].key if c.feature_id else "")
            if c.cost_type == "llm":
                parts = [("Amazon Bedrock", c.amount_usd)]
            else:
                ec2 = round(c.amount_usd * 0.7, 2)
                parts = [("Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute", ec2),
                         ("Amazon Relational Database Service", round(c.amount_usd - ec2, 2))]
            for svc, amt in parts:
                self.by_month.setdefault(c.period_month.isoformat(), []).append(
                    {"Keys": [key, svc], "Metrics": {"UnblendedCost": {"Amount": f"{amt:.2f}", "Unit": "USD"}}})

    async def get_cost_and_usage(self, **kw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        start = kw["TimePeriod"]["Start"]
        groups = self.by_month.get(start, [])
        offset = int(kw.get("NextPageToken") or 0)
        chunk = groups[offset:offset + self.page_size]
        out: dict[str, Any] = {"ResultsByTime": [{"TimePeriod": kw["TimePeriod"], "Groups": chunk, "Estimated": False}]}
        if offset + self.page_size < len(groups):
            out["NextPageToken"] = str(offset + self.page_size)
        return out

"""Zendesk Support (Tickets + Metrics).

Streams
  `organizations`: GET /api/v2/organizations?page[size]=100 (cursor pages), full refresh: domain names
                   drive identity stitching.
  `tickets`: incremental cursor export GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor.json?start_time=...&include=metric_sets,
             then `?cursor=<after_cursor>` until `end_of_stream`. The `after_cursor` is the stream cursor.

Handle time: Zendesk has no native handle time. If `time_field_id` (the Time Tracking app's "total time
spent (sec)" field) is configured it is used; otherwise handle time is estimated as replies × 12 minutes
and the ticket is flagged `handle_time_estimated`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator

from .base import Batch, Connector, SyncCtx, add_months, month_start
from .scrub import scrub_zendesk_org, scrub_zendesk_ticket

MINUTES_PER_REPLY = 12


def handle_minutes(ticket: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, bool]:
    if ticket.get("time_spent_seconds") is not None:
        return max(0, round(ticket["time_spent_seconds"] / 60)), False
    replies = ticket.get("replies") or 1
    return int(replies) * MINUTES_PER_REPLY, True


class ZendeskConnector(Connector):
    kind = "zendesk"
    streams = ("organizations", "tickets")

    def __init__(self, transport, time_field_id: int | None = None):
        super().__init__(transport)
        self.time_field_id = time_field_id

    async def _orgs(self, ctx: SyncCtx) -> AsyncIterator[Batch]:
        params: dict[str, Any] | None = {"page[size]": 100}
        url: str | None = "/api/v2/organizations"
        while url:
            r = await self.t.request("GET", url, params=params)
            envs = [ctx.envelope("zendesk_org", str(o["id"]), o.get("updated_at") or "", scrub_zendesk_org(o))
                    for o in r.body.get("organizations", [])]
            meta = r.body.get("meta") or {}
            if meta.get("has_more"):
                params = {"page[size]": 100, "page[after]": meta.get("after_cursor")}
            else:
                url = None
            yield Batch("organizations", envs, ctx.now().isoformat() if url is None else None)
