chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text:
# API reference

The base path is `/api`. Responses are JSON. Errors are returned as `{"error": "<code>"}` with an appropriate HTTP status. Authenticated endpoints need `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

## Auth
| Method | Path | Body / notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/auth/register` | `{email, password, display_name, locale}` → `{access_token, expires_in, user}`. Also sets the refresh cookie. |
| POST | `/auth/login` | `{email, password}` |
| POST | `/auth/refresh` | Uses the cookie; rotates it. |
| POST | `/auth/logout` | |

## Account & settings
`GET /me` · `PATCH /me {locale, display_name, ai_provider_consent, remember_locations, shared_learning_opt_in}` · `POST /me/password {current_password, new_password}` · `POST /me/logout-all` · `GET /me/audit` · `GET /me/export` · `DELETE /me {password}` · `GET /meta` (public: doc types, processes, feature availability) · `GET /dashboard`

chunks.title: API reference › Documents
chunks.text:
## Documents
| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/documents` | Query parameters: `q` (natural language), `category`, `doc_type`, `source`, `issuer`, `from`, `to`, `tag`, `duplicates=1`, `include_archived=1` |
| POST | `/documents` | multipart `files[]`, `source=upload\|whatsapp_import` → processing starts asynchronously |
| GET | `/documents/:id` | metadata, text excerpt, duplicate info, bundles it belongs to |
| PATCH | `/documents/:id` | `display_name, doc_type, category_key, issuer, doc_date, expiry_date, tags, archived` |
| DELETE | `/documents/:id` | `{confirm: true}` required |
| POST | `/documents/:id/reprocess` · `/duplicate {action: keep_both\|archive_this\|not_duplicate}` · `/link {disposition: inline\|attachment}` → single-use URL |
| GET | `/documents/:id/thumbnail` | |
| POST | `/import/whatsapp` | multipart `file` (exported chat .zip) |
| GET | `/dl/:token` | signed, single-use, valid 120 s |

chunks.title: API reference › Assistant
chunks.text:
## Assistant
`POST /assistant/message {text, conversation_id?}` → `{conversation_id, message_id, lang, text, blocks[], actions[], quick_replies[]}`

Block types:
- `requirements`: `{results:[{requirement, status, best, alternatives, freshness, uncertain, acquisition, previously_found_in}], sources_searched, sources_unavailable, sources_failed}`
- `suggestions`: labelled suggestions, never requirements
- `proposal`: a memory change awaiting confirmation
- `documents`: content-search hits

`GET /conversations` · `GET /conversations/:id` · `DELETE /conversations/:id`

## Memory
`GET /memory` → `{checklists, facts, proposals}` · `POST /memory/checklists` · `PATCH|DELETE /memory/checklists/:id` · `POST /memory/proposals/:id {accept}` · `DELETE /memory/facts/:id` · `DELETE /memory {confirm:true}`

## Bundles
`GET|POST /bundles` · `GET|PATCH|DELETE /bundles/:id` · `POST /bundles/:id/items` · `PATCH|DELETE /bundles/:id/items/:item {custom_filename, label, selected, document_id}` · `POST /bundles/:id/links {item_ids?}` → one signed link per file (separate originals, no ZIP) · `POST /bundles/:id/combined-link` → optional merged PDF

## Categories & connectors
`GET|POST /categories` · `DELETE /categories/:key` (custom only) · `GET /connectors` (in search order, with an honest `state`) · `POST /connectors/:kind/connect` → `{auth_url}` · `GET /oauth/google/callback` · `DELETE /connectors/:kind` · `POST /connectors/:kind/import {ref}`

chunks.title: Architecture
chunks.text:
# Architecture

## Stack decision

| Considered | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| React Native/Expo | Deferred to Stage 3 | Gallery and Downloads scanning needs native Android storage permissions. The REST API is built so a native client can use it as is. |
| Node/TypeScript backend | **Python + Flask** | The hard parts of this product are OCR, PDF handling, text classification and crypto, and Python has the strongest libraries for them (Tesseract, pdfplumber, pypdf, scikit-learn, `cryptography`). Its type-hinted modules map one-to-one onto the requested services. |
| PostgreSQL | **SQLite now**, Postgres-portable schema | Zero-ops MVP. The schema uses portable types, and `Database` is the only place that knows the dialect. Moving to Postgres means a driver swap plus `ON CONFLICT` and `BLOB→BYTEA` edits. |
| Object storage | Local encrypted blob store (`BlobStore`) | Same interface as S3/GCS (`put`, `get`, `delete`). Files are client-side encrypted before they reach any storage. |
| Background jobs | In-process `ThreadPoolExecutor` | Documents stuck in `processing` are re-queued at startup. Swap for RQ/Celery when running more than one process. |
| Frontend | No-build ES modules SPA | Nothing to compile, a strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`, no inline code), and installable as a PWA. |

chunks.title: Architecture › Module map
chunks.text:
## Module map

```
            ┌──────────── api/ (Flask blueprints, auth decorator, signed download links) ────────────┐
            │                                                                                         │
 assistant/ engine ──► intent (he/en)            services/ documents ──► extract (OCR) ──► classifier
            │   └────► discovery ──► connectors/ base (search order) ──► library │ whatsapp │ gmail │ drive
            │                                   └──► knowledge/catalog (acquisition guidance)
            ├────► services/memory (proposals → checklists)  ──► shared_learning (off)
            └────► services/bundles
 security/  crypto (envelope encryption, scrypt) · auth (JWT + refresh rotation) · audit · rate limit
```

chunks.title: Architecture › Key flows
chunks.text:
## Key flows

**Ingestion.** Upload, then magic-byte sniff, then SHA-256 (exact duplicate check), then encrypt and store. A background worker then runs: text extraction (PDF native text, else rasterise and OCR heb+eng), classification (knowledge scorer plus the personal nearest-neighbour layer), issuer/date/expiry extraction, a smart name, the encrypted thumbnail, near-duplicate check (Jaccard ≥ 0.85 within the same type), and finally search index invalidation.

**Discovery.** For each requirement, `discovery.find_requirement` asks every *searchable* connector in the mandated order (local files, gallery, downloads, WhatsApp, Gmail, Drive). It then de-duplicates (by document id, external ref, and filename+size) and ranks exact-type matches above content matches, and local copies above external ones. A requirement becomes `not_found` only when every searchable source answered. If a source failed, the status is `search_incomplete` and no acquisition advice is shown. Acquisition guidance is attached only after a complete search.

**Memory.** The engine never writes checklists directly. It creates a `memory_proposals` row, and only the user's confirmation (chat "yes", the button, or the Memory screen) applies it. Matching a later request uses the canonical process key first, then trigram overlap with the saved name.

**Statuses.** `found_local`, `found_whatsapp`, `found_gmail`, `found_gdrive`, `found_external_not_downloaded`, `not_found`, `search_incomplete`. Each answer also includes `sources_searched` and `sources_unavailable`.

chunks.title: Architecture › Intelligence without sending documents anywhere
chunks.text:
## Intelligence without sending documents anywhere

- OCR runs locally (Tesseract).
- The classifier is deterministic and explainable (`signals`), and it adapts per user through documents the user has relabelled.
- Search is TF-IDF over decrypted text, built in memory per user and never persisted. The `SearchIndex` seam allows a local embedding model later.
- The optional LLM sees only the request text, and the parsed keys are validated against the catalog.

chunks.title: Source integrations
chunks.text: # Source integrations

chunks.title: Source integrations › Gmail and Google Drive (Stage 2: implemented, needs credentials)
chunks.text:
## Gmail and Google Drive (Stage 2: implemented, needs credentials)
1. In Google Cloud Console, create a project and enable the **Gmail API** and the **Google Drive API**.
2. Configure the OAuth consent screen (External, testing mode). Add your Google account as a test user.
3. Create an OAuth client of type *Web application*, with the redirect URI `http://localhost:8000/api/oauth/google/callback` (or your HTTPS domain).
4. Set the following and restart:
   ```
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=...
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=...
   GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:8000/api/oauth/google/callback
   ```
5. In the app, go to **More → Connected sources → Gmail → Connect**.

Behaviour: the search queries Gmail as `has:attachment {"<Hebrew and English aliases>"}`, and Drive as `fullText contains` / `name contains`. Results show **"Found externally — not downloaded"**, with a direct link to the exact email or file and a *Download to library* action. That action fetches the attachment through the API, then encrypts, OCRs and classifies it like any upload.

`gmail.readonly` and `drive.readonly` are *restricted* scopes. Up to 100 test users work without review. A public launch needs Google OAuth verification, and for Gmail a third-party security assessment (CASA). Plan for this early.

The Google code was tested here against a mocked API (`tests/test_bundles_connectors.py`). It has not yet been run against live Google accounts, so the first real connection should be treated as an integration test.

chunks.title: Source integrations › WhatsApp
chunks.text:
## WhatsApp
WhatsApp offers **no official API for reading a personal account's chats or media**. The WhatsApp Business Platform is for businesses messaging customers. Scraping WhatsApp Web or using unofficial clients violates WhatsApp's terms, so DocMind does neither.

Supported routes:
- **Now:** in the chat, tap ⋮ → More → **Export chat** → **Include media**, then choose **Import WhatsApp chat** in DocMind. PDFs and images are imported and tagged with source `whatsapp`.
- **Stage 3 (Android app):** register DocMind as a share target, so a user can long-press a file in WhatsApp → Share → DocMind.

## Android local files and gallery (Stage 3)
The plan is an Expo/React Native client that uses the Storage Access Framework (`ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE`) for user-chosen folders such as Downloads, and the MediaStore/`READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` photo picker for the gallery. OCR stays on-device (ML Kit text recognition, which covers Latin script; Hebrew needs Tesseract on-device or the server path). The client sends documents to the same `/api/documents` endpoint with `source=device_gallery|device_downloads`.

## Adding a connector
Subclass `connectors.base.Connector` (or `LibraryConnector`), set `key`, `order` and `label`, implement `availability()` and `find()`, and add it to `registry()`. Discovery, statuses, de-duplication and the UI's source list pick it up automatically.

chunks.title: Roadmap
chunks.text:
# Roadmap

## Stage 1: done
Authentication, upload, encrypted library, OCR (he+en), classification, natural-language search, the assistant, consent-based checklists, bundles with individual downloads, an optional combined PDF, duplicate and outdated detection, WhatsApp export import, privacy controls, audit log, and 44 automated tests.

## Stage 2: code complete, needs live verification
- Gmail and Drive connectors (OAuth + PKCE, search, deep links, import). **Next step:** register an OAuth client, connect a real account, and verify Hebrew query quality on real mail.
- ✅ Background index of Gmail/Drive attachments (encrypted metadata only).

## Stage 3
- Expo Android app: SAF folder access, the photo picker, a share target from WhatsApp and Files, and on-device OCR.
- Smarter contextual suggestions, such as "your last application also used a previous scholarship approval".
- ✅ Expiry reminders (dashboard + .ics calendar export). Next: web push notifications (free, VAPID).

## Security options for later
- An optional PIN-derived encryption layer for vault documents (trade-off: their content would not be searchable while locked).
- Web push notifications (free, VAPID) for expiry reminders.
- Biometric unlock (WebAuthn / passkeys) for the vault on phones.

chunks.title: Roadmap › Stage 4
chunks.text:
## Stage 4
- Enable shared learning after a privacy review (k-anonymity is already in place; consider adding differential-privacy noise).
- More providers (OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud via share).
- Postgres, Redis (rate limits and job queue), S3 with KMS, horizontal scaling.
- Encrypted metadata with blind indexes, an external security audit, and SOC 2 groundwork.

## Known limitations (honest list)
- The assistant's local engine understands requests through a curated bilingual lexicon of 24 document types and 8 processes, plus free-form "documents for X" tasks. Unusual phrasings fall back to content search. The optional LLM provider covers more phrasings without sending documents.
- Classification and freshness rules are heuristic. They have been tested on fictional sample documents, not yet on a corpus of real ones. Confidence is shown, and users can correct the type; corrections improve future classification.
- HEIC/AVIF photos are decoded with ImageMagick (libheif); installing `pillow-heif` is optional and faster.
- PDF preview uses the browser's built-in viewer.
- Single-process deployment (in-memory rate limiting and job queue).

chunks.title: Security & privacy
chunks.text:
# Security & privacy

## Data at rest
- **Envelope encryption.** A master key from `DOCMIND_MASTER_KEY` wraps a per-user data key (DEK) and a per-file key. AES-256-GCM is used, with an authenticated context (AAD) that binds each ciphertext to its row id, so ciphertexts cannot be swapped between rows.
- **Encrypted:** file bytes, thumbnails, OCR/extracted text, chat messages and their structured payloads, and OAuth tokens.
- **Plaintext (needed for listing and filtering):** filenames, display names, type, category, issuer, dates and tags. A future hardening step can encrypt these too, using blind indexes.
- **Deletion.** Removing a document overwrites and unlinks the blob and deletes the wrapped key (crypto-shredding). Deleting an account cascades every row; without the wrapped DEK, any remaining ciphertext in backups is unreadable.

chunks.title: Security & privacy › Vault — PIN-protected folders
chunks.text:
## Vault — PIN-protected folders
- The user chooses which categories are protected. Identity, finance and medical are protected by default as soon as a PIN is set.
- While the vault is locked, protected documents are hidden **in every API response**, enforced at a single server-side choke point (an `after_request` redaction of all JSON). Names, filenames, dates, issuers, tags, previews, thumbnails, text, downloads, bundle links, calendar exports and conversation history are all covered. Search ignores their content. The assistant can only say that a matching document exists and is protected.
- File and detail endpoints return `423 vault_locked`; the app then asks for the PIN.
- The PIN is hashed with scrypt. Unlocking issues a 5-minute vault token held only in memory. The app also drops it as soon as it goes to the background.
- After 5 wrong PINs, the vault locks for 15 minutes. Setting or changing the PIN needs the account password, and changing the PIN or un-protecting a folder needs the vault to be unlocked.
- "Sign out of all devices" also invalidates vault tokens.
- Honest scope: the vault is an access gate on top of the encryption at rest that protects everything. It is not a second, PIN-derived encryption layer. That is deliberate, so OCR, search and reminders keep working, and it is listed as a future option in the roadmap.

chunks.title: Security & privacy › Authentication & sessions
chunks.text:
## Authentication & sessions
- scrypt (N=2^15, r=8) password hashing with constant-time comparison. Unknown emails take the same time as wrong passwords.
- 15-minute HS256 access tokens, held in memory only (never in localStorage).
- A 30-day refresh token in an `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie scoped to `/api/auth`, rotated on every use. Reusing a rotated token revokes **all** of the user's sessions.
- `token_version` makes "sign out of all devices" and password changes revoke access tokens immediately.
- Rate limits apply to register, login, refresh, upload, assistant and download links.
- **Per-account lockout:** after 10 wrong passwords, the account locks for 15 minutes, on top of the per-IP limits.
- **Two-step verification (TOTP, RFC 6238):** works with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password and others. The secret is encrypted with the user's key. Sign-in returns a 5-minute `mfa_token`, and a session starts only after a valid code. There are 8 single-use recovery codes, stored hashed. Turning 2FA off needs both the password and a current code.

chunks.title: Security & privacy › Transport & browser
chunks.text:
## Transport & browser
- Strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`, with no inline scripts or styles, no eval, and `frame-ancestors 'none'`), `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and HSTS in production. `Cache-Control: no-store` is set on all JSON and file responses.
- The UI builds every element from text nodes; user data never passes through `innerHTML`.
- Files are downloaded and previewed through single-use signed links that expire after 120 seconds. Long-lived tokens never appear in URLs.
- Uploads are type-checked by magic bytes. WhatsApp ZIP imports are capped by member count and total size and read in memory; nothing is extracted to disk paths.

## External services
- No passwords for external services are ever requested. Google uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE, read-only scopes and a one-time `state`. Tokens are encrypted, and disconnecting revokes them at Google.
- An LLM is used only if the operator configures one **and** the user turns on consent. It receives the request wording only.
- Shared learning is off globally (`DOCMIND_SHARED_LEARNING`) and per user. When enabled, it shares only canonical (process, document type) pairs. Contributors are recorded as HMAC hashes, and patterns appear only once K ≥ 20 distinct contributors agree.

chunks.title: Security & privacy › Audit
chunks.text:
## Audit
`audit_log` records sign-in and failures, uploads, updates, previews and downloads, deletions, memory decisions, connector events, exports and setting changes. Users can view their own log in Settings.

## Production checklist
- [ ] Set `DOCMIND_ENV=production`, `DOCMIND_MASTER_KEY`, `DOCMIND_JWT_SECRET` (from a KMS or secrets manager), and `DOCMIND_SECURE_COOKIES=1`.
- [ ] Serve behind TLS with a WSGI server (`gunicorn -w 1 --threads 8 'docmind.app:create_app()'`). Keep one worker until the rate limiter and job queue move to Redis.
- [ ] Back up the encrypted blobs and DB; store the master key separately.
- [ ] Get an external penetration test before handling real identity documents at scale.

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם
chunks.text:
# הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם

## עלויות — בדיקה (נובמבר 2026)
| רכיב | עלות |
|---|---|
| Python, Tesseract (OCR כולל עברית), poppler, כל הספריות | חינם, קוד פתוח |
| הרצה על המחשב שלך | חינם |
| פרויקט ב-Google Cloud + Gmail API + Drive API | חינם לשימוש רגיל (אין צורך בכרטיס אשראי) |
| מצב "Testing" ב-Google (עד 100 משתמשים) | חינם |
| ספק AI חיצוני | לא בשימוש (כבוי כברירת מחדל) |
| **השקה ציבורית מעבר ל-100 משתמשים** | **בתשלום**: בדיקת אבטחה CASA, כ-540 עד 1,000 דולר בשנה |

הערה: במצב Testing גוגל מנתקת את החיבור כל 7 ימים. DocMind יציג "נדרש חיבור מחדש", ולוחצים "חיבור" שוב.

## אפליקציית אנדרואיד (הדרך המומלצת, בחינם)
1. להוריד: https://yakov-ashgar27.github.io/DocMind/DocMind.apk ולהתקין. אם Play Protect מזהיר: "פרטים נוספים" ← "להתקין בכל זאת".
2. לפתוח, לבחור קוד גישה, ובמסך "מקורות מחוברים" ללחוץ **"סריקת הטלפון"**. לאשר **גישה לכל הקבצים** ו**הצגת התראות**.
3. מומלץ: ללחוץ **"לאפשר פעולה ברקע"** ולאשר בחלון של אנדרואיד.

**שני דברים חשובים על הסריקה:**
- **לא לסגור את DocMind מרשימת האפליקציות האחרונות (החלקה) בזמן הסריקה.** זה עוצר אותה. כיבוי מסך או מעבר לאפליקציה אחרת לא מפריעים, והתראה מציגה את ההתקדמות. אם הסריקה נעצרה, היא ממשיכה מאיפה שעצרה בפתיחה הבאה.
- **חיסכון סוללה** (בעיקר בסמסונג) יכול לעצור עבודה ברקע. אם לא אישרת בשלב 3: הגדרות ← אפליקציות ← DocMind ← סוללה ← **ללא הגבלה**.

הסריקה הראשונה עוברת על כל הטלפון ולוקחת זמן, אבל אפשר לחפש כבר במהלכה. האינדקס נשמר לצמיתות ומוצפן בטלפון, ובפעמים הבאות נקראים רק קבצים חדשים.

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם › הכי מהיר: מהטלפון בלבד, בלי מחשב (GitHub Codespaces, חינם)
chunks.text:
## הכי מהיר: מהטלפון בלבד, בלי מחשב (GitHub Codespaces, חינם)
מתאים לנסות עכשיו. גיטהאב מריצה את DocMind בשבילך בענן, והכתובת פתוחה רק לחשבון הגיטהאב שלך. חשבון חינמי כולל 60 שעות הרצה בחודש. כשהמכסה נגמרת, השירות פשוט נעצר ולא מחייב (כל עוד לא הוספת אמצעי תשלום).
1. בטלפון, מחובר/ת לגיטהאב בדפדפן, לפתוח: https://codespaces.new/yakov-ashgar27/DocMind
2. ללחוץ **Create codespace** ולחכות כ-3 עד 5 דקות בהקמה הראשונה (מותקנים OCR בעברית וכל השאר).
3. כשההקמה מסתיימת, לפתוח את לשונית **PORTS**, ובשורה של 8000 (DocMind) ללחוץ על סמל הגלובוס ("Open in Browser").
4. בדף שנפתח: ⋮ ← "התקנת אפליקציה" (Android), או שיתוף ← "הוסף למסך הבית" (iPhone).
5. בפעם הבאה: github.com/codespaces ← לבחור את ה-codespace ← Start. השרת עולה לבד.

חשוב:
- המכונה נעצרת אחרי 30 דקות בלי שימוש, ופותחים אותה שוב מ-github.com/codespaces.
- codespace שלא נפתח 30 יום נמחק אוטומטית יחד עם המסמכים שבו.
- המסמכים נשמרים בשרתים של GitHub, מוצפנים אבל באותה מכונה כמו המפתח. זה טוב לניסיון. לשימוש קבוע במסמכים אישיים עדיף להריץ על המחשב שלך (שלב 1 למטה).

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם › שלב 1 — הרצה על המחשב (פעם אחת)
chunks.text:
## שלב 1 — הרצה על המחשב (פעם אחת)
1. להתקין Python 3.11 ומעלה (python.org).
2. להתקין Tesseract עם עברית:
   - Windows: להתקין מ-UB-Mannheim/tesseract, ובהתקנה לסמן את השפה Hebrew. בנוסף להתקין את poppler ל-Windows ולהוסיף אותו ל-PATH.
   - Mac: `brew install tesseract tesseract-lang poppler`
3. להפעיל:
   - Windows: לחיצה כפולה על `start.bat`
   - Mac: לפתוח טרמינל בתיקייה `docmind` ולהריץ `./start.sh`
4. לפתוח בדפדפן את http://localhost:8000
5. (רשות) לתמונות iPhone בפורמט HEIC: להתקין ImageMagick (חינם, imagemagick.org)

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם › שלב 2 — יצירת פרטי חיבור ל-Google (כ-10 דקות)
chunks.text:
## שלב 2 — יצירת פרטי חיבור ל-Google (כ-10 דקות)
1. להיכנס ל-console.cloud.google.com ← **New Project** ← לתת שם (למשל DocMind) ← Create.
2. **APIs & Services ← Library**: לחפש ולהפעיל (Enable) את **Gmail API** ואת **Google Drive API**.
3. **Google Auth Platform / OAuth consent screen**:
   - User type: **External**
   - App name: DocMind, ולמלא אימייל תמיכה
   - Audience / Test users: להוסיף את כתובת ה-Gmail שלך
   - להשאיר במצב **Testing** (לא לפרסם)
4. **Clients ← Create client** ← סוג: **Web application**
   - Authorized redirect URI: `http://localhost:8000/api/oauth/google/callback`
   - Create ← להעתיק את **Client ID** ואת **Client secret**
5. בתיקייה `docmind`: להעתיק את `.env.example` לקובץ בשם `.env` ולמלא:
   ```
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=...
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=...
   GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:8000/api/oauth/google/callback
   ```
   חשוב: לא לשלוח את ה-secret לאף אחד, גם לא בצ'אט.
6. לעצור את השרת (Ctrl+C) ולהריץ שוב `python run.py`. הקובץ `.env` נטען אוטומטית.
7. באפליקציה: **עוד ← מקורות מחוברים ← Gmail ← חיבור**. גוגל תציג אזהרה "האפליקציה לא אומתה", וזה תקין כשהאפליקציה שלך: Advanced ← Go to DocMind ← לאשר.
8. לחזור על אותו הדבר עבור Google Drive.

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם › התקנה כאפליקציה בטלפון (בחינם)
chunks.text:
## התקנה כאפליקציה בטלפון (בחינם)
DocMind היא אפליקציית ווב שניתנת להתקנה (PWA): אייקון במסך הבית, מסך מלא, בלי שורת כתובת. כדי שהטלפון יגיע לשרת שרץ על המחשב שלך, בצורה פרטית ומאובטחת, משתמשים ב-Tailscale. החבילה האישית שלו חינמית.

1. להתקין Tailscale במחשב (tailscale.com/download) ולהתחבר עם חשבון Google.
2. להתקין את אפליקציית Tailscale בטלפון ולהתחבר עם אותו חשבון.
3. במחשב, כש-DocMind רץ, להריץ בטרמינל:
   ```
   tailscale serve --bg 8000
   ```
   (בפעם הראשונה הוא יבקש לאשר HTTPS, צריך לאשר.) תתקבל כתובת כמו `https://המחשב-שלך.xxxx.ts.net`
4. בטלפון לפתוח את הכתובת:
   - **Android (Chrome):** תפריט ⋮ ← "התקנת אפליקציה" / "הוספה למסך הבית"
   - **iPhone (Safari):** כפתור השיתוף ← "הוסף למסך הבית"

הכתובת זמינה רק למכשירים שלך ב-Tailscale, לא לכל האינטרנט. לא להשתמש ב-`tailscale funnel`, כי הוא פותח את השרת לכולם.
המחשב צריך להיות דלוק כדי שהאפליקציה בטלפון תעבוד.

אם מחברים את Gmail דרך כתובת ה-Tailscale, צריך להוסיף בגוגל גם את כתובת ההפניה `https://המחשב-שלך.xxxx.ts.net/api/oauth/google/callback`, ולעדכן אותה ב-`.env`.

## כספת — תיקיות מוגנות בקוד
הגדרות ← "הגדרת קוד כספת" (סיסמת החשבון + קוד של 4 עד 12 ספרות). מיד אחר כך התיקיות זיהוי אישי, כספים ורפואי מוגנות. את התיקיות המוגנות משנים במסך קטגוריות, בכפתור "מוגנת" על כל תיקייה.
כשהכספת נעולה, המסמכים האלה מוסתרים לגמרי: שם, תוכן, תצוגה, הורדה וחיפוש. לחיצה על "מסמך מוגן" מבקשת את הקוד. הכספת ננעלת לבד אחרי 5 דקות או כשיוצאים מהאפליקציה. אחרי 5 קודים שגויים היא ננעלת ל-15 דקות.

chunks.title: הפעלת DocMind וחיבור Gmail ו-Google Drive — בחינם › אימות דו-שלבי (מומלץ, בחינם)
chunks.text:
## אימות דו-שלבי (מומלץ, בחינם)
הגדרות ← אימות דו-שלבי ← הפעלה. מוסיפים את DocMind לאפליקציית Google Authenticator, מקלידים את הקוד, ושומרים את 8 קודי הגיבוי במקום בטוח.

## תזכורות תוקף (בחינם)
מסמך עם תאריך תוקף מופיע בדף הבית לפני שהוא פג. כפתור "הוספה ליומן" מוריד קובץ יומן שנפתח ב-Google Calendar, ביומן של iPhone וב-Outlook. בהגדרות בוחרים כמה זמן מראש להזכיר: 14, 30, 60 או 90 ימים.

## בדיקה
לשאול את העוזר: "תמצא את טופס 106" או "תמצא את אישור הלימודים". מה שנמצא במייל יסומן "נמצא בחוץ — עדיין לא הורד", עם כפתור "פתיחת המייל" וכפתור "הורדה לספרייה".

chunks.text:
מה הוא עושה What it does
לא עוד תיקייה בענן. עוזר שמבין מה צריך ומכין את זה בשבילך. Not another cloud folder: an assistant that understands what you need and prepares it.
⌕ מוצא לפי תוכן Finds by content זיהוי טקסט מקומי בעברית ובאנגלית וסיווג ל-30 סוגי מסמכים, גם לסריקות ולצילומי טלפון. Local Hebrew/English OCR and classification into 30 document types, including scans and phone photos.
✦ זוכר מה נדרש Remembers what's needed "מלגת מילואים", "משכנתא", "דמי אבטלה". בפעם הבאה הוא מתחיל מהרשימה ושואל מה השתנה. שום דבר לא נשמר בלי אישורך. "Reserve scholarship", "mortgage", "unemployment": next time it starts from your list and asks what changed. Nothing is saved without your approval.
↧ תיק מסמכים להורדה Download-ready bundles כל קובץ בנפרד עם שם מסודר, בלי ZIP. PDF מאוחד רק אם רוצים. Each file separately with tidy names, no ZIP. A combined PDF only if you want one.
⚑ אומר מאיפה להשיג Says where to get it רק אחרי שחיפש בכל המקורות, הוא מציע מקור רשמי להשגת המסמך החסר. Only after searching every source does it suggest the official place to obtain what's missing.
⏰ תזכורות תוקף Expiry reminders דרכון, רישיון וכדומה. הוספה ליומן של Google או של iPhone בלחיצה. Passport, licence and more, added to Google or iPhone Calendar in one tap.
✉ Gmail, Drive ווואטסאפ Gmail, Drive and WhatsApp חיפוש בקבצים מצורפים (בחיבור מאושר בלבד), וייבוא צ'אט מיוצא מוואטסאפ. Searches attachments (only with your approval) and imports exported WhatsApp chats.
שתי גרסאות — בוחרים אחת Two editions — pick one
אותו עוזר חכם, שתי דרכים להפעיל אותו. לרוב האנשים — גרסת הטלפון.
The same smart assistant, two ways to run it. For most people: the phone edition.
📱
מומלץ לרוב האנשים Recommended for most people
DocMind לטלפון DocMind for your phone
בלי הרשמה, בלי שרת, בחינם. המסמכים נשמרים מוצפנים רק בטלפון שלך , וזיהוי הטקסט בעברית רץ בטלפון עצמו.
No sign-up, no server, free. Your documents are stored encrypted on your phone only , and Hebrew text recognition runs on the phone itself.
🤖 Android — אפליקציה להורדה (מומלץ) downloadable app (recommended)
סורקת בעצמה את הגלריה, ההורדות ותיקיית וואטסאפ, ומופיעה בתפריט "שיתוף" של כל אפליקציה (וואטסאפ, Gmail). זיהוי הטקסט בעברית עובד גם בלי אינטרנט.
Scans your gallery, Downloads and WhatsApp folder by itself and appears in every app's Share menu (WhatsApp, Gmail). Hebrew text recognition works offline.
הורדת האפליקציה לאנדרואיד Download the Android app
ההורדה איטית? קישור חלופי (GitHub) Slow download? Alternative link (GitHub)
ללחוץ על ההורדה ולפתוח את הקובץ DocMind.apk . אם מופיעה בקשה: לאשר "התקנה מהמקור הזה" לדפדפן. אם Play Protect מזהיר על מפתח לא מוכר: "פרטים נוספים" ← להתקין בכל זאת (האפליקציה בקוד פתוח, ונבנית אוטומטית מהקוד שבעמוד הזה). לפתוח, לבחור קוד גישה וללחוץ "סריקת הטלפון", ולאשר "גישה לכל הקבצים" והצגת התראות. מומלץ: במסך הסריקה ללחוץ "לאפשר פעולה ברקע" (חלון אישור של אנדרואיד), כדי שהסריקה תמשיך במסך כבוי.
חשוב לדעת על הסריקה הראשונה: היא עוברת על כל הטלפון ויכולה לקחת זמן. אפשר לכבות את המסך או לעבור לאפליקציה אחרת, והתראה תציג את ההתקדמות. לא לסגור את DocMind מרשימת האפליקציות האחרונות (החלקה) , כי זה עוצר את הסריקה. אם זה קרה, היא ממשיכה מאיפה שעצרה בפתיחה הבאה. בטלפוני סמסונג ואחרים, אם לא אישרת פעולה ברקע: הגדרות ← אפליקציות ← DocMind ← סוללה ← ללא הגבלה . האינדקס נשמר לצמיתות, ובפעמים הבאות נקראים רק קבצים חדשים.
Download and open DocMind.apk . If asked, allow "Install from this source" for your browser. If Play Protect warns about an unknown developer: "More details" → Install anyway (the app is open source and built automatically from this project's code). Open it, choose a passcode, tap "Scan my phone", and allow "All files access" and notifications. Recommended: on the scan screen tap "Allow background activity" (Android's own dialog) so scanning continues with the screen off.
About the first scan: it goes through the whole phone and can take a while. You can turn the screen off or switch apps; a notification shows progress. Don't swipe DocMind away from recent apps , because that stops the scan; if it happens, it resumes where it stopped next time. On Samsung and other phones, if you didn't allow background activity: Settings → Apps → DocMind → Battery → Unrestricted . The index is kept permanently; later scans only read new files.

"""Simulated Android run of the phone edition: a fake window.DocMindNative (same API as NativeBridge.java)
serves the test fixtures as if they were gallery photos / a granted WhatsApp folder, so the real scanner,
OCR pipeline, classifier and encrypted import are exercised in Chromium. Also checks share-in and save-out."""
import time
import base64
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.argv = [sys.argv[0], "/tmp/asim"]
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
FIX = Path("/tmp/asim_fixtures")
import shutil  # noqa: E402
shutil.rmtree(FIX, ignore_errors=True)
shutil.copytree(ROOT / "backend/tests/fixtures", FIX)
def _landscape():
    from PIL import Image
    import random
    from PIL import ImageDraw
    random.seed(4)
    im = Image.new("RGB", (1600, 1200), (70, 130, 200))           # sky
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    d.rectangle([0, 700, 1600, 1200], fill=(60, 140, 60))            # grass
    for _ in range(300):
        x, y = random.randrange(1600), random.randrange(700, 1200)
        d.ellipse([x, y, x + 30, y + 30], fill=(random.randrange(150, 255), random.randrange(40, 90), 40))  # flowers
    im.save(FIX / "PXL_landscape.jpg", quality=92)
_landscape()

class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *a, **k):
        super().__init__(*a, directory=str(MOBILE), **k)

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path.startswith("/native/file/"):
            enc = self.path.split("/native/file/")[1]
            uri = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(enc + "=" * (-len(enc) % 4)).decode()
            if uri in LATE:
                time.sleep(4)
            data = (FIX / FILES[uri][0]).read_bytes()
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(data)
            return
        return super().do_GET()

    def do_POST(self):
        data = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(data["png"].split(",", 1)[1])))
        body = json.dumps({"text": pytesseract.image_to_string(img.convert("L"), lang="heb+eng")}).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

"""Generate clearly-fictional SAMPLE documents (Hebrew + English) for tests and demos.

Every document is stamped “SAMPLE / דוגמה”, uses invented names, invented institutions and test ID
numbers. They exist to exercise OCR + classification with realistic layouts and unhelpful filenames.

usage: python scripts/make_sample_docs.py <out_dir>
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import random
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter, ImageFont

FONT = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf"
BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf"


def page(lines, size=(1240, 1754), rtl=True, photo=False, seed=1):
    """Render lines [(text, pt, bold)] onto a page. RTL lines are right-aligned with proper bidi (raqm)."""
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    img = Image.new("RGB", size, (252, 251, 248))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    y = 110
    for text, pt, bold in lines:
        if not text:
            y += pt
            continue
        font = ImageFont.truetype(BOLD if bold else FONT, pt)
        is_rtl = rtl and any("֐" <= ch <= "׿" for ch in text)
        kw = {"direction": "rtl", "language": "he"} if is_rtl else {}
        w = d.textlength(text, font=font, **kw)
        x = size[0] - 110 - w if is_rtl else 110
        d.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=(25, 25, 30), **kw)
        y += int(pt * 1.7)
    stamp = ImageFont.truetype(BOLD, 34)
    d.text((size[0] - 330, size[1] - 120), "SAMPLE / דוגמה", font=stamp, fill=(200, 40, 40),
           direction="rtl", language="he")
    if photo:  # simulate a phone photo: slight rotation, blur, uneven background
        img = img.rotate(rnd.uniform(-1.5, 1.5), expand=True, fillcolor=(90, 90, 95))
        img = img.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(0.6))
    return img


def to_pdf(img: Image.Image) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, "PDF", resolution=150)
    return buf.getvalue()

def text_pdf(lines: list[str]) -> bytes:
    from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    c = canvas.Canvas(buf, pagesize=A4)
    y = 780
    for ln in lines:

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import struct
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8000"

EMAIL, PW, PIN = "yossi@example.com", "Sup3rSecretPw", "482915"


def totp(secret):
    key = base64.b32decode(secret + "=" * (-len(secret) % 8))
    d = hmac.new(key, struct.pack(">Q", int(time.time() // 30)), hashlib.sha1).digest()
    o = d[-1] & 15
    return f"{(struct.unpack('>I', d[o:o + 4])[0] & 0x7FFFFFFF) % 1000000:06d}"

# Changelog

## v1.1.1 (2026-11-15): field-hardening

Every fix below came from running WiFi-Doctor on a real Windows 11 laptop. Each has a regression test.

- **RCA:** a single dropped probe no longer counts as packet loss (minimum 2 lost probes per window).
- **RCA:** rolling windows reset when the chaos mode changes, so back-to-back simulations are diagnosed independently.
- **Stress test:** self-induced load is excluded from incidents and from the learned baseline, and the windows are cleared when the test ends.
- **Stress test:** transfer errors are logged and returned as `diagnostics` when no speed-test endpoint is reachable.
- **Diagnosis:** Wi-Fi remediation no longer repeats the same advice twice. "Wi-Fi" casing is fixed in the physical-layer text.
- **UI:** the chaos panel no longer stretches to the height of the bufferbloat card.
- **Windows launcher** (`scripts/run_local.bat`):
  - repairs a broken session PATH and installs missing tools via winget
  - stops only its own previous instance, never other apps
  - picks free ports when 8000 or 5173 are taken
  - keeps the backend tied to the console window

chunks.title: Changelog › v1.1.0 (2026-11-15)
chunks.text:
## v1.1.0 (2026-11-15)

- **Adaptive anomaly baselines:** a per-hop rolling median/MAD baseline (400 samples) with a robust z-score, combined with the static thresholds (hybrid triggering).
- **Physical Wi-Fi telemetry:** RSSI, band, channel, SSID and PHY rates from `netsh` (locale-tolerant), `iw`, `/proc/net/wireless`, `airport` and `system_profiler`. The data is used as evidence in LOCAL_WIFI diagnoses and shown as a topology badge.
- **Active bufferbloat test:** an 8-second load test that compares loaded and unloaded latency and grades the connection A+ to F. It has a 409 concurrency guard, a 10 s watchdog and an SQM recommendation.

## v1.0.0 (2026-11-15)

- Multi-layer prober (gateway, WAN, DNS) with a scapy → icmp_dgram → ping → TCP fallback chain.
- Deterministic RCA engine with confidence scoring, chaos simulation, a SQLite incident log and an ISP CSV report.
- React + TypeScript + Tailwind NOC dashboard, Docker Compose setup and CI.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Why WiFi-Doctor?
chunks.text:
## Why WiFi-Doctor?

"The Internet is slow" can mean four very different things: a weak Wi-Fi signal, a saturated uplink, a congested ISP, or a slow DNS resolver. Each one has a different fix and a different person to call.

Packet sniffers such as Wireshark show you everything and conclude nothing. WiFi-Doctor works the other way around:

| | Passive sniffers | **WiFi-Doctor** |
|---|---|---|
| Data collection | Captures existing traffic | **Actively probes** each layer of the path every 1.5 s |
| Output | Raw packet tables | **Plain-English diagnosis** + confidence score + fix |
| Correlation | Manual | Latency/jitter/loss **correlated with local bandwidth** automatically |
| Evidence | pcap files | **Timestamped incident log + CSV report** you can send to your ISP |
| Setup | Drivers, admin rights, expertise | Runs unprivileged and **never crashes** when it lacks permissions |

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Why WiFi-Doctor? › Key features
chunks.text:
### Key features

- **Multi-layer active probing**: Gateway (Wi-Fi/LAN) → ISP/WAN (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8` backup) → DNS (real UDP/53 A-record queries).
- **Deterministic RCA engine** with five verdicts (`LOCAL_WIFI`, `BUFFERBLOAT`, `ISP_WAN`, `DNS_SERVER`, `HEALTHY`), each with a confidence score and remediation steps.
- **Rolling-window telemetry math** with NumPy: current, average and P95 RTT, jitter, and packet loss per hop.
- **Adaptive anomaly baselines**: a ~10-minute robust baseline per hop (median + MAD) yields a z-score, so a jump from 12 ms to 60 ms is caught on *your* network even though it is below every static threshold.
- **Physical Wi-Fi telemetry**: RSSI, band, channel, SSID and PHY rates from `netsh` (Windows, locale-tolerant), `iw` / `/proc/net/wireless` (Linux) and `airport` / `system_profiler` (macOS), used as evidence in Wi-Fi diagnoses.
- **Active Bufferbloat test**: an 8-second on-demand load test compares loaded and unloaded latency and grades your connection from A+ to F.
- **Bandwidth and process correlation** through `psutil`: live Mbps, observed peak, utilisation %, and the top network-consuming process.
- **Graceful probe degradation**: `scapy` raw ICMP → unprivileged ICMP sockets → OS `ping` → TCP handshake RTT.
- **Chaos Engineering mode** that injects realistic faults, so you can watch a full diagnosis even on a healthy network.
- **Incident log in SQLite** with a 30 s anti-spam cooldown, worst-case metric tracking and a one-click **ISP Evidence Report (CSV)**.
- **NOC-style React dashboard** with a live hop topology, synchronised charts, and a resilient WebSocket client (backoff, jitter, watchdog).

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Validated on a real network
chunks.text:
## Validated on a real network

The test suite is not the only evidence. WiFi-Doctor was installed on a Windows 11 laptop (Hebrew locale, 5 GHz Wi-Fi, ISP router) and every feature was run against the live network. These are the measured results, not synthetic ones:

| Check | Result on the real network |
|---|---|
| Physical Wi-Fi telemetry (`netsh`, Hebrew Windows) | SSID, **−72 to −79 dBm**, 5 GHz ch 40, 802.11ac, 97.5 Mbps PHY rate parsed correctly |
| Adaptive baselines | Learned gateway 3–4 ms, WAN 8–9 ms, DNS 9–11 ms; z-scores near 0 when healthy |
| Bufferbloat test (3 independent runs) | Grade **C** every time: +71 / +105 / +107 ms under 51–83 Mbps of load |
| All four chaos modes, switched back-to-back | 4/4 correct root cause (LOCAL_WIFI 99 %, ISP_WAN, DNS_SERVER 94 %, BUFFERBLOAT) |
| Concurrency guards | Second test → `409`, test during chaos → `409`, chaos during test → `409` |
| Incident log / ISP CSV | Self-inflicted test load creates **no** incident; "real only" export excludes all simulated rows |

The diagnosis for that laptop was consistent across every tool: a weak signal (−77 dBm) and a router without queue management. The Wi-Fi badge, the gateway latency under load and the grade all pointed to the same fix.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Validated on a real network › Bugs that only real-world testing found
chunks.text:
### Bugs that only real-world testing found

Every one of these passed CI and was caught only by running the app on real hardware. Each now has a regression test.

1. **One lost ping raised a Wi-Fi alarm.** On a weak link, 1 dropped probe in a 20-probe window is 5 %, which is over the 3 % threshold. Loss triggers now require at least 2 lost probes.
2. **Back-to-back chaos modes were misdiagnosed** (ISP loss reported as Wi-Fi), because the previous scenario's samples were still in the rolling window. Windows now reset on every mode change.
3. **The bufferbloat test logged an incident against itself,** and its loaded RTTs leaked into the "normal" baseline. Self-induced load is now excluded from incidents and baselines, and the windows are cleared when a test ends.
4. **Closing the console left the backend running,** so the next launch silently served the old version. The backend is now attached to the console window.
5. **The launcher stopped another app's processes.** It found Docker Desktop on port 8000 and killed it. The launcher now stops only its own Python/Node processes and moves to free ports when another program holds 8000 or 5173.

---

The `Prober` runs three probes concurrently (`asyncio.gather`), each bounded by a 1 s timeout. 2. The `SystemMonitor` computes Mbps from NIC counter deltas. A worker thread refreshes the top-process scan every 3 s. 3. The `ChaosSimulator` (when enabled) layers synthetic faults on top of the real samples. 4. The `IncidentRecorder` persists state transitions to SQLite. ---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix
chunks.text:
## RCA Decision Matrix

The verdict is based on a short "recent" view: the median of the last 8 good RTTs and the loss over the last 20 probes (30 s). This lets it react within seconds without flapping on a single outlier. The dashboard still shows full 60-sample (90 s) statistics. Rules are evaluated top to bottom, and the first match wins.

| # | Layer | Trigger (thresholds) | Diagnosis | Recommended remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `LOCAL_WIFI` (CRITICAL) | 100 % WAN loss **and** gateway unreachable | Network link down | Check Wi-Fi association / cable, power-cycle router & modem |
| 1 | `BUFFERBLOAT` | (Gateway RTT **> 40 ms** OR WAN RTT **> 100 ms**) **AND** link utilisation **> 70 %** of observed peak | Local bandwidth saturation (bufferbloat) | Pause/limit the bulk transfer (top process is named), enable **SQM (fq_codel / CAKE)** at ~90 % of plan speed, QoS |
| 2 | `LOCAL_WIFI` | Gateway RTT **> 35 ms** OR gateway loss **> 3 %**, while local traffic **< 15 Mbps** | Wi-Fi signal degradation or router congestion | Move closer, switch to 5/6 GHz, change channel, reboot router, confirm with Ethernet |
| 3 | `ISP_WAN` | Gateway healthy (**< 15 ms, 0 % loss**) BUT WAN RTT **> 120 ms** OR WAN loss **> 3 %** | ISP backbone congestion or upstream routing issue | Power-cycle modem/ONT, check ISP status page, **export ISP Evidence Report** and open a ticket |
| 4 | `DNS_SERVER` | Gateway & WAN healthy BUT DNS resolution **> 150 ms** OR failing (> 3 % timeouts) | Slow / unresponsive DNS resolver | Switch to `1.1.1.1` / `8.8.8.8` on the device or router DHCP |
| 5 | `NONE` | All layers within thresholds | All network layers healthy | No action needed |

**Severity:** `CRITICAL` when loss is ≥ 10 % or latency exceeds the critical threshold for that hop (Gateway 100 ms · WAN 300 ms · DNS 500 ms). Otherwise `WARNING`.

**Confidence score (0–99):** combines *how far* the metrics exceed their thresholds, *how cleanly* the other layers isolate the fault (for example, a clean gateway raises confidence in an ISP verdict), and *how many samples* support it. Weaker fallback branches (such as a degraded gateway under moderate load) are scored lower on purpose.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix › Adaptive baselines (hybrid triggering)
chunks.text:
### Adaptive baselines (hybrid triggering)

Static thresholds remain the hard guardrails. In addition, every hop keeps a rolling buffer of its last **400 good samples** (`BASELINE_WINDOW_SIZE`, ~10 min). From it the analyzer computes a **robust z-score** for the recent RTT median:

```
z = (recent_median - baseline_median) / max(1.4826 × MAD, 1 ms)
```

A hop is flagged as an **anomaly** when the baseline has at least **60 samples**, **z > 3.5**, and the RTT is above a noise floor (gateway 15 ms, WAN 35 ms, DNS 45 ms). Anomalies feed the same decision tree as static breaches, add to the confidence score in proportion to z, and are reported as `WARNING` unless a static critical threshold is also crossed. Chaos-simulated samples never enter the baseline, samples taken during an anomaly are throttled (1 in 10), and the baseline resets when the gateway or resolver changes. The dashboard shows *"Normal baseline: 12 ms (Z: +8.4)"* under each hop.

### Physical-layer evidence

When `LOCAL_WIFI` fires and the radio is weak (RSSI **< −72 dBm**) or on **2.4 GHz**, the diagnosis cites it directly: *"Weak Wi-Fi signal (−78 dBm) on 2.4 GHz channel 6: switch to 5 GHz or move closer to the router."* The confidence score also rises, because the physical measurement backs up the latency evidence. On Windows 11 24H2+, `netsh` needs **Location services** turned on to report Wi-Fi details; without them the dashboard says so, and the RCA uses latency only.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › RCA Decision Matrix › Bufferbloat grade
chunks.text:
### Bufferbloat grade

| Latency increase under load | < 5 ms | < 30 ms | < 60 ms | < 200 ms | < 400 ms | ≥ 400 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Grade** | A+ | A | B | C | D | F |

Grades C–F include an SQM/QoS recommendation. The test runs 3 streaming downloads and 1 upload against Cloudflare's speed-test endpoints (with fallbacks) for 8 s while the prober keeps measuring. Only one test can run at a time (HTTP **409** otherwise, also while a chaos simulation is active), and a 10 s watchdog aborts any test that overruns.

**Edge cases handled:**

- A gateway that never answers ICMP while the Internet works is treated as *filtering probes*, not as a fault.
- Peak bandwidth has a 10 Mbps floor, so an idle machine never looks "saturated".
- If ICMP is silently filtered on the network but UDP/DNS works, the prober switches itself to TCP-handshake RTT.

Every threshold lives in [`backend/app/config.py`](backend/app/config.py), and each one can be overridden with an environment variable (for example `GATEWAY_WARN_MS=50`).

---

## Quickstart

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Option A: Docker Compose (one command)
chunks.text:
### Option A: Docker Compose (one command)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yakov-ashgar27/wifi-doctor.git
cd wifi-doctor
docker compose up --build
```

After the containers are up, open:

- Dashboard: `http://localhost:3088`
- API docs (Swagger): `http://localhost:8088/docs`

The Docker setup uses host ports 3088 and 8088, which are uncommon, so it does not collide with other local projects that already use 3000 or 8000.

> **Networking note:** with the default bridge network, *Hop 1* measures the Docker bridge gateway rather than your Wi-Fi router. On **Linux**, use the host-network override to diagnose your real Wi-Fi:
>
> ```bash
> docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.host.yml up --build
> ```
>
> On Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows), run the backend locally (Option B) for true Wi-Fi diagnostics, or set `GATEWAY_IP=<your router>` in `docker-compose.yml`.

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Option B: Local execution
chunks.text:
### Option B: Local execution

**Requirements:** Python **3.13** and Node.js **20+**.

**Linux / macOS**

```bash
./scripts/run_local.sh            # unprivileged: icmp_dgram / ping fallback
sudo ./scripts/run_local.sh       # optional: enables scapy raw-socket ICMP
```

**Windows: one click**

Double-click **`scripts\run_local.bat`**. The launcher:

- installs Python and Node.js with `winget` if they are missing
- creates the virtualenv and installs dependencies
- picks free ports if another app (such as a Docker project) holds 8000 or 5173
- opens the dashboard

Keep its window open; closing it stops WiFi-Doctor.

```powershell
# equivalent from a PowerShell prompt
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\run_local.ps1
```

> On Windows, scapy needs [Npcap](https://npcap.com/) and an Administrator shell. Without them, WiFi-Doctor automatically uses `ping.exe` and keeps measuring real latency. On Windows 11 24H2+, turn on **Location services** so `netsh` can report Wi-Fi signal details.

**Manual setup**

```bash
# Terminal 1: backend
cd backend
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

# Terminal 2: frontend
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api and /ws to :8000)
```

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Quickstart › Try the RCA engine in 10 seconds
chunks.text:
### Try the RCA engine in 10 seconds

1. Open the dashboard and wait for the verdict to read **All network layers healthy**.
2. Click **Simulate ISP Loss**. Within a few ticks the WAN node turns red, the latency chart spikes, and the verdict becomes **ISP backbone congestion** with high confidence.
3. Click **Normal**. The incident closes in the history table with its duration and worst-case metrics.
4. Click **Download ISP Evidence Report (CSV)**.
5. With the simulation on **Normal**, click **Run Bufferbloat Test (8s)** to grade your real connection under load.
6. Try **Simulate Wi-Fi Lag**. The gateway badge switches to a weak 2.4 GHz signal, and the diagnosis cites the physical evidence.

Simulated incidents are flagged (🧪 in the UI, `simulated=yes` in the CSV). Tick **Real incidents only** to keep them out of the report you send to your ISP.

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › API reference
chunks.text:
## API reference

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WS` | `/ws` | Live stream: `snapshot` (last 80 frames on connect), `telemetry` (every tick, now with per-hop `baseline_median_ms` / `z_score` and a `wifi` block), `incident` (opened/updated/closed), `chaos`, `stress_test` |
| `GET` | `/api/status` | Latest frame, network info, uptime, connected clients |
| `GET` | `/api/incidents?page=1&page_size=10&real_only=false&layer=ISP_WAN` | Paginated incident history |
| `GET` | `/api/incidents/export?real_only=true` | Streamed CSV evidence report (formula-injection safe, Excel-friendly BOM) |
| `GET` | `/api/chaos` | Current fault-injection mode |
| `POST` | `/api/chaos/{mode}` | `none` · `wifi_lag` · `isp_loss` · `dns_slowdown` · `bufferbloat` |
| `POST` | `/api/stress-test/start` | Start the 8 s bufferbloat test (`202`; `409` if one is running or chaos is active) |
| `GET` | `/api/stress-test/status` | Progress, live Mbps and the graded result |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | Liveness probe |

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Probe reliability (fallback chain)
chunks.text:
## Probe reliability (fallback chain)

| Priority | Backend | Needs | Used when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scapy` raw ICMP | root / `CAP_NET_RAW` / Admin + Npcap | Most accurate, using kernel packet timestamps |
| 2 | `icmp_dgram` | Linux `ping_group_range` or macOS | Unprivileged ICMP sockets, no subprocess cost |
| 3 | `subprocess` | OS `ping` binary | Stock Windows; RTT parsed by a locale-tolerant regex |
| 4 | `tcp` | nothing | Locked-down containers. Times the TCP handshake (SYN→SYN/ACK **or RST**) |

Capabilities are detected at startup. If a backend starts failing at runtime (for example, permissions are revoked), the prober **demotes itself** to the next backend instead of crashing. DNS timing never needs privileges because it sends a hand-built DNS packet over a normal UDP socket.

---

chunks.title: 🩺 WiFi-Doctor › Testing
chunks.text:
## Testing

```bash
cd backend
pip install pytest
python -m pytest -q
```

The test suite feeds synthetic probe streams into the analyzer and checks every RCA branch. It also confirms that each chaos mode is diagnosed as the correct layer with ≥ 70 % confidence. Further tests check:

- the MAD/z-score math and hybrid triggering
- the Wi-Fi parsers, against captured `netsh` (English and German), `iw`, `/proc/net/wireless` and macOS output, including the Ethernet, disconnected and Location-permission cases
- the bufferbloat grade scale, the timeout and offline paths, and the HTTP 409 concurrency guard

API tests need `pip install httpx`.

chunks.text:
## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PROBE_INTERVAL_S` | `1.5` | Tick interval |
| `PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` | `1.0` | Per-probe timeout |
| `WAN_PRIMARY` / `WAN_BACKUP` | `1.1.1.1` / `8.8.8.8` | WAN probe targets |
| `GATEWAY_IP` / `DNS_SERVER` | auto | Override auto-detection |
| `PROBE_BACKEND` | auto | Force `scapy`, `icmp_dgram`, `subprocess` or `tcp` |
| `INCIDENT_COOLDOWN_S` | `30` | Minimum gap between new incidents |
| `BASELINE_WINDOW_SIZE` / `BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES` | `400` / `60` | Adaptive baseline length and warm-up |
| `ZSCORE_THRESHOLD` | `3.5` | Robust z-score that counts as an anomaly |
| `WIFI_WEAK_RSSI_DBM` | `-72` | RSSI below which Wi-Fi is cited as weak |
| `STRESS_DURATION_S` / `STRESS_TIMEOUT_S` | `8` / `10` | Bufferbloat test window and hard abort |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/wifi_doctor.db` | Storage |
| `GATEWAY_WARN_MS`, `WAN_WARN_MS`, `DNS_WARN_MS`, `LOSS_WARN_PCT`, `BLOAT_UTILIZATION_PCT`, … | see `config.py` | RCA thresholds |

## Privacy

WiFi-Doctor is 100 % local. It contacts only your gateway, two public anycast resolvers (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`) and your configured DNS server. It has no telemetry, no accounts, and no cloud.

"""Async SQLite engine + session management."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase

from .config import settings


def _ensure_sqlite_dir(url: str) -> None:
    parsed = make_url(url)
    if parsed.get_backend_name() == "sqlite" and parsed.database not in (None, "", ":memory:"):
        Path(parsed.database).expanduser().resolve().parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


_ensure_sqlite_dir(settings.database_url)

engine = create_async_engine(
    settings.database_url,
    echo=False,
    connect_args={"timeout": 15} if settings.database_url.startswith("sqlite") else {},
)

SessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False, class_=AsyncSession)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


async def init_db() -> None:
    from . import models  # noqa: F401  (register tables on Base.metadata)

    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)


async def dispose_db() -> None:
    await engine.dispose()


async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with SessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

chunks.text:
"""
Telemetry math + Root Cause Analysis decision engine.

Per hop we keep a ``deque(maxlen=60)`` of RTT samples (``None`` = lost probe)
and derive current / average / P95 / jitter / loss. Every tick the RCA engine
walks a deterministic decision tree and emits a structured ``Diagnosis``.

Decisions use a short "recent" view (median of the last 8 good RTTs, loss over
the last 20 probes) so the verdict reacts within seconds and is robust to a
single outlier, while the dashboard shows full-window statistics.

Decision order (first match wins):

  0. Link down          WAN + gateway unreachable                 -> LOCAL_WIFI   (CRITICAL)
  1. BUFFERBLOAT        (GW > 40 ms OR WAN > 100 ms) AND util > 70 %
  2. LOCAL_WIFI         (GW > 35 ms OR GW loss > 3 %) AND traffic < 15 Mbps
     LOCAL_WIFI (weak)  GW degraded under moderate, non-saturating load
  3. ISP_WAN            GW healthy (< 15 ms, 0 % loss) AND (WAN > 120 ms OR WAN loss > 3 %)
     ISP_WAN (weak)     WAN degraded while GW is merely "OK"
  4. DNS_SERVER         GW & WAN healthy AND (DNS > 150 ms OR DNS failing)
  5. HEALTHY
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import statistics
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

from ..config import Settings
from .prober import HOP_DNS, HOP_GATEWAY, HOP_WAN, NetworkInfo, ProbeSample
from .system_monitor import BandwidthSnapshot
from .wifi_stats import WifiInfo

HEALTHY, WARNING, CRITICAL, UNKNOWN = "HEALTHY", "WARNING", "CRITICAL", "UNKNOWN"
LAYER_NONE, LOCAL_WIFI, ISP_WAN, DNS_SERVER, BUFFERBLOAT = (
    "NONE", "LOCAL_WIFI", "ISP_WAN", "DNS_SERVER", "BUFFERBLOAT",
)

HOP_LABELS = {
    HOP_GATEWAY: "Local Router / Gateway",
    HOP_WAN: "ISP / External WAN",
    HOP_DNS: "DNS Resolver",
}


def _r(value: float | None, nd: int = 2) -> float | None:
    return None if value is None or math.isnan(value) else round(float(value), nd)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ stats
@dataclass
class HopStats:
    hop: str
    label: str
    target: str | None
    method: str
    current_ms: float | None
    avg_ms: float | None
    p95_ms: float | None
    min_ms: float | None

    recent_ms: float | None
    recent_loss_pct: float
    samples: int
    last_ok: bool
    status: str
    simulated: bool = False
    recent_lost: int = 0
    # Adaptive baseline (robust z-score). Optional / backward compatible.
    baseline_median_ms: float | None = None
    baseline_sigma_ms: float | None = None
    baseline_samples: int = 0
    z_score: float | None = None
    anomaly: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


class BaselineTracker:
    """Long rolling buffer of *good* RTTs with a robust (median/MAD) z-score.

    sigma = max(1.4826 * MAD, floor): 1.4826 makes the MAD a consistent
    estimator of the standard deviation for normal data, and the floor stops
    ultra-stable wired links (MAD ~ 0) from turning 0.3 ms of noise into z=10.
    """

    MAD_TO_SIGMA = 1.4826

    def __init__(self, maxlen: int, min_samples: int, sigma_floor_ms: float, admit_every: int = 10):
        self.samples: deque[float] = deque(maxlen=maxlen)
        self.min_samples = min_samples
        self.sigma_floor_ms = sigma_floor_ms
        self.admit_every = max(1, admit_every)
        self._held = 0

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self.samples.clear()

    def compute(self, recent_rtt_n: int, recent_loss_n: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data = list(self.samples)
        ok = [s for s in data if s is not None]
        n = len(data)
        arr = np.asarray(ok, dtype=float)
        # Jitter: mean absolute difference between consecutive successful RTTs
        # (the RFC 3550 inter-arrival idea, without the 1/16 smoothing).
        jitter = float(np.mean(np.abs(np.diff(arr)))) if arr.size >= 2 else None
        recent_ok = [s for s in data[-recent_rtt_n * 2 :] if s is not None][-recent_rtt_n:]
        recent_window = data[-recent_loss_n:]
        return {
            "current_ms": data[-1] if data else None,
            "avg_ms": float(arr.mean()) if arr.size else None,
            "p95_ms": float(np.percentile(arr, 95)) if arr.size else None,
            "min_ms": float(arr.min()) if arr.size else None,
            "max_ms": float(arr.max()) if arr.size else None,
            "jitter_ms": jitter,
            "loss_pct": (n - len(ok)) / n * 100.0 if n else 0.0,
            "recent_ms": float(statistics.median(recent_ok)) if recent_ok else None,
            "recent_loss_pct": (
                sum(1 for s in recent_window if s is None) / len(recent_window) * 100.0
                if recent_window else 0.0
            ),
            "recent_lost": sum(1 for s in recent_window if s is None),
            "samples": n,
            "last_ok": bool(data) and data[-1] is not None,
        }

"""
Active multi-layer network prober.

Hop 1  Gateway   ICMP echo to the default gateway (local Wi-Fi / LAN segment)
Hop 2  WAN       ICMP echo to 1.1.1.1, with 8.8.8.8 raced as backup
Hop 3  DNS       Real UDP/53 A-record query against the system resolver

ICMP backends are tried in order of fidelity and the prober degrades
gracefully instead of crashing:

    scapy        raw L3 sockets (root / Administrator + Npcap / CAP_NET_RAW)
    icmp_dgram   unprivileged ICMP datagram sockets (Linux ping_group_range, macOS)
    subprocess   the OS ``ping`` binary, RTT parsed via regex (works on stock Windows)
    tcp          TCP handshake RTT (SYN -> SYN/ACK or RST) - always available

DNS never needs privileges: it is a hand-built DNS packet sent over a normal
UDP socket, so the measured time is true resolver latency.
"""

return header + qname + struct.pack("!HH", 1, 1)  # QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN


class _DnsProtocol(asyncio.DatagramProtocol):
    def __init__(self, txid: int, future: asyncio.Future):
        self.txid = txid
        self.future = future

    def datagram_received(self, data: bytes, addr) -> None:
        if len(data) >= 12 and struct.unpack("!H", data[:2])[0] == self.txid and not self.future.done():
            self.future.set_result(data)

    def error_received(self, exc: Exception) -> None:
        if not self.future.done():
            self.future.set_exception(exc)


async def dns_query_time(server: str, domain: str, timeout: float) -> tuple[float | None, str | None]:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    txid = random.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
    future: asyncio.Future = loop.create_future()
    transport = None
    try:
        transport, _ = await loop.create_datagram_endpoint(
            lambda: _DnsProtocol(txid, future), remote_addr=(server, 53)
        )
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        transport.sendto(build_dns_query(domain, txid))
        data = await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout)
        rtt = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0
        rcode = data[3] & 0x0F
        if rcode in (0, 3):  # NOERROR / NXDOMAIN: resolver answered
            return rtt, None
        return None, f"rcode={rcode}"
    except (asyncio.TimeoutError, TimeoutError):
        return None, "timeout"
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, exc.__class__.__name__
    finally:
        if transport is not None:
            transport.close()

    async def initialize(self) -> None:
        await self.refresh_network(force=True)
        forced = self.settings.force_probe_backend
        order = [forced] + [b for b in BACKEND_ORDER if b != forced] if forced in BACKENDS else BACKEND_ORDER
        chain = []
        for name in order:
            ok = await asyncio.to_thread(BACKENDS[name].available)
            if ok:
                chain.append(name)
        self._chain = chain or ["tcp"]
        self._select(self._chain[0])
        log.info("probe backend chain: %s", " -> ".join(self._chain))

    def _select(self, name: str) -> None:
        self._pinger = BACKENDS[name]()
        self.network.probe_backend = name
        self._backend_errors = 0
        self._all_icmp_failed_ticks = 0

    def _demote(self, reason: str) -> None:
        current = self._pinger.name
        idx = self._chain.index(current) if current in self._chain else -1
        if idx + 1 < len(self._chain):
            nxt = self._chain[idx + 1]
        elif current != "tcp":
            nxt = "tcp"
        else:
            return
        log.warning("probe backend %s demoted (%s) -> %s", current, reason, nxt)
        self._select(nxt)

    async def refresh_network(self, force: bool = False) -> None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        if not force and now - self._last_detect < self.settings.network_redetect_s:

        self._last_detect = now

def _detect() -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None, str | None]:
            local_ip = detect_local_ip()
            gw, iface = detect_gateway()
            gw = self.settings.gateway_override or gw
            dns = self.settings.dns_override or detect_dns_server(gw)
            return local_ip, gw, iface or interface_for_ip(local_ip), dns

        local_ip, gw, iface, dns = await asyncio.to_thread(_detect)
        if (gw, dns) != (self.network.gateway_ip, self.network.dns_server):
            log.info("network: iface=%s ip=%s gateway=%s dns=%s", iface, local_ip, gw, dns)
        self.network.local_ip = local_ip
        self.network.gateway_ip = gw
        self.network.interface = iface
        self.network.dns_server = dns

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- probes
    async def _ping(self, host: str) -> tuple[float | None, str | None]:
        try:
            return await self._pinger.ping(host, self.settings.probe_timeout_s), None
        except BackendUnavailable as exc:
            self._demote(str(exc))
            return None, "backend-unavailable"
        except Exception as exc:  # never let a probe crash the loop
            self._backend_errors += 1
            if self._backend_errors >= 3:
                self._demote(repr(exc))
            return None, exc.__class__.__name__

    async def probe_gateway(self) -> ProbeSample:
        gw = self.network.gateway_ip
        method = self._pinger.name
        if not gw:
            return ProbeSample(HOP_GATEWAY, None, None, method, "no-gateway")
        rtt, err = await self._ping(gw)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_GATEWAY, gw, rtt, method, err if rtt is None else None)

    async def probe_wan(self) -> ProbeSample:
        method = self._pinger.name
        primary = asyncio.create_task(self._ping(self.settings.wan_primary))
        backup = asyncio.create_task(self._ping(self.settings.wan_backup))
        p_rtt, p_err = await primary
        if p_rtt is not None:
            backup.cancel()
            return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_primary, p_rtt, method)
        b_rtt, b_err = await backup
        if b_rtt is not None:
            return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_backup, b_rtt, method)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, self.settings.wan_primary, None, method, p_err or b_err or "timeout")

    async def probe_dns(self) -> ProbeSample:
        server = self.network.dns_server or "1.1.1.1"
        domain = next(self._dns_cycle)
        rtt, err = await dns_query_time(server, domain, self.settings.probe_timeout_s)
        return ProbeSample(HOP_DNS, server, rtt, "udp53", err)

"""
Incident lifecycle: turns the per-tick verdict stream into IncidentLog rows.

* Opens an incident when status leaves HEALTHY (subject to a 30 s cooldown
  after the previous incident opened, so a flapping link cannot spam the DB).
* While open, tracks the *worst* metrics seen and escalates severity / root
  cause if a more severe diagnosis appears. Only escalations touch the DB.
* Closes the incident after N consecutive HEALTHY ticks and stores duration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker

from ..config import Settings
from ..models import IncidentLog, IncidentOut
from .analyzer import CRITICAL, HEALTHY, TelemetryFrame

log = logging.getLogger("wifi_doctor.incidents")

_SEVERITY_RANK = {HEALTHY: 0, "WARNING": 1, CRITICAL: 2}


def _max(a: float | None, b: float | None) -> float | None:
    if a is None:
        return b
    if b is None:
        return a
    return max(a, b)


class IncidentRecorder:
    def __init__(self, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], settings: Settings):
        self.sessions = session_factory
        self.s = settings
        self.open_id: int | None = None
        self.open_started: datetime | None = None
        self.last_opened_at: float = 0.0
        self._healthy_streak = 0
        self._peak: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self._severity = HEALTHY
        self._confidence = 0

    async def close_dangling(self) -> None:
        """Incidents left open by a previous crash/shutdown get closed on boot."""
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            await session.execute(
                update(IncidentLog)
                .where(IncidentLog.resolved_at.is_(None))
                .values(resolved_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc))
            )
            await session.commit()

def _merge_peak(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> None:
        for key, value in self._metrics(frame).items():
            self._peak[key] = _max(self._peak.get(key), value)
        top = (frame.bandwidth.top_process or {}).get("name")
        if top:
            self._peak["top_process"] = top

    async def _open(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> dict[str, Any]:
        d, net = frame.diagnosis, frame.network
        self._peak = {}
        self._merge_peak(frame)
        self._severity, self._confidence = d.status, d.confidence_score
        row = IncidentLog(
            started_at=datetime.fromtimestamp(frame.timestamp, timezone.utc),
            severity=d.status,
            root_cause_layer=d.root_cause_layer,
            confidence_score=d.confidence_score,
            title=d.title,
            explanation=d.explanation,
            recommended_action=d.recommended_action,
            gateway_ip=net.gateway_ip,
            wan_target=frame.hops["wan"].target,
            dns_server=net.dns_server,
            probe_backend=net.probe_backend,
            simulated=frame.chaos_mode != "none",
            chaos_mode=frame.chaos_mode,
            **self._peak,
        )
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            session.add(row)
            await session.commit()
            await session.refresh(row)
        self.open_id, self.open_started = row.id, row.started_at
        self.last_opened_at = time.time()
        log.warning("incident #%s opened: %s (%s)", row.id, d.title, d.root_cause_layer)
        return {"event": "opened", "incident": IncidentOut.model_validate(row).model_dump(mode="json")}

    async def _update(self, frame: TelemetryFrame) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        d = frame.diagnosis
        self._merge_peak(frame)
        escalate = _SEVERITY_RANK[d.status] > _SEVERITY_RANK[self._severity] or (
            d.status == self._severity and d.confidence_score >= self._confidence + 10
        )
        if not escalate:
            return None
        self._severity, self._confidence = d.status, d.confidence_score
        values = {
            "severity": d.status,
            "root_cause_layer": d.root_cause_layer,
            "confidence_score": d.confidence_score,
            "title": d.title,
            "explanation": d.explanation,
            "recommended_action": d.recommended_action,
            **self._peak,
        }
        if frame.chaos_mode != "none":
            values.update(simulated=True, chaos_mode=frame.chaos_mode)
        row = await self._write(values)
        return {"event": "updated", "incident": row} if row else None

    async def _close(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        started = self.open_started or now
        if started.tzinfo is None:
            started = started.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        values = {"resolved_at": now, "duration_s": round((now - started).total_seconds(), 1), **self._peak}
        row = await self._write(values)
        log.info("incident #%s resolved after %.0fs", self.open_id, values["duration_s"])
        self.open_id = None
        self.open_started = None
        self._healthy_streak = 0
        self._severity = HEALTHY
        return {"event": "closed", "incident": row} if row else None

    async def _write(self, values: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            await session.execute(update(IncidentLog).where(IncidentLog.id == self.open_id).values(**values))
            await session.commit()
            row = (await session.execute(select(IncidentLog).where(IncidentLog.id == self.open_id))).scalar_one_or_none()
            return IncidentOut.model_validate(row).model_dump(mode="json") if row else None

"""
Chaos Engineering / Fault Injection.

The simulator sits between the real probes and the Analyzer. Real
measurements keep flowing; the active fault is layered *on top* of them, the
way a real fault would add delay or drop packets on one segment of the path.
Faults ramp in over ~3 ticks so charts show a realistic onset rather than a
step function.

"""
Active Bufferbloat stress test: loaded vs. unloaded latency.

1. The unloaded baseline is the average gateway/WAN RTT from the last 5
   ticks before the test starts.
2. Concurrent streaming downloads (and an upload) saturate the link for
   ``stress_duration_s`` (8 s) while the normal 1.5 s prober keeps measuring.
3. Latency measured *under load* is compared to the baseline. The inflation
   is graded with the usual bufferbloat scale:

       < +5 ms A+ | < +30 ms A | < +60 ms B | < +200 ms C | < +400 ms D | else F

Safety: one run at a time (``StressTestBusy`` -> HTTP 409), a strict
``stress_timeout_s`` (10 s) watchdog, and transfer workers that stop at the
next chunk boundary. Networking uses only the standard library (urllib in
worker threads), so the test adds no dependencies and never blocks the loop.

def grade_for_inflation(inflation_ms: float | None) -> str:
    """Map latency increase under load to a bufferbloat grade."""
    if inflation_ms is None:
        return "F"  # every probe under load was lost: as bad as it gets
    for limit, grade in GRADE_SCALE:
        if inflation_ms < limit:
            return grade
    return "F"


def needs_sqm(grade: str) -> bool:
    return grade in ("C", "D", "F")

def _median_p95(values: list[float | None]) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    vals = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    if not vals:
        return None, None
    arr = np.asarray(vals, dtype=float)
    return float(np.median(arr)), float(np.percentile(arr, 95))


def compute_result(
    unloaded: list[_Sample],
    loaded: list[_Sample],
    peak_down: float,
    peak_up: float,
    bytes_down: int,
    bytes_up: int,
    endpoint: str | None,

    """Pure function: grade a finished test (unit-tested directly)."""
    un_gw = _avg([s.gateway for s in unloaded])
    un_wan = _avg([s.wan for s in unloaded])
    gw_med, gw_p95 = _median_p95([s.gateway for s in loaded])
    wan_med, wan_p95 = _median_p95([s.wan for s in loaded])

    base, under = un_wan, wan_med

    async def start(self, chaos_active: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        async with self._lock:
            if self.running:
                raise StressTestBusy("A bufferbloat test is already running.")
            if chaos_active:
                raise StressTestBusy("Disable the chaos simulation before running a real stress test.")
            unloaded = [self._sample(f) for f in self._frames()[-5:]]
            self._run = _RunState(uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], time.time(), time.monotonic(), unloaded)
            self.state, self.progress, self.result, self.error, self.finished_at = "running", 0.0, None, None, None
            self.diagnostics = []
            self.live_download_mbps = self.live_upload_mbps = 0.0
            self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._execute(), name="bufferbloat-test")
        await self._emit()
        return self.status()

    def on_frame(self, frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Called by the telemetry loop every tick; keeps the samples taken under load."""
        run = self._run
        if not self.running or run is None:
            return
        if time.monotonic() - run.started_mono >= self.warmup_s:
            run.loaded.append(self._sample(frame))

    async def wait(self) -> None:
        if self._task:
            await asyncio.shield(self._task)

    async def shutdown(self) -> None:
        if self._task and not self._task.done():
            self._task.cancel()
            try:
                await self._task
            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
                pass

        assert self._run is not None
        start = self._run.started_mono
        window: deque[tuple[float, int, int]] = deque()
        while True:
            now = time.monotonic()
            elapsed = now - start
            down, up = counters.snapshot()
            window.append((now, down, up))
            while window and now - window[0][0] > 1.0:
                window.popleft()
            if len(window) >= 2 and window[-1][0] > window[0][0]:
                span = window[-1][0] - window[0][0]
                self.live_download_mbps = (window[-1][1] - window[0][1]) * 8 / 1e6 / span
                self.live_upload_mbps = (window[-1][2] - window[0][2]) * 8 / 1e6 / span
                if span >= 0.45:
                    peaks["down"] = max(peaks["down"], self.live_download_mbps)
                    peaks["up"] = max(peaks["up"], self.live_upload_mbps)
            self.progress = min(1.0, elapsed / self.duration_s)
            await self._emit()
            if elapsed >= self.duration_s:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(min(0.5, max(0.05, self.duration_s - elapsed)))

def _set_radio_type(info: WifiInfo, line: str) -> None:
    if info.radio_type:
        return
    for token, std in (("EHT", "802.11be"), ("HE-", "802.11ax"), ("VHT", "802.11ac"), ("MCS", "802.11n")):
        if token in line:
