def parse_proc_wireless(text: str, interface: str | None = None) -> WifiInfo:
    """Parse ``/proc/net/wireless`` (signal level only)."""
    info = WifiInfo(interface=interface, source="proc")
    for line in (text or "").splitlines()[2:]:
        if ":" not in line:
            continue
        name, rest = line.split(":", 1)
        name = name.strip()
        if interface and name != interface:
            continue
        parts = rest.split()
        if len(parts) >= 3:
            level = _num(parts[2])
            if level is not None:
                level = int(level)
                # Old drivers report 0..255 unsigned
                info.rssi_dbm = level - 256 if level > 0 else level
            info.interface = name
            info.is_wireless = True
            return info
    info.error = "no wireless interface"
    return info


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- macOS
def parse_airport(text: str) -> WifiInfo:
    """Parse legacy ``airport -I`` output (removed in macOS 14.4+)."""
    info = WifiInfo(source="airport")
    values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
        if ":" in line:
            k, v = line.split(":", 1)
            values[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    if not values or values.get("AirPort", "").lower() == "off" or "SSID" not in values:
        info.error = "not connected"
        return info
    info.ssid = values.get("SSID")
    rssi = _num(values.get("agrCtlRSSI"))
    info.rssi_dbm = int(rssi) if rssi is not None else None
    ch = _num((values.get("channel") or "").split(",")[0])
    info.channel = int(ch) if ch is not None else None
    info.band = band_from_channel(info.channel)
    info.tx_rate_mbps = _num(values.get("lastTxRate"))

"""Chaos control + live status endpoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request

from ..engine.simulator import ChaosMode
from ..models import ChaosState

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["control"])

MODES = [m.value for m in ChaosMode]


def _service(request: Request):
    return request.app.state.service


@router.get("/chaos", response_model=ChaosState)
async def get_chaos(request: Request) -> ChaosState:
    sim = _service(request).simulator
    return ChaosState(mode=sim.mode.value, since=sim.since, available=MODES)


@router.post("/chaos/{mode}", response_model=ChaosState)
async def set_chaos(mode: str, request: Request) -> ChaosState:
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"Unknown chaos mode '{mode}'. Use one of: {', '.join(MODES)}")
    service = _service(request)
    if mode != "none" and service.stress.running:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="A bufferbloat stress test is running; wait for it to finish.")
    if service.simulator.mode.value != mode:
        # Rolling windows still hold the previous scenario's synthetic samples;
        # start clean so each verdict reflects only the current mode (baselines are kept).
        service.analyzer.reset()
    service.simulator.set_mode(mode)
    await service.broadcast({"type": "chaos", "mode": mode, "since": service.simulator.since})
    return ChaosState(mode=mode, since=service.simulator.since, available=MODES)


@router.get("/status")
async def status(request: Request) -> dict:
    service = _service(request)
    return {
        "app": "WiFi-Doctor",
        "uptime_s": round(time.time() - service.started_at, 1),
        "clients": len(service.clients),
        "chaos_mode": service.simulator.mode.value,
        "network": service.prober.network.to_dict(),
        "wifi": service.monitor.wifi.to_dict() if service.monitor.wifi else None,
        "stress_test": service.stress.status(),
        "latest": service.latest,
    }

"""
TelemetryService: the real-time pipeline.

    Prober ─┐
            ├─> ChaosSimulator ─> Analyzer (RCA) ─┬─> WebSocket broadcast
    SystemMonitor ┘                               └─> IncidentRecorder ─> SQLite
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Any

from fastapi import WebSocket

from .config import Settings
from .database import SessionLocal
from .engine.analyzer import Analyzer
from .engine.prober import Prober
from .engine.recorder import IncidentRecorder
from .engine.simulator import ChaosSimulator
from .engine.stress_test import StressTestRunner
from .engine.system_monitor import SystemMonitor

log = logging.getLogger("wifi_doctor.service")


class TelemetryService:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings):
        self.settings = settings
        self.prober = Prober(settings)
        self.monitor = SystemMonitor(settings)
        self.analyzer = Analyzer(settings)
        self.simulator = ChaosSimulator()
        self.recorder = IncidentRecorder(SessionLocal, settings)
        self.clients: set[WebSocket] = set()
        self.history: deque[dict[str, Any]] = deque(maxlen=settings.history_frames)
        self.latest: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        self.stress = StressTestRunner(settings, frames=lambda: list(self.history), broadcast=self.broadcast)
        self.started_at = time.time()
        self._task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._top_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._wifi_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._last_top_refresh = 0.0
        self._last_wifi_refresh = -1e9
        self._quiet_until = 0.0  # suppress self-inflicted incidents around a stress test
        self._stress_active = False

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ lifecycle
    async def start(self) -> None:
        await self.prober.initialize()
        self.monitor.set_interface(self.prober.network.interface)
        self.monitor.sample()  # prime counters
        await self.recorder.close_dangling()
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(), name="telemetry-loop")

async def _refresh() -> None:
            try:
                await asyncio.to_thread(self.monitor.refresh_top_process)
            except Exception:
                log.debug("top-process scan failed", exc_info=True)

        self._top_task = asyncio.create_task(_refresh())

    def _maybe_refresh_wifi(self) -> None:
        """PHY stats shell out (netsh / iw / system_profiler): worker thread, every few seconds."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - self._last_wifi_refresh < self.settings.wifi_refresh_s:
            return
        if self._wifi_task and not self._wifi_task.done():
            return
        self._last_wifi_refresh = now

        async def _refresh() -> None:
            try:
                await asyncio.to_thread(self.monitor.refresh_wifi)
            except Exception:
                log.debug("wifi scan failed", exc_info=True)

        self._wifi_task = asyncio.create_task(_refresh())

    async def tick(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        probes = await self.prober.probe_all()
        self.monitor.set_interface(self.prober.network.interface)
        bandwidth = self.monitor.sample()
        self._maybe_refresh_top_process()
        self._maybe_refresh_wifi()

        probes, bandwidth = self.simulator.apply(probes, bandwidth)
        wifi = self.simulator.apply_wifi(self.monitor.wifi)
        if self.stress.running:
            # Latency stays inflated for a moment after the load stops (queues drain).
            self._quiet_until = time.monotonic() + 2 * self.settings.probe_interval_s
            self._stress_active = True
        elif self._stress_active:
            # Test just ended: the 30 s loss window still holds probes that timed out
            # under our own load. Start the rolling windows clean (baselines are kept).
            self._stress_active = False
            self.analyzer.reset()
        self_loaded = self.stress.running or time.monotonic() < self._quiet_until
        frame = self.analyzer.ingest(
            probes, bandwidth, self.prober.network, self.simulator.mode.value, wifi, learn_baseline=not self_loaded
        )
        payload = frame.to_dict()
        self.latest = payload
        self.history.append(payload)
        self.stress.on_frame(payload)

        await self.broadcast({"type": "telemetry", "frame": payload})
        event = await self.recorder.process(frame, suppress=self_loaded)
        if event:
            await self.broadcast({"type": "incident", **event})
        return payload

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ websocket
    async def register(self, ws: WebSocket) -> None:
        await ws.accept()
        self.clients.add(ws)
        await ws.send_text(
            json.dumps({"type": "snapshot", "frames": list(self.history), "stress_test": self.stress.status()})
        )

    def unregister(self, ws: WebSocket) -> None:
        self.clients.discard(ws)

    async def broadcast(self, message: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        if not self.clients:
            return
        text = json.dumps(message, default=str)

        async def _send(ws: WebSocket) -> WebSocket | None:
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(ws.send_text(text), timeout=2.0)
                return None
            except Exception:
                return ws

        dead = await asyncio.gather(*(_send(ws) for ws in list(self.clients)))
        for ws in dead:
            if ws is not None:
                self.clients.discard(ws)

def _feed(analyzer: Analyzer, n: int, gen, bandwidth=None):
    rng = random.Random(3)
    frame = None
    for i in range(n):
        frame = analyzer.ingest(gen(rng, i), bandwidth or bw(), NET)
    return frame


def _stable(rng, _i):
    return probes(rng.uniform(1.5, 2.5), rng.uniform(11, 13), rng.uniform(8, 10))


class TestHybridTriggering:
    def test_baseline_fields_surface_in_frame(self):
        frame = _feed(Analyzer(settings), 80, _stable)
        wan = frame.hops[HOP_WAN]
        assert wan.baseline_samples >= settings.baseline_min_samples
        assert 11 <= wan.baseline_median_ms <= 13
        assert wan.z_score is not None and abs(wan.z_score) < 3.5
        assert not wan.anomaly
        d = frame.to_dict()["hops"]["wan"]
        assert {"baseline_median_ms", "z_score", "anomaly", "baseline_samples"} <= d.keys()

    def test_adaptive_trigger_catches_what_static_misses(self):
        """WAN goes 12 ms -> 60 ms: far below the 120 ms static threshold, but 30+ sigma
        above this network's normal. Only the adaptive path can see it."""
        a = Analyzer(settings)
        _feed(a, 100, _stable)
        frame = _feed(a, 12, lambda r, i: probes(r.uniform(1.5, 2.5), r.uniform(58, 62), r.uniform(8, 10)))
        wan = frame.hops[HOP_WAN]
        assert wan.anomaly and wan.z_score > 3.5
        assert wan.recent_ms < settings.wan_warn_ms           # static would say "healthy"
        assert wan.status == "WARNING"
        assert frame.diagnosis.root_cause_layer == "ISP_WAN"
        assert frame.diagnosis.status == "WARNING"
        assert "baseline" in frame.diagnosis.explanation

    def test_no_anomaly_without_enough_baseline(self):
        a = Analyzer(settings)
        _feed(a, 30, _stable)                                 # < 60 samples
        frame = _feed(a, 12, lambda r, i: probes(2, r.uniform(58, 62), 9))
        assert not frame.hops[HOP_WAN].anomaly
        assert frame.diagnosis.status == "HEALTHY"

    def test_noise_floor_suppresses_tiny_absolute_changes(self):

def bw(down: float = 1.0, up: float = 0.2, peak_down: float = 100.0, peak_up: float = 20.0) -> BandwidthSnapshot:
    return BandwidthSnapshot(down, up, peak_down, peak_up, "wlan0", 866.0, True, None)


def probes(gw: float | None, wan: float | None, dns: float | None) -> dict[str, ProbeSample]:

        HOP_WAN: ProbeSample(HOP_WAN, "1.1.1.1", wan, "test"),
        HOP_DNS: ProbeSample(HOP_DNS, "192.168.1.1", dns, "udp53"),
    }


def run(n: int, gen, bandwidth=None, chaos: ChaosSimulator | None = None):
    analyzer = Analyzer(settings)

    for i in range(n):

        b = bandwidth or bw()
        if chaos:

# One-command startup:   docker compose up --build
# Dashboard:             http://localhost:3088
# API docs:              http://localhost:8088/docs
#
# Host ports 3088/8088 are deliberately uncommon so WiFi-Doctor can run next
# to other local projects that already use 3000/8000.
#
# Default = bridge networking (works on Linux, macOS and Windows Docker Desktop).
# In bridge mode "Hop 1" is the Docker bridge gateway, not your Wi-Fi router.
# For true Wi-Fi diagnostics on Linux, add the host-network override:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.host.yml up --build

services:
  backend:
    build: ./backend
    container_name: wifi-doctor-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    cap_add:
      - NET_RAW      # enables the high-fidelity scapy / raw ICMP probe backend
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////data/wifi_doctor.db
      - CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3088,http://127.0.0.1:3088,http://localhost:5173
      # Optional overrides:
      # - GATEWAY_IP=192.168.1.1
      # - DNS_SERVER=192.168.1.1
      # - PROBE_BACKEND=subprocess
    volumes:
      - wifi-doctor-data:/data
    ports:
      - "8088:8000"

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    container_name: wifi-doctor-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "3088:80"

volumes:
  wifi-doctor-data:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WiFi-Doctor local runner for Linux / macOS.
#   ./scripts/run_local.sh          -> backend + frontend dev server
#   sudo ./scripts/run_local.sh     -> same, with raw-socket (scapy) probing
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PY="${PYTHON:-python3}"

echo "==> WiFi-Doctor | root: $ROOT"

# ---------- backend ----------
cd "$ROOT/backend"
if [ ! -d .venv ]; then
  echo "==> creating Python virtualenv"
  "$PY" -m venv .venv
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install --quiet --upgrade pip
pip install --quiet -r requirements.txt

echo "==> starting backend on http://127.0.0.1:8000"
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 &
BACKEND_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  echo; echo "==> shutting down"
  kill "$BACKEND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

# ---------- frontend ----------
cd "$ROOT/frontend"
if [ ! -d node_modules ]; then
  echo "==> installing frontend dependencies"
  npm install --no-fund --no-audit
fi
echo "==> dashboard: http://localhost:5173"
npm run dev

game states
Seven states, and every path leads back to the menu.
MENU PLAYING PAUSED PLAYER_DIED LEVEL_COMPLETE GAME_OVER VICTORY
two algorithms that make it smart
The enemy hunts you with BFS
Breadth-first search finds the first step on the shortest path to the player, around walls and bombs.
queue = deque([(start, None)])
while queue:
pos, first = queue.popleft()
for d in Direction:
nxt = step(pos, d)
if nxt == goal: return first or d
if walkable(nxt) and nxt not in seen:
seen.add(nxt)
queue.append((nxt, first or d))
Chain reactions with a queue
Every bomb a flame touches joins the queue, and each bomb explodes exactly once.
queue = list(due_bombs)
while queue:
bomb = queue.pop()
if bomb in done: continue
done.append(bomb)
for tile in flame_path(bomb):
other = bomb_at(tile)
if other and other not in done:
queue.append(other)

quality
84 pytest tests, headless – no window needed

13 slide presentation, plus SRS and work plan
Tests cover game logic, enemies, bombs, levels, high scores, sound synthesis, translations and right-to-left text.

The work plan split the team into four roles: management & spec, game logic, enemies & levels, and interface & quality.
key insights
Separate logic from display Keeping Pygame out of the rules made the core testable, and turned the renderer into a thin layer that is easy to change.
Tests alongside the code Writing tests in parallel with each module, not at the end, kept the last weeks free for user testing and polish.

← back to projects
Final project · University of Haifa
FitVision AI
A web information system that watches a workout through the phone camera, coaches technique in real time, and turns every set into an analytical progress report for the trainer.
▶ Live demo
Source code
The demo runs on a free server that sleeps when idle, so the first load takes about 30 seconds.
Project Final project · University of Haifa
Team 4 students · Scrum
My role Lead full-stack developer
Status MVP live · field-tested
the idea
The problem
Many people train without a coach next to them, at home or in an open gym. They repeat exercises with poor form and get no objective feedback, which raises the risk of injury. Trainers, on their side, have no systematic way to follow trainees remotely and rely on what the trainee reports.
The solution
Pose detection in the browser, straight from the phone camera
Rep counting and form feedback on screen and by voice, as you train
Every workout logged at the set, rep and error-event level
Automatic reports, trends and alerts for the trainer
Video never leaves the phone – only numbers reach the server

chunks.title: fitness-tracker.html
chunks.text:
my role
I was the lead full-stack developer, responsible for the system architecture and the database. In practice that meant owning the server side and the design documents behind it:
Architecture Overall system design, chapter 4 of the specification: DFD (levels 0 and 1), ERD, business rules and the permission model.
Database A normalized 17-table SQL Server schema, versioned with Alembic migrations.
API The FastAPI server: authentication with JWT, role-based access control for trainees, trainers and admins.
Reports engine Automatic post-workout reports with trends, exported to RTL PDF and Excel by background workers.
how it works
The heavy work happens on the trainee's phone. The server only receives the numeric results of each set, which keeps the system fast and private by design.
Trainee phone React PWA
MediaPipe Pose 33 body landmarks per camera frame, in a Web Worker
Technique engine joint angles, rep counting, rule checks
Live coach skeleton overlay, counter, voice cues
↓ HTTPS · set data as JSON only – no video
Server Python · FastAPI
API gateway JWT authentication and an RBAC check on every request
Core services users, plans, sessions, sets, reps, errors
Reports engine metrics, trends, PDF & Excel in the background
Alerts engine daily scheduled job, alerts to the trainer
↓ SQLAlchemy · cache & queue · email
Data & services

chunks.title: fitness-tracker.html
chunks.text:
↓ SQLAlchemy · cache & queue · email
Data & services
SQL Server 17 tables, numeric data only
Redis + RQ cache and background job queue
Email reports and reminders
↑ HTTPS · REST
Trainer browser
Dashboard & reports trends, alerts, notes, PDF / Excel export
counting a rep
A rep is a state machine over a joint angle, not a single threshold. This is what stops noise and half-reps from being counted. Example: the knee angle in a squat.
Standing start / end of a rep
angle drops below 150°
Down checks descent rules
below the 100° depth threshold
Bottom records the lowest angle
rises 10° from the minimum
Up checks ascent rules
above 160° → rep +1
Going back up without reaching the bottom is a partial rep and is not counted. All thresholds live in the database (TechniqueRules), so each exercise can be tuned without changing code.

chunks.text:
above 160° → rep +1
Going back up without reaching the bottom is a partial rep and is not counted. All thresholds live in the database (TechniqueRules), so each exercise can be tuned without changing code.
data model
Seventeen normalized tables, in five groups. The core is a strict hierarchy: a session holds sets, a set holds reps, and every form mistake is stored as an event on the rep where it happened. That level of detail is what makes the trainer reports possible.
People & access Users TraineeProfiles TrainerProfiles TrainerTraineeAssignments AuditLog
Plans Goals WorkoutPlans PlanExercises
Exercise catalog Exercises TechniqueRules
Workout data WorkoutSessions ↳ ExerciseSets ↳ Repetitions ↳ FormErrorEvents
Reporting Reports TrainerNotes ReportDeliveries
the app
Trainee screens on the phone: home, camera setup and the live workout with skeleton overlay and form alerts. The interface is in Hebrew, right to left.
Trainer dashboard on desktop
testing with a real user
After the MVP was built we ran it on a real Android phone and read the results straight from the database. The data showed problems that no test on paper had caught:
What the data showed What we changed
A squat set logged 10 reps, but 3 were noise – twitches of 200–300 ms when entering the frame. A movement shorter than 0.6 s, or one that doesn't go 10° past the threshold, is no longer counted.
In bicep curls not a single rep passed – the thresholds were too strict for a side-view camera. Recalibrated 50° → 75° and 20° → 35°, shipped as a database migration, not a code release.
The same correction repeated on every frame, even after it was fixed. A coaching layer: one cue per rule per rep, rotating phrasings, plus "go all the way down" prompts and milestones.
From 2–3 meters away the on-screen text was hard to read. Voice feedback on by default, in Hebrew or English, with a short sound for every good rep.

engineering
17 database tables
66 automated tests in CI
3 databases tested: SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite
0 frames of video sent to the server
Works offline: a workout is saved on the phone in IndexedDB and syncs automatically when the network is back.
Installable: a PWA for phones, tablets and laptops, including iPhone and iPad.
Deployed: every push to main redeploys the app to Render, with PostgreSQL on Neon.
key insights
Privacy is an architecture decision Running pose detection on the device meant the server never needs video. That one choice solved privacy, bandwidth and server cost together.
Rules belong in data, not code Storing technique thresholds as database rows turned the post-trial recalibration into a migration, and lets an admin add exercises without a developer.
Real users beat assumptions One session on a real phone exposed noise, wrong thresholds and unreadable screens. Reading the raw data showed exactly where to fix.
Let constraints pick the tools Hebrew PDFs ruled out WeasyPrint, so reports print through Chromium. Slow report jobs moved to a Redis queue to keep the API fast.
what's next
Accuracy Validation against 40 labeled videos, with a target of at least 95% rep-count accuracy and 85% recall on form errors for every exercise.
Pilot A pilot with 5 trainers and 15 trainees, aiming for a SUS usability score of 70 or more.
Exercises More exercises beyond the four in the MVP (squat, lunge, bicep curl, shoulder press) – added as data through TechniqueRules.
Showcase Live demo, poster and presentation at the department's project conference, June 2028.

Web game · puzzle-stealth
The Map Lies
“The map always lies. The only question is about what.” A grid-based puzzle-stealth game where the minimap you rely on is deliberately wrong – and every level is mathematically guaranteed to be solvable without guessing.
▶ Play in the browser
Source code
Installable as an app on Windows, Mac, Android, iPhone and iPad, and playable offline. Hebrew by default, English one click away.
Type Puzzle-stealth web game
Stack React 19 · TypeScript · Vite
Levels 5 hand-made + endless procedural
Verified 500 generated levels per test run
the idea
How it plays
You crawl through a pitch-black dungeon with a lantern that lights only the 3×3 tiles around you. A minimap in the corner shows the whole level – but it hides one or more deliberate lies. Compare what the lantern shows with what the map claims, and click the tile to call out the lie.
What makes it work
Catch every lie and the fog lifts and the map “confesses”
Disguised traps punish players who trust the map blindly
From level 5 the map gets angry : it glitches near an uncaught lie, but never says where
All sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API – no audio files

chunks.title: the-map-lies.html
chunks.text:
five kinds of lies
Lie The map says Reality
Phantom Wall Wall Open floor – often a hidden shortcut
Illusion Floor Open path Solid wall, a dead end
Disguised Trap Safe floor or a treasure chest A lethal spike trap
Fake Exit Exit in room A The real exit is in room B
Relocated Treasure Chest in room A The real chest is in room B
the level generator
Every endless-mode level comes from a seeded random generator, so the same seed always builds the same dungeon. One attempt runs five stages:
Carve A recursive-backtracker maze on odd coordinates.
Open up Knock out ~10% of walls for loops, then carve 1–3 rooms.
Place Exit on the safe tile farthest from the start, by BFS; chests in dead ends.
Inject lies Draw N lies, spaced apart and away from the start.
Validate Accept only if every rule passes; otherwise retry with the next seed.
zero-guessing validator
The hard part of a game built on lies is fairness: a player must always be able to deduce a lie, never guess it. Every level – generated or hand-made – must pass five invariants, all checked with BFS on the true grid:
R1 · Reachability A trap-free path from start to the real exit always exists.
R2 · Observability Every lie is inside the lantern’s view from some reachable tile.
R3 · No blind steps Every trap is visible one step before you could stand on it.
R4 · Deducible Each lie creates a contradiction the player can actually see.
R5 · Bookkeeping Map and truth differ only at declared lies – no accidental ones.

chunks.title: the-map-lies.html
chunks.text:
R4 · Deducible Each lie creates a contradiction the player can actually see.
R5 · Bookkeeping Map and truth differ only at declared lies – no accidental ones.
proof, not hope
500 generated levels validated on every run (100 levels × 5 seeds)
~0.5 ms average generation time, under 10 ms worst case
≤ 3 attempts any level has ever needed
0 runtime dependencies besides React
The test script also feeds the validator deliberately broken levels – a choke-point trap, an undeclared difference, a sealed-off lie – and checks it rejects each one.
It checks that generation is deterministic and that the game rules behave as specified.
GitHub Actions runs the verification and the build on every push, then deploys to GitHub Pages.
key insights
Fairness has to be provable A game about lies is only fun if the lies are fair. Writing the rules down as invariants turned “feels fair” into something a test can check.
Generate, then validate Instead of a generator that is clever enough to never fail, a simple generator plus a strict validator and retry is easier to trust and to change.
Test the tester Feeding the validator broken levels on purpose proves it actually catches the problems it claims to.
Seeds make bugs reproducible Because every level comes from a seed, any strange level can be replayed exactly with ?seed= and ?level= .

AI project · retrieval-augmented generation
yakov .LLM
A portfolio is a stack of repositories that nobody has time to read. So I built a reader that never gets tired: an AI assistant that has gone through every line I have pushed to GitHub, answers questions about it in Hebrew or English, and points to the exact lines behind each answer. And when I push a change, it reads that too.
▶ Ask it something
Code
Works in the browser and installs as an app on phone and desktop. Try “How does the Bomberman enemy find the player?” and click the number next to the answer.
Type AI assistant · RAG
Stack Python · JavaScript · LLM APIs
Knows Every repo on my GitHub, 600+ passages
Running cost $0 (free tiers)
the idea
The problem
A recruiter opens my GitHub for a minute and a half. In that time they can't learn why the Bomberman enemy uses breadth-first search, how FitVision counts a squat, or why The Map Lies never forces a guess. All of that is in the code, but nobody will dig for it.
The answer
Ask anything about my projects, in Hebrew or English
Every claim in the answer carries a number like [2]
Click it, and the exact lines open with a link to them on GitHub
If the code doesn't say, it says so. No made-up features

chunks.title: yakov-llm.html
chunks.text:
from question to cited answer
Read Follow my GitHub account and pull every repo: code, docs, pages and config.
Split Cut files into passages that remember their repo, path and line numbers.
Search Rank the passages for the question with a BM25 engine I wrote from scratch.
Write A language model drafts the answer from the top passages only, streamed word by word.
Cite Each claim links to its passage, so the reader can check the source instead of trusting the model.
a search engine from scratch
I could have used a vector database and an embedding model. For about 600 passages full of exact identifiers like find_path_step or RBAC , plain keyword ranking is faster, needs no model download, and is easy to explain. The interesting part was making it understand both of my languages:
Code-aware findPathStep also counts as find , path and step , and chase_range as chase and range .
Hebrew-aware Hebrew glues words together: “והאויבים” also searches for “האויבים” and “אויבים”.
Bilingual A Hebrew question about English code gets English search terms: “אויב” brings in enemy , “רודף” brings in chase .
Fair ranking Words in file names and headings weigh more, test files step back unless you ask about tests, and no single file can fill the whole answer.
# BM25: rare words that appear often in a short passage score highest
score += idf(term) * tf * (K1 + 1) / (tf + K1 * (1 - B + B * length / avg_length))
it keeps itself up to date
A portfolio assistant that forgets my latest work is worse than none. yakov.LLM compares every repo's last push time with what it already knows, and re-reads only what changed. There are three ways it hears about a change:
Every 30 minutes The server checks my GitHub account and swaps in the new index without a restart.
On every push A webhook with a signed secret can trigger a sync within seconds.
Every 6 hours A GitHub Action rebuilds the knowledge base and republishes the app.
The first surprise On its very first run, it found a new project on my account and read its code. The project was yakov.LLM itself.

chunks.title: yakov-llm.html
chunks.text:
Every 6 hours A GitHub Action rebuilds the knowledge base and republishes the app.
The first surprise On its very first run, it found a new project on my account and read its code. The project was yakov.LLM itself.
measured, not guessed
I wrote 38 questions with known answers, 20 in Hebrew and 18 in English, and score the search on every change. A question is a hit when the file that holds the answer is in the top five results.
87% of questions find the right file in the top 5
70→85% Hebrew questions, before and after the bilingual glossary
<1 ms per search, in Python or in the browser
26 automated tests, plus a guard that fails CI if accuracy drops
The same search engine runs in Python on the server and in JavaScript in the browser. A test runs both on every question and requires identical results.
The server has no dependencies : the HTTP server, the streaming model client and the search engine all use only the standard library.
The model is pluggable: Gemini and Groq on free tiers, Claude , or any OpenAI-compatible API. Without any key it still answers with the matching passages.
key insights
Retrieval is the product The model can only be as right as the passages it gets. Measuring the search did more for answer quality than any prompt tweak.
Citations build trust An answer you can check in one click is worth more than a longer one you have to believe.
Simple beats fashionable BM25 plus a small bilingual glossary beat my expectations for code questions. The evaluation set will say when embeddings start to pay off.
Build with AI, verify like an engineer I built yakov.LLM with Claude as a pair programmer. The tests, the evaluation set and the parity check are how I made sure that what we built actually works.
tech stack
Python (standard library) BM25 RAG Gemini · Groq · Claude APIs Server-Sent Events Vanilla JavaScript PWA & service worker GitHub Actions GitHub Pages Docker · Render pytest · Playwright

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Contents
chunks.text:
## Contents

[The problem](#the-problem) · [What it does](#what-it-does) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Data Studio](#data-studio-bring-your-own-data) · [Connectors](#connect-your-data-sources-self-hosted-free) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Design decisions](#design-decisions) · [Statistical methods](#statistical-methods) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Testing](#testing) · [Limitations](#limitations--roadmap)

---

## The problem

Digital teams make product decisions from dashboards every day. Three mistakes recur, and each one is expensive:

| Mistake | What it looks like | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **Shipping noise** | "Variant B is up 3%, ship it!" The test is underpowered and *p = 0.18*. | Roll-outs of features that do nothing, or harm, and a team that stops trusting experiments. |
| **Averages hide the problem** | The overall funnel looks fine, while mobile users in one market abandon at twice the rate. | Revenue leaks silently at the highest-intent step. |
| **Choosing AI on vibes** | An LLM is picked from a few impressive answers, without confidence intervals, hallucination rates or cost per ticket. | Over-paying for accuracy that isn't significantly better, or deploying a model that fabricates answers. |

Most tools stop at charts. **PulsePort turns data into decisions:** every insight comes with the statistical test behind it, a correction for multiple comparisons, and a plain-language recommendation.

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › What it does
chunks.text:
## What it does

PulsePort answers three questions for any digital product: a booking portal, an online store, a SaaS app, a bank.

1. **Where are we losing users, and who exactly?** An ordered funnel analysis tests every segment *and segment pair* (e.g. *country × device*) at every step against everyone else. It controls the false-discovery rate, estimates lost conversions, and detects when latency predicts abandonment.
2. **Did the change actually work?** A/B analysis runs frequentist and Bayesian inference side by side. It adds a sample-ratio-mismatch check, Fisher's exact test for small samples, Holm correction for more than two variants and a pre-registered power rule. The result is an explicit **GO / NO-GO / KEEP RUNNING / STOP** verdict that **prevents false-positive roll-outs**.
3. **Which AI assistant should we deploy?** Model evaluation reports scores with confidence intervals, hallucination rates against a safety guardrail, P95 latency, cost per 1,000 tickets, and significance tests between models.

It works in two modes:

| | **Data Studio** (public site) | **Full platform** (self-hosted, `docker compose up`) |
|---|---|---|
| Data in | CSV upload, paste from Excel or Sheets, Google Sheet / CSV link | Plus PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Google Analytics 4, server-side CSV |
| Engine | TypeScript port of the stats engine, **verified against SciPy** | Python / SciPy engine + analytical SQL on PostgreSQL 16 |
| Privacy | Runs entirely in the browser; nothing is uploaded | Credentials stay on your server, with read-only queries |
| Cost | Free (GitHub Pages) | Free (open source, your own machine) |

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › What it does › Example: what it finds on the bundled e-commerce sample
chunks.text:
### Example: what it finds on the bundled e-commerce sample

> 🔴 **country × device = BR · mobile under-performs at checkout_start → payment**: 32.6% pass vs 64.4% for everyone else (−31.8 pp, FDR q < 0.0001). Closing the gap is worth ≈24 conversions in the period.
> 🔴 **Slower checkout load predicts abandonment** at checkout_start → payment: r = −0.23, Holm-adjusted p < 0.0001.
> 🟢 Desktop out-performs at product_view → add_to_cart (+4.0 pp, q = 0.008).

And on an A/B test with a +2.9% lift (p = 0.18):

> 🟡 **KEEP RUNNING**. Inconclusive, so do not roll out yet. The test has only 63% power to detect a +5% effect, and P(B>A) = 90.9% is suggestive but not conclusive. About 48 more days are needed at current traffic.

---

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Data Studio: bring your own data
chunks.text:
## Data Studio: bring your own data

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| **1. Connect** | Upload a CSV, paste a table copied from Excel or Google Sheets, or connect a **Google Sheet / public CSV URL**. Re-connect any time to refresh with live data. |
| **2. Detect & map** | Columns are profiled (id, timestamp, category, number, boolean) and the dataset type is detected. Every mapping can be changed, and any column names work. |
| **3. Analyse** | The same statistics as the Python engine run **in your browser**, verified against SciPy on 22 test groups. |
| **4. Act** | Insights are ranked by severity and business impact. Export a Markdown report or a CSV of the results. |

**Supported datasets**

| Type | Minimum columns | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **Event log / funnel** | session or user id, event name (optional: timestamp, latency, up to 3 segment columns) | Ordered funnel. Every segment **and segment pair** is tested at every step against everyone else, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and an estimate of lost conversions. You also get the latency ↔ abandonment link (Holm-adjusted), a daily trend with a 7-day MA, and a week-over-week change alert. |
| **Funnel, aggregated** | step, users (optional: segment columns) | The same diagnostics from counts, e.g. a GA4 export or a `GROUP BY` result. Warns when counts aren't nested. |
| **A/B test, per user** | variant, converted 0/1 (optional: numeric metric, timestamp, segments) | Sample-ratio-mismatch check, z / χ² / **Fisher exact** for small samples, Katz CI, Holm correction for more than two variants, Beta-Binomial P(B>A) and expected loss, power at your MDE, days remaining, Mann-Whitney and Welch on the metric, effect reversals by segment, and a verdict. |
| **A/B test, summary** | variant, users, conversions | The same, from aggregated counts. |
| **AI evaluation log** | model, score (optional: hallucination flag, latency, cost, category) | Mean score with t-CI, Wilson CI on hallucination, Kruskal-Wallis, Welch on the top two, χ² on safety, a category leaderboard, a cost trade-off and a guardrail verdict. |

Five sample datasets ship with the app: a shipping portal, an **e-commerce checkout**, an A/B test per user, an A/B summary and an AI evaluation log. Anyone can try it in one click.

---

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Connect your data sources (self-hosted, free)
chunks.text:
## Connect your data sources (self-hosted, free)

In the self-hosted version, the **Your Data → Database / GA4** tab connects directly to:

| Source | How it connects | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PostgreSQL** | asyncpg | Any SELECT / WITH query. Templates for event logs, A/B tests and AI logs. |
| **MySQL / MariaDB** | aiomysql | Same. |
| **SQLite** | aiosqlite, opened read-only | Put files in `connectors/data/`. |
| **Google Analytics 4** | Official Data API (free quota) | Users per event × country / device / channel, analysed as an aggregated funnel. |
| **CSV URL** | Fetched by the server | Works when the browser would be blocked by CORS. |

**Safety model**
- **Two layers of read-only protection.** First, a static check accepts only a single SELECT / WITH statement. Second, **every query runs inside a `READ ONLY` transaction with a timeout**, so the database itself refuses writes. CI proves the second layer separately on real PostgreSQL and MySQL, with the first layer disabled.
- **Row cap.** Results are limited to `PULSEPORT_CONNECTOR_MAX_ROWS` (default 500k).
- **Passwords.** They are sent only to your own server and never stored. To keep credentials off the browser entirely, use **saved connections**:
  ```bash
  PULSEPORT_CONNECTIONS='{"warehouse":{"type":"postgres","host":"host.docker.internal","database":"analytics","user":"readonly","password":"…"}}'
  PULSEPORT_ALLOW_ADHOC_CONNECTIONS=false   # only saved connections can be used
  ```
- **Path restriction.** SQLite files are opened only from `connectors/data/`, and paths are traversal-checked.
- **Reaching your own machine.** A database running on your own computer is reachable from Docker as `host.docker.internal`.

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Connect your data sources (self-hosted, free)
chunks.text:
**Try it instantly:** click **Use bundled demo database**. That queries the PostgreSQL that ships with the stack.
Connect Google Analytics 4 (one-time, ~5 minutes, free) 1. In [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), create a project and enable the **Google Analytics Data API**. 2. Create a **service account** → *Keys* → *Add key* → JSON. Save it as `connectors/secrets/ga4-service-account.json` (it's git-ignored). 3. In GA4, go to *Admin → Property access management*. Add the service account's e-mail as **Viewer**. 4. Copy the numeric **Property ID** from *Admin → Property details*. Then run `docker compose up` and pick **Google Analytics 4** in the Data Studio. GA4 returns *users per event* (aggregated). For exact per-user journeys, enable the free **GA4 → BigQuery export** and query the event table with SQL.

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Design decisions
chunks.text:
## Design decisions

| Decision | Why | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Analyse user data in the browser** | Privacy by construction: data never leaves the device. Hosting costs nothing, and analysis is instant. | Practical up to about 1–2M rows. Larger data should be aggregated in SQL first, via a connector. |
| **Port the stats engine to TypeScript and test it against SciPy** | One source of truth. The browser must give the *same* numbers as the Python engine, so 22 parity test groups compare against SciPy reference values (erfc to 1e-12, Bayesian P(B>A) to 1e-6). | Two implementations to maintain, so parity is enforced in CI. |
| **Frequentist *and* Bayesian, side by side** | p-values answer "is it real?". P(B>A) and expected loss answer "what's the risk if we ship?". Executives need both. | More numbers on screen, so the verdict summarises them. |
| **Power at a pre-registered MDE, not "observed power"** | Observed power is a restatement of the p-value and would make STOP unreachable. | You need to choose an MDE (default +5%). |
| **FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg) across segment × step tests** | Testing 6 countries × 2 devices × 4 steps × pairs means hundreds of comparisons. Without correction, false alarms are guaranteed. | Slightly less sensitive to tiny effects. |
| **Pairs reported only when they add information** | "Mobile in Norfolk" is not a finding if *all* mobile is equally weak. A pair is reported only when it is worse than both of its parts. | Some real interactions with small effects stay in the table rather than the headline. |
| **SRM check before any A/B verdict** | A broken 50/50 split invalidates the whole test. It's the most common real-world A/B bug. | None. |
| **Rule-based management brief, not an LLM** | Every sentence traces back to a computed number, so the brief can't hallucinate. | Less flowing prose. |
| **Two independent read-only layers for SQL** | Static checks can be bypassed; a `READ ONLY` transaction can't. CI tests the second layer with the first disabled. | A column literally named `lock`, `set` or `call` must be quoted or aliased. |
| **Synthetic demo with known ground truth** | The planted signals (a regional bottleneck, a 14% lift, an underpowered test) let tests verify that the analytics *find what was planted*. | The demo isn't real company data. The Data Studio is for that. |

---

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Statistical methods
chunks.text:
## Statistical methods
Frequentist (stats_engine/frequentist.py, lib/stats.ts) **Two-proportion z-test (pooled):** $$ z = \frac{\hat p_B - \hat p_A}{\sqrt{\bar p(1-\bar p)\left(\frac{1}{n_A}+\frac{1}{n_B}\right)}}, \qquad \bar p = \frac{x_A + x_B}{n_A + n_B} $$ **Pearson χ²** on the 2×2 table, without Yates correction, so χ² = z² exactly. A unit test asserts this. When an expected cell count is below 5, **Fisher's exact test** is used instead. **Relative-uplift CI (Katz log risk-ratio):** asymmetric and always > −100%: $$ \ln\!\frac{\hat p_B}{\hat p_A} \;\pm\; z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{1-\hat p_A}{n_A\hat p_A} + \frac{1-\hat p_B}{n_B\hat p_B}} $$ **Effect sizes:** Cohen's $h = 2\arcsin\sqrt{p_B} - 2\arcsin\sqrt{p_A}$; Cohen's $d$ with pooled SD; rank-biserial $r = 2U_A/(n_An_B) - 1$. **Mann-Whitney U** (two-sided, with tie and continuity correction) and **Welch's t** handle skewed continuous metrics. **Sample size (Fleiss):** $$ n = \frac{\left[z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar p\bar q} + z_{1-\beta}\sqrt{p_1q_1 + p_2q_2}\right]^2}{(p_2-p_1)^2} $$ This is verified against the textbook value (10% → 12%, α = 0.05, power 0.8 ⇒ **3,841 per arm**) and cross-checked against `statsmodels`. **Multiple comparisons:** Benjamini–Hochberg q-values for segment diagnostics; Holm step-down for multi-arm tests and latency checks. **SRM:** χ² goodness-of-fit against the planned split.
Bayesian (stats_engine/bayesian.py)

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Statistical methods
chunks.text:
Conjugate model: prior $\text{Beta}(1,1)$, posterior $\text{Beta}(1 + x,\; 1 + n - x)$. $$ P(p_B > p_A) = \int_0^1 f_B(x)\,F_A(x)\,dx $$ The integral is computed by adaptive quadrature (Simpson's rule in the browser). It is validated against Evan Miller's closed form to 1e-7, with a Monte-Carlo estimate reported alongside. **Expected loss** of shipping B: $\mathbb{E}[\max(p_A - p_B, 0)]$. A test checks the identity $\mathbb{E}[\text{loss}_B] - \mathbb{E}[\text{loss}_A] = \mathbb{E}[p_A] - \mathbb{E}[p_B]$.
Decision rule | Verdict | Condition | |---|---| | **GO** | p < α, uplift > 0, P(B>A) ≥ 95%, expected loss < 0.1 pp | | **NO-GO** | p < α and uplift < 0, or a sample-ratio mismatch | | **KEEP RUNNING** | not significant **and** power to detect the pre-registered MDE < 80% | | **STOP** | not significant although the test *could* detect the MDE, so there's no worthwhile effect |
Sample analytical SQL (analytics/sql_queries.py) ```sql -- Funnel with step conversion via LAG() WITH session_flags AS ( -- one row per session (conditional aggregation) SELECT s.session_id, BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'ROUTE_SEARCH') AS did_search, BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'RATE_QUOTE') AS did_quote, BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'BOOKING_CONFIRMED') AS did_book FROM scoped_sessions s JOIN session_events e USING (session_id) GROUP BY s.session_id ), funnel AS ( -- unpivot with LATERAL VALUES SELECT v.* FROM stage_totals t CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (1,'PORTAL_VISIT',t.portal_visit), ...) v(step_order, stage, sessions) ) SELECT stage, sessions, ROUND(100.0 * sessions / NULLIF(LAG(sessions) OVER w, 0), 2) AS step_conversion_pct, ROUND(100.0 * sessions / NULLIF(FIRST_VALUE(sessions) OVER w, 0), 2) AS cumulative_conversion_pct FROM funnel WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY step_order);

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Statistical methods
chunks.text:
-- Bottleneck detector: P95 vs SLA and latency ↔ conversion correlation
SELECT region,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY quote_latency_ms)                                     AS p95_latency_ms,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY quote_latency_ms) FILTER (WHERE device_type='Mobile') AS p95_mobile_ms,
       CORR(quote_latency_ms, reached_quote)                                                              AS latency_conv_corr
FROM searched
GROUP BY region;
```

Optional filters use `CAST(:param AS TYPE) IS NULL OR col = CAST(:param AS TYPE)`. One prepared statement covers every filter combination.
</details>

---

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Quick start
chunks.text:
## Quick start **Use it now:** open the [live app](https://yakov-ashgar27.github.io/PulsePort-Analytics/), go to *Your Data*, and upload a CSV or try a sample. **Run the full platform** (Docker, free): ```bash git clone https://github.com/yakov-ashgar27/PulsePort-Analytics.git cd PulsePort-Analytics docker compose up --build ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | App | http://localhost:3000 | | API docs (OpenAPI / Swagger) | http://localhost:8000/docs | | PostgreSQL | `localhost:5432` (pulseport / pulseport) | On first start the API seeds **50,000 portal sessions (~110k events), 40,000 experiment assignments and 900 graded AI answers** with PostgreSQL `COPY`, which takes a few seconds. The backend image **runs the statistical test suite during `docker build`**, so a mathematically broken engine never ships.
Local development without Docker ```bash cd backend && python3.13 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt && python -m pytest export PULSEPORT_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://pulseport:pulseport@localhost:5432/pulseport uvicorn app.main:app --reload cd frontend && npm install && npm test && npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api → :8000) ```

chunks.title: ⚓ PulsePort Analytics › Testing
chunks.text:
## Testing

Each layer is tested against **first principles or an independent reference**, never against itself. All of it runs in CI on every push.

| Suite | What it proves |
|---|---|
| **Python engine**: 60 tests (`backend/tests`) | Hand-computed z, χ² = z², the textbook sample size, Evan Miller's closed form for P(B>A), Wilson reference values, a power round-trip, the expected-loss identity, PDF normalisation, the GO/NO-GO/KEEP RUNNING/STOP rules, SQL safety rules, and the GA4 & SQLite connectors. |
| **Browser engine**: 22 test groups (`frontend/src/lib/**/*.test.ts`) | Parity with SciPy for every function, plus end-to-end Data Studio runs on every sample, including that the planted bottlenecks and verdicts are *found*. |
| **API smoke test** against a real PostgreSQL | Seeds the database, calls every endpoint, and asserts that the designed signals surface through SQL → stats → API. |
| **Connector test** against real PostgreSQL + MySQL | Round-trips data, checks the row cap and the API guard, and proves that **the database itself blocks writes** with the static check disabled. |
| **Frontend** | Strict TypeScript typecheck and production build. |

```bash
cd backend && python -m pytest -v
cd frontend && npm test
```

chunks.text:
## Limitations & roadmap - **Demo data is synthetic.** The planted signals make the analytics verifiable. The AI benchmark profiles are simulated and don't measure real vendors; they live in `MODEL_PROFILES`. Use the Data Studio for real data. - **GA4 returns aggregated counts**, so funnels from it are "users per event", not strictly ordered journeys. For exact journeys, query the GA4 BigQuery export. - **The browser handles up to about 1–2M rows.** Aggregate larger data in SQL first. - **Roadmap:** BigQuery and Snowflake connectors, CUPED variance reduction, sequential testing (always-valid p-values), and scheduled reports. ---

"""
AI assistant benchmarking & governance.

Aggregates are computed in PostgreSQL (AVG, STDDEV_SAMP, PERCENTILE_CONT);
inferential statistics (t-intervals, Wilson intervals, Kruskal-Wallis,
Welch t, χ²) are computed in Python from those aggregates / raw scores.

NOTE: evaluation runs are *simulated* (see seed/generators.py). In a real
deployment ``run_batch`` would call each provider's API and grade the answer
against a ground-truth rubric; the storage and statistics layers are
unchanged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..analytics import sql_queries as Q
from ..models import AiEvalRun
from ..seed.generators import AI_CATEGORIES, MODEL_PROFILES, generate_ai_eval_runs
from ..seed.maritime_seeder import AI_COLS, ai_records, copy_rows
from .metrics import compare_models, mean_ci_from_moments, wilson_ci

HALLUCINATION_GUARDRAIL = 0.05  # max acceptable hallucination rate for production


async def get_benchmark(session: AsyncSession, category: str | None = None) -> dict:
    params = {"category": category}
    agg = (await session.execute(Q.AI_MODEL_AGGREGATES, params)).mappings().all()
    raw = (await session.execute(Q.AI_RAW_SCORES, params)).mappings().all()
    matrix = (await session.execute(Q.AI_CATEGORY_MATRIX)).mappings().all()
    totals = (await session.execute(Q.AI_RUN_TOTALS)).mappings().one()

    vendors = {m.name: m.vendor for m in MODEL_PROFILES}
    models = []
    for r in agg:
        n, k = int(r["n"]), int(r["hallucinations"])
        mean, sd = float(r["mean_accuracy"]), float(r["sd_accuracy"] or 0.0)
        lo, hi = mean_ci_from_moments(mean, sd, n)
        h_lo, h_hi = wilson_ci(k, n)
        cost = float(r["cost_per_1k_usd"])
        models.append(
            {
                "model": r["model"],
                "vendor": vendors.get(r["model"], "—"),
                "n": n,
                "mean_accuracy": mean,
                "accuracy_ci_low": lo,
                "accuracy_ci_high": hi,
                "hallucination_rate": k / n,
                "hallucination_ci_low": h_lo,
                "hallucination_ci_high": h_hi,
                "p50_latency_ms": float(r["p50_latency_ms"]),
                "p95_latency_ms": float(r["p95_latency_ms"]),
                "cost_per_1k_usd": cost,

                "p50_latency_ms": float(r["p50_latency_ms"]),
                "p95_latency_ms": float(r["p95_latency_ms"]),

                "accuracy_per_dollar": mean / cost if cost else 0.0,

    )

    return {
        "category": category,
        "categories": list(AI_CATEGORIES),
        "guardrail_hallucination_rate": HALLUCINATION_GUARDRAIL,
        "models": models,
        "tests": tests,
        "category_matrix": [dict(r) for r in matrix],
        "totals": dict(totals),
        "simulated": True,
    }


async def run_batch(session: AsyncSession, n_prompts: int) -> dict:
    """Simulate a new evaluation batch, persist it with COPY, return fresh metrics."""
    existing = (await session.execute(select(func.count(func.distinct(AiEvalRun.prompt_id))))).scalar_one()
    batch_id = f"batch-{datetime.now(UTC):%Y%m%d%H%M%S}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    rows = generate_ai_eval_runs(
        n_prompts=n_prompts,
        seed=uuid.uuid4().int % (2**32),
        batch_id=batch_id,
        prompt_offset=int(existing),
    )
    conn = await session.connection()
    await copy_rows(conn, "ai_eval_runs", AI_COLS, ai_records(rows))
    await session.commit()
    result = await get_benchmark(session)
    result["last_batch"] = {"batch_id": batch_id, "prompts": n_prompts, "runs": len(rows)}
    return result

def model_summary(
    accuracy: Sequence[float],
    hallucination: Sequence[bool],
    latency_ms: Sequence[float],
    cost_usd: Sequence[float],
) -> dict:
    acc = np.asarray(accuracy, dtype=float)
    hal = np.asarray(hallucination, dtype=bool)
    lat = np.asarray(latency_ms, dtype=float)
    cost = np.asarray(cost_usd, dtype=float)
    mean, lo, hi = mean_ci_t(acc)
    k = int(hal.sum())
    h_lo, h_hi = wilson_ci(k, hal.size)
    cost_1k = float(cost.mean() * 1000) if cost.size else math.nan
    return {
        "n": int(acc.size),
        "mean_accuracy": mean,
        "accuracy_ci_low": lo,
        "accuracy_ci_high": hi,
        "hallucination_rate": k / hal.size if hal.size else math.nan,
        "hallucination_ci_low": h_lo,
        "hallucination_ci_high": h_hi,
        "p50_latency_ms": float(np.percentile(lat, 50)) if lat.size else math.nan,
        "p95_latency_ms": float(np.percentile(lat, 95)) if lat.size else math.nan,
        "cost_per_1k_usd": cost_1k,
        "accuracy_per_dollar": mean / cost_1k if cost_1k else math.nan,
    }


def compare_models(accuracy_by_model: dict[str, Sequence[float]],
                   halluc_by_model: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]) -> dict:
    """
    Omnibus + pairwise tests:

    * Kruskal-Wallis H across all models' accuracy distributions
    * Welch t-test between the top-2 models by mean accuracy
    * χ² test of independence on hallucination counts (model × flag)
    """
    names = [m for m, v in accuracy_by_model.items() if len(v) >= 2]
    out: dict = {"kruskal_h": None, "kruskal_p": None, "top_two": None,
                 "welch_t": None, "welch_p": None, "halluc_chi2": None, "halluc_p": None}
    if len(names) >= 2:
        h, p = stats.kruskal(*[accuracy_by_model[m] for m in names])
        out["kruskal_h"], out["kruskal_p"] = float(h), float(p)
        ranked = sorted(names, key=lambda m: float(np.mean(accuracy_by_model[m])), reverse=True)
        a, b = ranked[0], ranked[1]

    if table.shape[0] >= 2 and (table.sum(axis=0) > 0).all():
        chi2, p, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(table)

chunks.title: sql_queries.py
chunks.text:
"""
Analytical SQL layer (PostgreSQL 16).

All queries are raw, parameterised SQL executed through ``sqlalchemy.text``.
Optional filters use the ``CAST(:param AS type) IS NULL OR ...`` idiom so a
single prepared statement serves every filter combination, and every bind is
explicitly typed so asyncpg can prepare the statement without guessing.

Conventions
-----------
* A session "belongs" to the date range in which its PORTAL_VISIT happened,
  so later funnel events are never cut off by the window boundary.
* Percentages are returned as 0–100 numerics rounded to 2 dp.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import text

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Shared CTE: sessions in scope after filters (one row per session)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
_SCOPED_SESSIONS = """
scoped_sessions AS (
    SELECT session_id, region, device_type, event_ts AS started_at
    FROM session_events
    WHERE stage = 'PORTAL_VISIT'
      AND (CAST(:region      AS TEXT)        IS NULL OR region      = CAST(:region AS TEXT))
      AND (CAST(:device_type AS TEXT)        IS NULL OR device_type = CAST(:device_type AS TEXT))
      AND (CAST(:date_from   AS TIMESTAMPTZ) IS NULL OR event_ts   >= CAST(:date_from AS TIMESTAMPTZ))
      AND (CAST(:date_to     AS TIMESTAMPTZ) IS NULL OR event_ts   <  CAST(:date_to   AS TIMESTAMPTZ))
),
-- Pivot each session's events into one row of stage flags (conditional aggregation)
session_flags AS (
    SELECT
        s.session_id,
        s.region,
        s.device_type,
        s.started_at,
        BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'ROUTE_SEARCH')       AS did_search,
        BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'RATE_QUOTE')         AS did_quote,
        BOOL_OR(e.stage = 'BOOKING_CONFIRMED')  AS did_book,
        MAX(e.quote_latency_ms)                 AS quote_latency_ms
    FROM scoped_sessions s
    JOIN session_events e USING (session_id)
    GROUP BY s.session_id, s.region, s.device_type, s.started_at
)
"""

# 2. Multi-stage funnel with LAG() step-to-step conversion

FUNNEL = text(

WITH {_SCOPED_SESSIONS},
stage_totals AS (
    -- Conditional aggregation: one pass, four counters
    SELECT
        COUNT(*)                          AS portal_visit,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE did_search) AS route_search,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE did_quote)  AS rate_quote,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE did_book)   AS booking_confirmed
    FROM session_flags
),
funnel AS (
    -- Unpivot to one row per stage so window functions can walk the funnel
    SELECT v.step_order, v.stage, v.sessions
    FROM stage_totals t
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES
        (1, 'PORTAL_VISIT',      t.portal_visit),
        (2, 'ROUTE_SEARCH',      t.route_search),
        (3, 'RATE_QUOTE',        t.rate_quote),
        (4, 'BOOKING_CONFIRMED', t.booking_confirmed)
    ) AS v(step_order, stage, sessions)
)
SELECT

    stage,
    sessions,

    ROUND(100.0 - 100.0 * sessions / NULLIF(LAG(sessions) OVER w, 0), 2)

"""
Defence-in-depth for user-supplied SQL.

The *real* guarantee is that every query runs inside a READ ONLY transaction
with a statement timeout (see sql.py). This module adds a cheap static check so
obviously unsafe input is rejected with a clear message before any connection
is opened.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date, datetime, time
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

_LINE_COMMENT = re.compile(r"--[^\n]*")
_BLOCK_COMMENT = re.compile(r"/\*.*?\*/", re.S)
_STRING = re.compile(r"'(?:[^']|'')*'")
_FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\b(insert|update|delete|merge|drop|alter|create|truncate|grant|revoke|copy|call|exec|execute|"
    r"vacuum|analyze|attach|detach|pragma|load_file|outfile|dumpfile|lock|unlock|set|begin|commit|rollback)\b",
    re.I,
)


class UnsafeQuery(ValueError):
    pass


def check_read_only_sql(sql: str) -> str:
    """Return the normalised statement, or raise UnsafeQuery."""
    if not sql or not sql.strip():
        raise UnsafeQuery("Query is empty.")
    stripped = _BLOCK_COMMENT.sub(" ", _LINE_COMMENT.sub(" ", sql)).strip()
    stripped = stripped.rstrip(";").strip()
    without_strings = _STRING.sub("''", stripped)
    if ";" in without_strings:
        raise UnsafeQuery("Only a single statement is allowed.")
    first = re.match(r"^\(*\s*(\w+)", without_strings)
    if not first or first.group(1).lower() not in {"select", "with", "values", "table"}:
        raise UnsafeQuery("Only read-only queries are allowed (SELECT / WITH).")
    m = _FORBIDDEN.search(without_strings)
    if m:
        raise UnsafeQuery(f"Keyword '{m.group(1).upper()}' is not allowed in a read-only query.")
    return stripped

def run_ga4(src: Ga4Source, max_rows: int, client=None) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]], bool]:
    """Page through runReport (100k rows / page) and flatten to a table."""
    if client is None and not ga4_configured():
        raise HTTPException(
            400,
            "GA4 is not configured: mount a service-account JSON and set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS "
            "(see README → Connect Google Analytics 4).",
        )
    client = client or _ga4_client()
    headers = [*src.dimensions, *src.metrics]
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    offset = 0
    page = min(100_000, max_rows + 1)
    while True:
        resp = client.run_report(_ga4_request(src, page, offset))
        for r in resp.rows:
            rows.append([v.value for v in r.dimension_values] + [v.value for v in r.metric_values])
        offset += len(resp.rows)
        if len(rows) > max_rows:
            return headers, rows[:max_rows], True
        if not resp.rows or offset >= resp.row_count:
            return headers, rows, False


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- CSV
async def _fetch_csv(src: CsvUrlSource, max_rows: int) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]], bool]:
    import csv
    import io

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=get_settings().connector_timeout_s, follow_redirects=True) as c:
        r = await c.get(src.url, headers={"Accept": "text/csv,text/plain,*/*"})
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise HTTPException(502, f"Source returned HTTP {r.status_code}")
    text_body = r.text.lstrip("")
    if text_body.lstrip().lower().startswith(("<!doctype", "<html")):
        raise HTTPException(422, "The URL returned a web page, not CSV")
    try:
        dialect = csv.Sniffer().sniff(text_body[:20_000], delimiters=",;\t|")
    except csv.Error:
        dialect = csv.excel
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text_body), dialect)
    headers = next(reader, [])
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    for row in reader:
        if len(rows) >= max_rows:
            return headers, rows, True
        rows.append(row)
    return headers, rows, False

"""
Pure, deterministic synthetic-data generators (no database dependency).

The generated data is *synthetic* and designed to contain specific,
known statistical signals so that the analytics layer can be verified:

1. A regional bottleneck: BR-Santos and CN-Shanghai **mobile** users get a
   slow rate-quote API (log-normal latency, median ≈ 3.2 s) which causes a
   significant drop-off between ROUTE_SEARCH and RATE_QUOTE.
2. EXP-01: +14 % relative lift in booking conversion, p < 0.01.
3. EXP-02: +2.9 % relative lift, p ≈ 0.18 (underpowered, not significant).
4. AI evaluation runs for three assistant models across four maritime
   support categories with different accuracy / cost / latency profiles.

Experiment outcomes are generated with *exact* conversion counts (then
shuffled) so the headline p-values are reproducible regardless of RNG state.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import numpy as np

def _uuid(rng: np.random.Generator) -> str:
    return str(uuid.UUID(bytes=rng.bytes(16), version=4))


def _quote_success_prob(latency_ms: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Users abandon slow quotes: logistic decay centred at 3.5 s."""
    return 0.70 / (1.0 + np.exp((latency_ms - 3500.0) / 900.0))


def generate_session_events(
    n_sessions: int = 50_000,
    days: int = 90,
    seed: int = 7,
    end: datetime | None = None,
) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """
    Yield one dict per funnel event. Every session has a PORTAL_VISIT; later
    stages are reached with region/device-dependent probabilities. The
    rate-quote API latency is recorded on the ROUTE_SEARCH event, i.e. the
    latency the user experienced while waiting for the quote.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    end = end or datetime.now(UTC).replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    start = end - timedelta(days=days)

    shares = np.array([r.traffic_share for r in REGIONS])
    region_idx = rng.choice(len(REGIONS), size=n_sessions, p=shares / shares.sum())
    is_mobile = rng.random(n_sessions) < MOBILE_SHARE

    # Timestamps: uniform over the window, with ~25 % less traffic at weekends
    offsets = rng.uniform(0, days * 86_400, size=n_sessions * 2)
    ts = np.array([start + timedelta(seconds=float(s)) for s in offsets])
    weekday_ok = np.array([t.weekday() < 5 or rng.random() < 0.75 for t in ts])
    ts = ts[weekday_ok][:n_sessions]
    if ts.size < n_sessions:  # extremely unlikely; top up
        ts = np.concatenate([ts, ts[: n_sessions - ts.size]])

    lat_median = np.where(
        is_mobile,
        [REGIONS[i].mobile_latency_median_ms for i in region_idx],
        [REGIONS[i].desktop_latency_median_ms for i in region_idx],
    )
    latency = rng.lognormal(np.log(lat_median), 0.45).round().astype(int)

    p_search = np.where(is_mobile, 0.62, 0.71)
    p_quote = _quote_success_prob(latency)
    p_book = np.where(is_mobile, 0.24, 0.31)

def generate_ai_eval_runs(
    n_prompts: int = 300,
    seed: int = 23,
    batch_id: str = "seed",
    created_at: datetime | None = None,
    prompt_offset: int = 0,
) -> list[dict]:
    """
    ``n_prompts`` support prompts (balanced across categories), each answered
    by every model ⇒ ``n_prompts × len(MODEL_PROFILES)`` rows. A shared
    per-prompt difficulty term induces realistic within-prompt correlation.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    created_at = created_at or datetime.now(UTC)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for p in range(n_prompts):
        category = AI_CATEGORIES[p % len(AI_CATEGORIES)]
        acc_shift, hall_mult = CATEGORY_DIFFICULTY[category]
        prompt_difficulty = rng.normal(0, 4.0)
        in_tokens = int(rng.integers(500, 1600))
        for m in MODEL_PROFILES:
            acc = rng.normal(m.mean_accuracy + acc_shift + prompt_difficulty, m.accuracy_sd)
            halluc = rng.random() < min(0.95, m.hallucination_rate * hall_mult)
            if halluc:
                acc -= rng.uniform(25, 45)  # hallucinated answers score poorly
            out_tokens = int(rng.integers(150, 600))
            cost = in_tokens / 1e6 * m.usd_per_m_input + out_tokens / 1e6 * m.usd_per_m_output
            rows.append(
                {
                    "batch_id": batch_id,
                    "prompt_id": f"MP-{prompt_offset + p + 1:05d}",
                    "category": category,
                    "model": m.name,
                    "accuracy_score": float(np.clip(acc, 0, 100).round(1)),
                    "hallucination": bool(halluc),
                    "latency_ms": int(rng.lognormal(np.log(m.latency_median_ms), m.latency_sigma)),

"""
Idempotent database seeder.

Uses PostgreSQL ``COPY`` through asyncpg's ``copy_records_to_table`` (≈10×
faster than batched INSERTs for ~170k rows) and a transaction-scoped
advisory lock so that several API replicas starting together seed only once.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from decimal import Decimal

from sqlalchemy import func, select, text
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine

from ..config import get_settings
from ..models import SessionEvent
from .generators import (
    generate_ai_eval_runs,
    generate_experiment_assignments,
    generate_session_events,
)

log = logging.getLogger("pulseport.seed")

_SEED_LOCK_KEY = 0x50554C5345  # "PULSE"

EVENT_COLS = ("session_id", "event_ts", "stage", "region", "device_type", "quote_latency_ms")
ASSIGN_COLS = ("experiment_id", "session_id", "variant", "assigned_at", "converted", "time_to_quote_s")
AI_COLS = (
    "batch_id", "prompt_id", "category", "model", "accuracy_score", "hallucination",
    "latency_ms", "input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cost_usd", "created_at",
)


def ai_records(rows: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    return [
        tuple(Decimal(str(r[c])) if c == "cost_usd" else r[c] for c in AI_COLS) for r in rows
    ]


async def copy_rows(conn, table: str, columns: tuple[str, ...], records: list[tuple]) -> None:
    """Bulk-load via the asyncpg driver connection underneath SQLAlchemy."""
    raw = await conn.get_raw_connection()
    await raw.driver_connection.copy_records_to_table(table, records=records, columns=columns)


async def seed_if_empty(engine: AsyncEngine) -> bool:
    settings = get_settings()
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.execute(text("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(:k)"), {"k": _SEED_LOCK_KEY})
        existing = (await conn.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(SessionEvent))).scalar_one()
        if existing:
            log.info("Database already seeded (%s events) — skipping", existing)
            return False

async def bottlenecks(session: AsyncSession, params: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Enrich each region from the SQL detector with a two-proportion test of
    its search→quote rate against *all other regions combined*.
    """
    rows = _rows(await session.execute(Q.BOTTLENECK_DETECTOR, params))
    tot_s = sum(r["searches"] for r in rows)
    tot_q = sum(r["quotes"] for r in rows)
    for r in rows:
        rest_s, rest_q = tot_s - r["searches"], tot_q - r["quotes"]
        if r["searches"] and rest_s:
            t = two_proportion_test(rest_q, rest_s, r["quotes"], r["searches"])
            r["p_value_vs_rest"] = t.p_value_z
            r["rate_diff_vs_rest_pp"] = t.absolute_diff * 100
            r["significant"] = t.significant
        else:
            r["p_value_vs_rest"], r["rate_diff_vs_rest_pp"], r["significant"] = None, None, False
    return rows

"""
Deterministic executive-brief generator.

Translates statistical outputs into a management memo with a clear
Go / No-Go per decision. It is rule-based on purpose: every sentence is
traceable to a computed number, so the brief cannot hallucinate.
"""

def _pct(x: float, digits: int = 1) -> str:
    return f"{x * 100:.{digits}f}%"


def _prob(p: float) -> str:
    """Avoid displaying 100.0% / 0.0% for probabilities that are merely extreme."""
    if p > 0.999:
        return "> 99.9%"
    if p < 0.001:
        return "< 0.1%"
    return f"{p:.1%}"


def _rel(v: str) -> str:
    """Prefix "=" unless the value already carries a relation ("> 99.9%", "< 0.001 pp")."""
    return v if v[:1] in "<>" else f"= {v}"


def _loss(x: float) -> str:
    pp = x * 100
    return "< 0.001 pp" if pp < 0.001 else f"{pp:.3f} pp"

def _to_markdown(brief: dict) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# {brief['title']}",
        f"_Generated {brief['generated_at']} · α = {brief['alpha']} · target power = {brief['power']:.0%}_",
        "",
        "## Executive Summary",
        *[f"- **{s['title']}** → **{s['verdict']}**" for s in brief["sections"]],
        "",
    ]
    for s in brief["sections"]:
        lines += [
            f"## {s['title']}  ·  {s['verdict']}",
            f"**Hypothesis.** {s['hypothesis']}",
            "",
            "**Statistical evidence.**",
            *[f"- {e}" for e in s["evidence"]],
            "",
            f"**Risk assessment.** {s['risk']}",
            "",
            f"**Recommendation.** {s['recommendation']}",
            "",
        ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


async def build_brief(session: AsyncSession) -> dict:
    s = get_settings()
    exps = [await analyze_experiment(session, e.experiment_id) for e in EXPERIMENTS]
    bench = await get_benchmark(session)
    bn = await analytics.bottlenecks(session, analytics.filter_params(None, None, None, None))
    brief = {
        "title": "PulsePort Analytics — Management Brief",
        "generated_at": datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC"),
        "alpha": s.alpha,
        "power": s.target_power,
        "sections": [*map(_experiment_section, exps), _ai_section(bench), _ops_section(bn)],
    }
    brief["markdown"] = _to_markdown(brief)
    return brief

"""Experiment analysis: frequentist + Bayesian + power, and a decision rule."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
from fastapi import HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..analytics import sql_queries as Q
from ..config import get_settings
from ..seed.generators import EXPERIMENTS, EXPERIMENTS_BY_ID
from ..stats_engine.bayesian import bayesian_ab_test
from ..stats_engine.frequentist import (
    achieved_power,
    mann_whitney_test,
    required_sample_size,
    two_proportion_test,
)


def decide(
    freq: dict, bayes: dict, days_remaining: float | None, power_at_mde: float | None = None
) -> dict:
    """
    Decision rule combining both paradigms (all thresholds from settings):

    GO            p < α, uplift > 0, P(B>A) ≥ 95 %, expected loss < threshold
    NO-GO         p < α and uplift < 0  (variant is significantly worse)
    KEEP RUNNING  not significant and power to detect the pre-registered MDE
                  is below target (underpowered)
    STOP          not significant although the test could reliably detect the
                  MDE ⇒ any real effect is smaller than worth shipping
    """
    s = get_settings()
    sig, uplift = freq["significant"], freq["relative_uplift"]
    p_beat, loss = bayes["prob_b_beats_a"], bayes["expected_loss_b"]

    if sig and uplift > 0 and p_beat >= 0.95 and loss < s.expected_loss_threshold:
        return {
            "verdict": "GO",
            "headline": "Roll out Variant B",
            "rationale": (
                f"Statistically significant lift (p = {freq['p_value_z']:.2g} < α = {s.alpha}), "
                f"{'>99.9%' if p_beat > 0.999 else f'{p_beat:.1%}'} probability that B beats A "
                f"and negligible expected loss ({'<0.001' if loss * 100 < 0.001 else f'{loss * 100:.3f}'} pp)."
            ),
        }
    if sig and uplift < 0:
        return {
            "verdict": "NO-GO",
            "headline": "Do not ship — variant is significantly worse",
            "rationale": f"B underperforms A (p = {freq['p_value_z']:.2g}).",
        }
    if power_at_mde is None:
        power_at_mde = freq["achieved_power"]
    if power_at_mde < s.target_power:
        eta = f" ≈ {days_remaining:.0f} more days at current traffic" if days_remaining else ""
        return {

            f"none (p = {freq['p_value_z']:.2f}); keep control and reallocate traffic."
        ),
    }


async def analyze_experiment(session: AsyncSession, experiment_id: str) -> dict:
    spec = EXPERIMENTS_BY_ID.get(experiment_id)
    if spec is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, f"Unknown experiment {experiment_id}")
    s = get_settings()

    arms = {r["variant"]: r for r in
            (await session.execute(Q.EXPERIMENT_ARM_COUNTS, {"experiment_id": experiment_id})).mappings()}
    if set(arms) != {"A", "B"}:
        raise HTTPException(409, f"Experiment {experiment_id} has no data for both arms")
    a, b = arms["A"], arms["B"]

    freq = two_proportion_test(a["conversions"], a["n"], b["conversions"], b["n"], s.alpha).to_dict()
    bayes = bayesian_ab_test(a["conversions"], a["n"], b["conversions"], b["n"]).to_dict()

    ttq = (await session.execute(Q.EXPERIMENT_TIME_TO_QUOTE, {"experiment_id": experiment_id})).all()
    ttq_a = np.array([t for v, t in ttq if v == "A"])
    ttq_b = np.array([t for v, t in ttq if v == "B"])
    mw = mann_whitney_test(ttq_a, ttq_b, s.alpha).to_dict()

    first = min(a["first_assigned"], b["first_assigned"])
    last = max(a["last_assigned"], b["last_assigned"])
    days_running = max((last - first).total_seconds() / 86_400, 1.0)
    daily_traffic = (a["n"] + b["n"]) / days_running

    # How many users per arm would detect the *observed* effect at target power?
    days_remaining = None
    required_n = None
    if freq["rate_a"] != freq["rate_b"] and 0 < freq["rate_b"] < 1:
        required_n = required_sample_size(freq["rate_a"], freq["rate_b"], s.alpha, s.target_power)
        remaining = max(0, 2 * required_n - (a["n"] + b["n"]))
        days_remaining = math.ceil(remaining / daily_traffic) if remaining else 0

async def list_experiments(session: AsyncSession) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for spec in EXPERIMENTS:
        res = await analyze_experiment(session, spec.experiment_id)
        f = res["frequentist"]
        out.append({
            "experiment_id": spec.experiment_id,
            "name": spec.name,
            "primary_metric": spec.primary_metric,
            "relative_uplift": f["relative_uplift"],
            "p_value": f["p_value_z"],
            "prob_b_beats_a": res["bayesian"]["prob_b_beats_a"],
            "verdict": res["decision"]["verdict"],
        })
    return out
